sanskrit_text: प्रणम्य जगदुपत्तिस्थितिसंहारकारणम् । स्वर्गावर्गयोद्वारं त्रैलोक्यशरणं शिवम् ।।१।।
transliteration: Praṇamya jagadupattisthitisaṃhārakāraṇam | Svargāvargayodvāraṃ trailokyaśaraṇaṃ śivam ||1||
commentary: Salutations to lord Śiva, who is the root-cause of evolution, existence and dissolution of the universe, the gateway of heaven and emancipation and the ultimate saviour of the three worlds (heaven, earth and the one underneath). The commentator explains that Madhavakara invokes Lord Siva at the beginning of his work to remove obstacles and ensure welfare for readers. Svarga is heaven and Apavarga is liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

sanskrit_text: सोपद्रवारिष्टनिदानलिङ्गं समासतः सिद्धषजां नियोगात् । नानामुनीनां वचनैरिदानीं निबध्यते रोगविनिश्चयोऽयम् ॥२॥ अल्पमेधसामपि सुखं यथा स्यादातङ्कविज्ञानमनेन तस्मात् । नानातन्त्रविहीनानामपि च प्रवृत्तिरियं क्रियते निदाने ॥३॥
transliteration: Sopadravāriṣṭanidānaliṅgaṃ samāsataḥ siddhaṣajāṃ niyogāt | Nānāmunīnāṃ vacanairidānīṃ nibadhyate rogaviniścayoyam ||2|| Alpamedhasāmapi sukhaṃ yathā syādātaṅkavijñānamanena tasmāt | Nānātantravihīnānāmapi ca pravṛttiriyaṃ kriyate nidāne ||3||
commentary: On the instruction of noble physicians, the valuable statements of various sages of Ayurveda are precisely compiled here containing complications, prognosis (bad-prognosis), aetiology and symptomatology of the diseases. This work is useful for physicians who have no access to various treatises and also for those who have low mental abilities, helping them understand diseases easily. The commentary explains that upadrava (complication) is the complication of a disease which follows the main disease, and arista is the definite bad prognosis.

sanskrit_text: निदानं पूर्वरूपाणि रूपाण्युपशयस्तथा । संप्राप्तिरिति विज्ञानं रोगाणां पञ्चधा स्मृतम् ।।४।।
transliteration: Nidānaṃ pūrvarūpāṇi rūpāṇyupaśayastathā | Saṃprāptiriti vijñānaṃ rogāṇāṃ pañcadhā smṛtam ||4||
commentary: Nidāna (aetiology), Pūrvarūpa (premonitory symptoms/prodromata), Rūpa (signs and symptoms or symptomatology), Upaśaya (positive trial treatment) and Sampṛāpti (pathogenesis) are the five means of getting the knowledge of diseases. The commentator explains that these five factors are essential for diagnosis and treatment planning.

sanskrit_text: प्रायूं येन लक्ष्यते ।।५।। उत्पित्सुरामयो दोषविशेषेणानधिष्ठितः । लिङ्गमव्यक्तमल्पत्वाद् व्याधीनां तद्यथायथम् ।।६।।
transliteration: Prāyūṃ yena lakṣyate ||5|| Utpitsurāmayo doṣaviśeṣeṇānadhiṣṭhitaḥ | Liṅgamavyaktamalpatvād vyādhīnāṃ tadyathāyatham ||6||
commentary: Pūrvarūpa is of two types: Sāmānya (general) and Viśeṣa (particular). Sāmānya is the type of prodromata in which the signs and symptoms of future disease manifest when the Dosas vitiate the Dūsyas in the body. Viśiṣṭa or Viśeṣa prodromata indicates at the specific Dosa-involvement. The commentator explains that these symptoms are not completely manifested and are mild in nature.

sanskrit_text: तदेव व्यक्ततां यातं रूपमित्यभिधीयते । संस्थानं व्यञ्जनं लिङ्गं लक्षणं चिद्वहमाकृतिः ।।७।।
transliteration: Tadeva vyaktatāṃ yātaṃ rūpamityabhidhīyate | Saṃsthānaṃ vyañjanaṃ liṅgaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cidvahamākṛtiḥ ||7||
commentary: The same Pūrvarūpa, when manifested clearly, is named as Rūpa (symptomatology). Saṃsthana, vyañjana, liṅga, lakṣaṇa, cihna and ākṛti are the synonyms of Rūpa. The commentator explains that a group of symptoms indicates the existence of a disease, and individually these symptoms may be considered as diseases but when associated with others indicate a particular disease.

sanskrit_text: औषधमन्नं विहारो यो हेतुव्याधिविपरीतरः । करोति हि यथाकालं सौख्यं स उपशयः स्मृतः ॥८॥ सात्म्यमपि तमाहुर्ये विपरीतस्त्वनुपशयः ॥९॥
transliteration: Auṣadhamannaṃ vihāro yo hetuvyādhiviparītaraḥ | Karoti hi yathākālaṃ saukhyaṃ sa upaśayaḥ smṛtaḥ ||8|| Sātmyamapi tamāhurye viparītastvanupaśayaḥ ||9||
commentary: The medicine, food and behaviour which are selectively given as Hetuviparita (opposing to the aetiological factors), Vyadhiviparita (opposing to the disease) and Hetuvyadhiviparita (opposing both) and when they bring about normalcy, they are called Upasaya (positive trial). When the result is other way round, such trial is known as Anupasaya (negative trial). This is also known as Satmya (homologous) and Asatmya (non-homologous) respectively.

sanskrit_text: यथा दुष्टेन दोषेण दोषी दुष्यति स प्रभोः । यथाऽऽमयस्य संप्राप्तिर्ज्ञेया सा जातिरागतिः ॥१०॥
transliteration: Yathā duṣṭena doṣeṇa doṣī duṣyati sa prabhoḥ | Yathā''mayasya saṃprāptirjñeyā sā jātiragatiḥ ||10||
commentary: The process in which the vitiated dosas extend in the body and cause disease is called Samprapti (pathogenesis). Jati (genesis) and Agati (occurrence) are the synonyms of Samprapti. The benefit of the knowledge of Samprapti is that the management of the disease is planned accordingly. The commentator explains that Samprapti is the explanation of origination of a disease following the movement of vitiated dosas.

sanskrit_text: संख्याविकल्पप्राधान्यबलकालाविशेषतः । सा भिघते यथाऽत्रैव वक्ष्यतेऽष्टौ ज्वरा इति ॥११॥ दोषाणां समवेतानां विकल्पोऽशांशकल्पना । स्वतन्यपारतन्याभ्यां व्याथैः प्राधान्यमादिशेत् ॥१२॥ हेत्वादिकातन्यायिवैबलावलविशेषणम् । नक्तदिनतुंभुक्तांशैव्याधिकालो यथामलम् ॥१३॥
transliteration: Saṃkhyāvikalpaprādhānyabalakālāviśeṣataḥ | Sā bhighate yathātraiva vakṣyate'ṣṭau jvarā iti ||11|| Doṣāṇāṃ samavetānāṃ vikalpo'śāṃśakalpanā | Svatanyapāratanyābhyāṃ vyāthaiḥ prādhānyamādiśet ||12|| Hetvādikātanyāyivāibalāvalaviśeṣaṇam | Naktadinatuṃbhuktāṃśaivyādhikālo yathāmalam ||13||
commentary: Samprapti is classified as per Saankhya (enumeration), Vikalpa (variation as per dosa predominance), Pradhanya (to consider whether the disease is primary or secondary), Bala (strength of the disease) and Kāla (time of occurrence or aggravation). The commentator explains that the enumeration of fevers as eight types comes under Sankhya, and the prominence and less importance of Dosa involved comes under Vikalpa.

topic_heading: Cause of All Diseases - Vitiation of Dosas
sanskrit_text: सर्वेषामेव रोगाणां निदानं मलकुपिताः । कुपिताश्च यथामूतं विविधाहितसेवनात् ॥१४॥ निदानार्थकरो रोगो रोगस्याप्युपजायते ॥१५॥
transliteration: Sarveṣāmeva rogāṇāṃ nidānaṃ malakupitāḥ | Kupitāśca yathāmūtaṃ vividhāhitasevanāt ||14|| Nidānārthakaro rogo rogasyāpyupajāyate ||15||
commentary: The cause of all diseases is vitiation of impurities (Dosas). The reason for this vitiation is indulging in taking bad foods and things that harm the body. A disease can become a cause for another disease. The commentator explains that the reason for diseases is of two types: Sannikrsta (proximal) and Viprakrsta (distant). The distant reason is indulging in consumption of incompatible foods and the proximal reason is the Vata etc. Dosas.

topic_heading: Disease as a Cause for Another Disease
sanskrit_text: तद्यथा ज्वरसन्तापाद्रक्तपित्तमुदीयंते । रक्तपिताज्ज्वरस्ताभ्यां शोषश्चाप्युपजायते ॥१६॥ प्लीहाभिवृद्ध्या जठरं जठराच्छोष एव च । अशोंभ्यो जाठरं दुःखं गुल्मश्चाप्युपजायते ॥१७॥ प्रतिश्यायादथो कासः कासात् संजायते क्षयः । क्षयो रोगस्य हेतुत्वे शोषस्याप्युपजायते ॥१८॥
transliteration: Tadyathā jvarasantāpādraktapittamudīyante | Raktapittājjvarastābhyāṃ śoṣaścāpyupajāyate ||16|| Plīhābhivṛddhyā jaṭharaṃ jaṭharācchoṣa eva ca | Aśoṃbhyo jāṭharaṃ duḥkhaṃ gulmaścāpyupajāyate ||17|| Pratiśyāyādattho kāsaḥ kāsāt saṃjāyate kṣayaḥ | Kṣayo rogasya hetutve śoṣasyāpyupajāyate ||18||
commentary: A disease can become a cause for another disease. As in the case of Raktapitta which develops from the burning sensation caused by Jvara, Raktapitta can cause fever and these two give rise to Soṣa (emaciation). Plīhā vṛddhi (splenomegaly) leads to Jathara (abdominal disorder) which in turn causes Śotha (oedema). Arśa (piles) causes the painful Jathara and also Gulma. Day sleep etc. causes Pratiśyāya which leads to Kāsa. Kāsa precipitates Kṣaya which ultimately leads to Śoṣa.

sanskrit_text: दक्षापमानसंकृद्धरुद्रनिःश्वाससंभवः । ज्वरोऽष्टथा पृथगद्वन्द्वसंघातागन्तुजः स्मृतः ।।१।।
transliteration: Dakṣāpamānasaṃkṛddharudraniḥśvāsasaṃbhavaḥ | Jvaro'ṣṭathā pṛthagdvandvasaṃghātāgantujaḥ smṛtaḥ ||1||
commentary: Jvara (fever) was first originated from the exhalation of Rudra (lord Śiva) when he was outraged by the humiliation caused by Dakṣa. It is of eight types: three separately by the Tridoṣas, three due to combination of each two of them, one due to combination of all of them, and one due to unforeseen causes (3 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 8). The commentator explains that fever is important because it afflicts beings before any other disease, is the strongest, troubles body and mind, and invariably affects during birth and death.

sanskrit_text: पित्तं पित्तस्थानमाश्रित्य कुर्यात्तत्रैव सामान्यलक्षणम् । अन्यत्र सामान्यलक्षणमाहुः ॥२॥
transliteration: Pittaṃ pittasthānamāśritya kuryāttatraiva sāmānyalakṣaṇam | Anyatra sāmānyalakṣaṇamāhuḥ ||2||
commentary: The commentator explains that Pitta and Vata play a role in fever pathogenesis. In Agantu fever, the heat is produced at a later stage. The accidental disease becomes the natural one and the natural disease becomes accidental when they are more powerful. The Samprapti (pathogenesis) of accidental fever is different because of the differentiation of factors involved.

sanskrit_text: स्वेदावरोधः सन्तापः सर्वाङ्गग्रहणं तथा । युगपद्यत्र रोगे च स ज्वरो व्यपदिश्यते ।।३।।
transliteration: Svedāvarodhaḥ santāpaḥ sarvāṅgagrahaṇaṃ tathā | Yugapadyatra roge ca sa jvaro vyapadiśyate ||3||
commentary: Obstruction of sweat, burning and pain all over the body - if these symptoms are seen together in any disease, it is called as fever. The commentator explains that these symptoms must appear together to be considered fever. Svedāvarodha is obstruction of sweating, Santāpa is burning sensation of body and mind, and Sarvāṅgagrahaṇa is pain all over the body.

sanskrit_text: श्रमोऽरतिर्वैवर्ण्यं विरसास्यत्वमेव च । गुरुवाक्यबालद्वेषो लोचने सलिलप्लवः ॥४॥ तमः प्रवेश इव च सर्वस्येन्द्रियविभ्रमः । अग्निद्वेषश्च शीतं च शीतेच्छा च ज्वरे मता ॥५॥ ज्वलनातपवाय्वम्बुभक्तिद्वेषावनिश्चितौ । आलस्यं नयने सास्रं रोमहर्षोऽग्रहर्षणम् ॥६॥ शीतं शीतं ज्वरे शीतं कम्पः शिरसि वेदना । उत्पत्स्यति भविष्यति प्राग्रूपाण्यथ ज्वरे ॥७॥
transliteration: Śramo'ratirvaivarṇyaṃ virasāsyatvameva ca | Guruvākyabāladvēṣō lōcanē salilaplavaḥ ||4|| Tamaḥ pravēśa iva ca sarvasyēndriyavibhramaḥ | Agnidvēṣaśca śītaṃ ca śītēcchā ca jvarē matā ||5|| Jvalanātapavāyvambubhaktidvēṣāvaniścitau | Ālasyaṃ nayanē sāsraṃ rōmaharṣō'graharṣaṇam ||6|| Śītaṃ śītaṃ jvarē śītaṃ kampaḥ śirasi vēdanā | Utpatsyati bhaviṣyati prāgrūpāṇyatha jvarē ||7||
commentary: The premonitory symptoms of fever include: fatigue, disinterest, discolouration, opposite taste in the mouth, dislike of elders' words and children, eyes filled with tears, feeling of entering darkness, disturbance of senses, indefinite like and dislike of heat, sun, wind, water and food, laziness, tears in eyes, horripilation, craving for cold, and headache. The commentator explains that these are the signs of an upcoming fever that is yet to manifest.

topic_heading: Signs and Symptoms of Vāta Type of Fever
sanskrit_text: वेपथुर्विषमारम्भः कण्ठौष्ठशोषणम् । निद्रानाशः क्षवस्तम्भो रूक्षता सर्वगात्रता ॥८॥ शिरोहृद्रुक् शरीराध्मानं जृम्भा विविधा रुजः । वातजे ज्वरे ॥९॥
transliteration: Vepathurviṣamārambhaḥ kaṇṭhauṣṭhaśoṣaṇam | Nidrānāśaḥ kṣavastambho rūkṣatā sarvagāt ratā ||8|| Śirohṛdruk śarīrādh mānaṃ jṛmbhā vividhā ru jaḥ | Vāta je jvare ||9||
commentary: Trembling, irregularity in bouts of fever, drying of throat and lips, insomnia, obstruction of sneeze, dryness in the body, pain in the head, heart and body, perception of different or opposite taste, pain and bloating in the abdomen and yawning are present in fever caused by Vāta. The commentator explains that Kṣavastambha means obstruction of sneeze, and Ādhmana is painful bloating of the abdomen filled with Vāyu.

topic_heading: Signs and Symptoms of Pitta Type of Fever
sanskrit_text: तीव्रवेगोऽतिसारश्च निद्रानाशः सवेदना । कण्ठौष्ठतालुनासानां पाकः स्वेदः प्रलापनम् ॥१०॥ कटुकास्यत्वमूर्च्छा च दाहो मदस्तृष्णा भ्रमः । पीतविण्मूत्रनेत्रत्वं पैत्तिके ज्वरे ॥११॥
transliteration: Tīvravego'tisāraśca nidrānāśaḥ savedanā | Kaṇṭhauṣṭhatālunāsānāṃ pākaḥ svedaḥ pralāpanam ||10|| Kaṭukāsyatvamūrcchā ca dāho madastṛṣṇā bhramaḥ | Pītaviṇmūtranetratvaṃ paittike jvare ||11||
commentary: Severity in bouts of fever (high temperature), diarrhoea, less-sleep, vomiting, ulceration in the throat, lips, buccal cavity and nose, sweating, irrelevant talk, bitterness in the mouth, Syncope, burning sensation, intoxication, thirst, yellowishness in faeces, urine and eyes and giddiness are the signs and symptoms of Pitta type of fever. The commentator explains that diarrhoea in Pitta type of fever is due to mobile and liquid qualities of Pitta.

topic_heading: Signs and Symptoms of Kapha Type of Fever
sanskrit_text: स्तैमित्यं स्तिमितो वेग आलस्यं मधुरास्यता । शुक्लमूत्रपुरीषत्वं स्तम्भस्तृप्तिरथापि च ॥१२॥ गौरवं शीतमुत्क्लेदो रोमहर्षोऽतिनिद्रता । (स्रोतोरोधो रुगल्पत्वं प्रसेको लवणास्यता । नात्युष्णागात्रतां छर्दिर्लालास्रावोऽविपाकता ।।) प्रतिश्यायोऽरुचिः कासः कफजेऽक्ष्णोष्ठशुक्लता ।।१३।।
transliteration: Staimityaṃ stimito vega ālasyaṃ madhurāsyatā | Śuklamūtrapurīṣatvaṃ stambhastṛptirathāpi ca ||12|| Gauravaṃ śītamutkledo romaharṣo'tinidratā | (Srotorodho rugalpatvaṃ praseko lavaṇāsyatā | Nātyuṣṇāgātratāṃ chardirlālāsrāvo'vipākatā ||) Pratiśyāyo'ruciḥ kāsaḥ kaphaje'kṣṇoṣṭhaśuklatā ||13||
commentary: Feeling of immobility in the body, mild temperature, laziness, sweet taste in the mouth, whitish colour in urine and faeces, rigidity, feeling of contentment, heaviness, cold, nausea, skintillation, over-sleep, obstruction in the internal channels, less pain in the body, dribbling saliva, salty taste in the mouth, not so high temperature, vomiting, salivation, indigestion, rhinitis, distaste, cough and whitish colour in the eyes are the signs and symptoms of kapha fever. The commentator explains that Staimitya is the feeling of being covered by a wet-cloth, and Stimita Vega is mildness in temperature.

sanskrit_text: द्वन्द्वजाः सन्निपाताश्च द्विदोषैः सर्वलक्षणैः । सर्वलक्षणयुक्तास्तु संघाताः परिकीर्तिताः ॥१४॥
transliteration: Dvandvajāḥ sannipātāśca dvidoṣaiḥ sarvalakṣaṇaiḥ | Sarvalakṣaṇayuktāstu saṃghātāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ||14||
commentary: The dual-Dosa and Tridosa fevers are identified by the combination of symptoms. The commentator explains that these are known as Dvandva (dual-Dosa) and Sannipata (tri-Dosa) fevers, and their symptomatology is a combination of the individual Dosa symptoms mentioned earlier. This follows the principle of Prakrtisamasamavaya (similarity in qualities of cause and effect).

topic_heading: Signs and Symptoms of Vāta-Śleṣma Type of Fever
sanskrit_text: स्तैमित्यं सन्धिरुग्गौरवं निद्रा शिरसो ग्रहः । प्रतिश्यायः कासः स्वेदो दाहो मध्यस्तु वेगः स्याद्वातश्लेष्मज्वरे ॥१५-१६॥
transliteration: Staimityaṃ sandhiruggauravaṃ nidrā śiraso grahaḥ | Pratiśyāyaḥ kāsaḥ svedo dāho madhyastu vegaḥ syādvātaśleṣmajvare ||15-16||
commentary: Immobility, severe pain in the joints, sleep, heaviness in the body, gripping sensation in the head, corryza, cough, excessive sweat, burning sensation and medium bouts of temperature are the features of Vātaśleṣma type of fever. The commentator notes that excessive sweat in this context is due to irrelevant relationship of cause and effect.

topic_heading: Signs and Symptoms of Śleṣma-Pitta Type of Fever
sanskrit_text: आस्योपदेहः कटुता च तन्द्रा मोहश्च कासोऽरुचिरप्यथो तृट् । शीतोष्णयोश्चैव पुनः पुनश्च भवेत् कफपित्तोल्बणज्वरस्य लिङ्गम् ॥१७॥
transliteration: Āsyopadehaḥ kaṭutā ca tandrā mohaśca kāso'rucirapyatho tṛṭ | Śītoṣṇayoścaiva punaḥ punaśca bhavet kaphapittolbaṇajvarasya liṅgam ||17||
commentary: Sticky and bitter sensation in the mouth, drowsiness, delusion, cough, distaste, thirst and repeated alternative feeling of warmth and cold in the body are the features of Śleṣma-pitta type of fever. The commentator explains that sticky sensation is due to Kapha and bitterness, due to Pitta. Tandrā is sleep-like tiredness feeling in the eyes, and Moha is like syncope.

topic_heading: Signs and Symptoms of Sannipāta Fever
sanskrit_text: क्षणे दाहः क्षणे शीतमस्थिसन्धिशिरोरुजा । सास्नावे कलुषे रक्ते निर्धृगने चापि लोचने ॥१८॥ सस्वनी सरुजी कर्णो कण्ठः शूकैरिवावृतः । तद्रा मोहः प्रलापश्च कासः श्वासोऽरुचिर्भ्रमः ॥१९॥ परिद्रथा खरस्पशा जिह्वा स्तस्ताङ्गता परम् । छीवनं रक्तपितस्य कफेनोन्मिश्रितस्य च ॥२०॥ शिरसो लोठनं तृष्णा निद्रानाशो हृदि व्यथा । स्वेदमूत्रपुरीषाणां चिराद्दृशनमल्पशः ॥२१॥ कृशत्वं नातिगात्राणां प्रततं कण्ठकृजनम् । कोठानां श्यावरक्तानां मण्डलानां च दर्शनम् ॥२२॥ मूकत्वं स्रोतसां पाको गुरुत्वमुदरस्य च । चिरात् पाकश्च दोषाणां सन्निपातज्वराकृतिः ॥२३॥
transliteration: Kṣaṇe dāhaḥ kṣaṇe śītamasthisandhiśirorujā | Sāsnāve kaluṣe rakte nirdhṛgane cāpi locane ||18|| Sasvanī sarujī karṇo kaṇṭhaḥ śūkairivāvṛtaḥ | Tadrā mohaḥ pralāpaśca kāsaḥ śvāso'rucirbhramaḥ ||19|| Paridrathā kharaspāśā jihvā stastāṅgatā param | Chīvanaṃ raktapitasya kaphenonmiśritasya ca ||20|| Śiraso loṭhanaṃ tṛṣṇā nidrānāśo hṛdi vyathā | Svedamūtrapurīṣāṇāṃ cirāddṛśanamalpaśaḥ ||21|| Kṛśatvaṃ nātigātrāṇāṃ pratataṃ kaṇṭhakṛjanam | Koṭhānāṃ śyāvaraktānāṃ maṇḍalānāṃ ca darśanam ||22|| Mūkatvaṃ srotasāṃ pāko gurutvamudarasya ca | Cirāt pākaśca doṣāṇāṃ sannipātajvarākṛtiḥ ||23||
commentary: Alternate feeling of burning and cold within moments, pain in the bones, joints and head; exudation, turbidity and redness and feeling of protrusion in the eyes; sounds and pain in the ears, pricking sensation in the throat, drowsiness, delusion, delirium, cough, dyspnoea, distaste, giddiness, burnt-rough feeling on the tongue, flaccidity in the body, spitting blood and Pitta sometimes mixed with Kapha, rotating the head, thirst, lack of sleep, pain in the heart, less amount of sweat, urine and faeces with long gaps, mild emaciation, continuous wheezing sounds in the throat, appearance of bullae in blackish or red colour and patches on the body, inability of speech, ulceration in the orifices, heaviness in the abdomen and delayed digestion of impurities are the features of Sannipata fever. The commentator explains that these symptoms correspond to one of the thirteen Sannipata fevers.

sanskrit_text: दोषे विबद्धे नष्टाग्नौ सम्पूर्णलक्षणज्वरः । प्रत्याख्येयो दुरुत्सर्गः सन्निपातो न सिध्यति ॥२४॥
transliteration: Doṣe vibaddhe naṣṭāgnau sampūrṇalakṣaṇajvaraḥ | Pratyākhyeyo durutsargaḥ sannipāto na sidhyati ||24||
commentary: If the Dosas are not passed freely in the system, the digestive fire is destroyed and the manifestation is complete with full symptomatology, that Sannipāta fever is incurable otherwise it is difficult to cure. The commentator explains that Dosa here means excreta and Pitta etc. Dosas. Sannipata is foremost among the tough diseases.

sanskrit_text: सन्निपातज्वरस्यान्ते कर्णमूले सुदारुणः । शोथः सञ्जायते तेन कन्निष्टदेव प्रमुच्यते ।।२५।।
transliteration: Sannipātajvarasyānte karṇamūle sudāruṇaḥ | Śothaḥ sañjāyate tena kanniṣṭadeva pramucyate ||25||
commentary: Severe inflammation at the root of the ear originates at the end of Sannipāta fever (as a complication) from which somebody alone is relieved (all others die). The commentator explains that this is a complication of Sannipatajvara.

topic_heading: Āgantu Jvara (Fever due to Extrinsic Factors)
sanskrit_text: अभिघाताभिघाराभ्यामभिशपापाभिभङ्गतः । आगन्तुजायते दोषैर्यथास्वं तं विभावयेत् ॥२६॥ श्यावास्यता विषकृते तथाऽतीसारमेव च । भक्तारुचिः पिपासा च तोदश्च सह मूर्च्छया ॥२७॥ ओषधिगम्यजे मूर्च्छां शिरोरुग्वमथुः क्षवः । कामजे चित्तविभ्रंशस्तन्द्राऽऽलस्यमभोजनम् ॥२८॥ हृदये वेदना चास्य गात्रं च परिशूंच्यति । भयात् प्रलापः शोकाच्च भवेत् कोपाच्च वेपथुः । अभिघाराभिशपाभ्यां मोहस्तुष्णा च जायते ॥२९॥ भूताभिभङ्गादुद्वेगो हास्यरोदनकम्पनम् ॥
transliteration: Abhighātābhighārābhyāmabhiśapāpābhibhaṅgataḥ | Āgantujāyate doṣairyathāsvaṃ taṃ vibhāvayet ||26|| Śyāvāsyatā viṣakṛte tathā'tīsārameva ca | Bhaktāruciḥ pipāsā ca todaśca saha mūrcchayā ||27|| Oṣadhigamyaje mūrcchāṃ śirorugvamathuḥ kṣavaḥ | Kāmaje cittavibhraṃśastandrā''lasyamabhojanam ||28|| Hṛdaye vedanā cāsya gātraṃ ca pariśūṃcyati | Bhayāt pralāpaḥ śokācca bhavet kopācca vepathuḥ | Abhighārābhiśapābhyāṃ mohastuṣṇā ca jāyate ||29|| Bhūtābhibhaṅgādudvego hāsyarodanakampanam ||
commentary: Āgantu Jvara (sudden fever) is caused by injury, witch-craft, wrath of pious people and affliction of evil spirits. In fever caused by poison, there is blackish discolouration in the mouth, distaste in food, thirst, pricking sensation and syncope. In fever caused by strong medicinal odours, syncope, headache, vomiting and sneezing. In Kāma Jvara (fever caused by unsatisfied lust), instability of mind, drowsiness, laziness, not eating, pain in the heart and emaciation. Delirium occurs in fevers caused by fear and grief. Trembling in fever caused by anger. Fever caused by witch-craft features delusion and thirst. Fever resulting from affliction of evil spirits has tension, irrelevant laughing, weeping and trembling.

sanskrit_text: कामशोकभयाद्वायुः क्रोधात् पित्तं तथा कफः । भूताभिभङ्गात्संसर्गस्त्रयो दोषाः प्रकुप्यति ॥३०॥
transliteration: Kāmaśokabhayādvāyuḥ krodhāt pittaṃ tathā kaphaḥ | Bhūtābhibhaṅgātsaṃsargastrayo doṣāḥ prakupyati ||30||
commentary: Vāta aggravates due to lust, grief and fear, Pitta due to anger and all the three Dosas due to affliction of Bhutas. The commentator explains that there will be the signs similar to those of the afflicted Bhuta along with the qualities of aggravated Dosas.

sanskrit_text: अल्पोऽथवा यदा दोषो बलवानपि नाश्रयम् । लब्ध्वा कुर्याज्ज्वरं दोषो विषमं धातुसंश्रयात् ॥३१॥
transliteration: Alpo'thavā yadā doṣo balavānapi nāśrayam | Labdhvā kuryājjvaraṃ doṣo viṣamaṃ dhātusaṃśrayāt ||31||
commentary: Dosa which is aggravated but feeble to cause any trouble, or that of an individual who has been relieved from fever, enters one of the Rasa etc. tissues and causes Visamajvara (irregular fever). The commentator explains that 'Alpo Bala' means the Dosa which is aggravated but having no capability to cause fever initially, but possesses such strength in due course of time.

sanskrit_text: रसरक्तगतः सन्ततं मांसगतोऽन्येद्युकः । मेदोगतः स्यात्तृतीयकोऽस्थिमज्जगतश्चतुर्थकः ॥३२॥ विषमो घोरः स्याच्चतुर्थको रोगसङ्करः । आख्यातो धातुभिर्ज्वरः सुश्रुतेन चिकित्सिते ॥३३॥
transliteration: Rasaraktagataḥ santataṃ māṃsagato'nyedyukaḥ | Medogataḥ syāttṛtīyako'sthimajjagataścaturthakaḥ ||32|| Viṣamo ghoraḥ syāccaturthako rogasaṅkaraḥ | Ākhyāto dhātubhirjvaraḥ suśrutena cikitsite ||33||
commentary: When the Dosa is lodged in Rasa dhatu, it causes Santata fever; in Rakta dhatu also Santata. Anyeduska fever occurs as the Dosa enters the Mamsa. The fever is called Trtiyaka when it is in the Medas. Caturthaka occurs when the vitiated Dosa affects Asthi and Majja. The commentator explains that Ghora is unbearable and Antaka means like Yama, the death-God. Roga Sankaram means a syndrome of many diseases.

topic_heading: Time of Bouts of Irregular Fever
sanskrit_text: सप्ताहं वा दशाहं वा द्वादशाहमथापि वा । सन्ततो योऽविसर्गी स्यात्सन्ततः स निगद्यते ॥३४॥ अहोरात्रे सततको द्वौ कालावनुवर्तते । अन्येष्टुष्कस्त्वहोरात्र एककालं प्रवर्तते ॥३५॥ तृतीयस्तृतीयेऽहनि, चतुर्थेऽहनि चतुर्थकः ॥
transliteration: Saptāhaṃ vā daśāhaṃ vā dvādaśāhamathāpi vā | Santato yo'visargī syātsantataḥ sa niga dyate ||34|| Ahorātre satatako dvau kālāvanuvartate | Anyeṣṭuṣkastvahorātra ekakālaṃ pravartate ||35|| Tṛtīyastṛtīye'hani, caturthe'hani caturthakaḥ ||
commentary: The fever that continuously exists up to seven days, ten days or twelve days is called Santata. Satata manifests twice in a day and night, Anyeduska once in a day and night, Trtiyaka on every third day and Caturthaka manifests on every fourth day. The commentator explains that the differentiation of time duration is the predominance of three Dosas, and the Santata fever of twelve days is Tridosaja.

sanskrit_text: भूताभिभङ्गात्संसर्गस्त्रयो दोषाः प्रकुप्यति । विषमज्वरो भूतज इत्याहुरेके ॥३६॥
transliteration: Bhūtābhibhaṅgātsaṃsargastrayo doṣāḥ prakupyati | Viṣamajvaro bhūtaja ityāhureke ||36||
commentary: Some scholars say that Visama Jvara is caused by affliction of evil spirits. The commentator explains that this is mentioned in some treatises, and generally Āgantu fever is followed in the Visama Jvara.

topic_heading: Variations of Tertian and Quartan Fever
sanskrit_text: कफपित्तात्त्रिकग्राही पृष्ठाद्वातकफात्मकः । वातपित्तात्तु शिरोग्राही स्यात्तृतीयकः ॥३७॥ चतुर्थको दर्शयति प्रभावं द्विविधं ज्वरः । जङ्गाभ्यां श्लैष्मिकः पूर्वं शिरसोऽनिलसंभवः ॥३८॥
transliteration: Kaphapittāttrikagrāhī pṛṣṭhādvātakaphātmakaḥ | Vātapittāttu śirogrāhī syāttṛtīyakaḥ ||37|| Caturthako darśayati prabhāvaṃ dvividhaṃ jvaraḥ | Jaṅgābhyāṃ ślaiṣmikaḥ pūrvaṃ śiraso'nilasaṃbhavaḥ ||38||
commentary: Trītiyaka (tertian) fever is of three variations. Due to predominance of Kapha and Pitta, this fever is seated in the Trika (Coccyx); the second variety afflicts the Pṛṣṭha (back) due to domination of Vāta-Kapha and the third one grips the head because of the affluence of Vāta-Pitta. Caturthaka (quartan) fever manifests its effect in two ways - the two calf muscles are first affected in one type where Śleṣma is dominant and in another, head is affected due to predominance of Vāta. The commentator explains that when the affliction is in the Coccyx, pain exists in that particular region.

sanskrit_text: विषमश्चतुर्थकविपर्ययः । द्व्यहं ज्वरयत्यादौ द्व्यहं मुञ्चति चान्ततः ॥३९॥
transliteration: Viṣamaścaturthakaviparyayaḥ | Dvyahaṃ jvarayatyādau dvyahaṃ muñcati cāntataḥ ||39||
commentary: The reversal quartan fever grips for two days with relief on predecessor and successive days to the two days (on which fever manifests). The commentator explains that some treatises mention the fever afflicting bone and marrow is Caturthaka Viparyaya which relieves on the first day, manifests for the next two days and again relieves on the fourth day.

sanskrit_text: वातबलासको ज्वरो यो मन्दज्वरः स रूक्षः शोफः सादः स्तम्भो गात्राणां श्लेष्मणश्च बाहुल्यम् ॥४०॥
transliteration: Vātabalāsako jvaro yo mandajvaraḥ sa rūkṣaḥ śophaḥ sādaḥ stambho gātrāṇāṃ śleṣmaṇaśca bāhulyam ||40||
commentary: The individual afflicted by Vātabalāsā fever has continuous mild fever, dryness in the body, oedema, depression, rigidity in the limbs and profuse Ślesma. The commentator explains that Balāsaka means Slesma, and as this is caused by Vata and Kapha, it is named thus.

sanskrit_text: स्नेहगौरवमुष्मा च गात्रे यस्य स ज्वरः । मन्दोष्णशीतो देहे स प्रलेपकः स्मृतः ॥४१॥
transliteration: Snehagauravamuṣmā ca gātre yasya sa jvaraḥ | Mandoṣṇaśīto dehe sa pralepakaḥ smṛtaḥ ||41||
commentary: The individual feels as if his limbs are coated with heat and heaviness. He has mild fever of cold touch in the body. Such person is to be known as suffering from Pralepaka fever. The commentator explains that the connection of heat and heaviness is due to Kapha and Pitta predominance.

sanskrit_text: विदग्धेऽन्नरसे देहे पित्तश्लेष्मोल्बणे तथा । अर्धं तपति देहस्य शीतं चार्धं प्रजायते ॥४२॥ काये पित्ते स्थिते शीतं हस्तपादेषु जायते । काये श्लेष्मणि पित्ते च हस्तपादेषु दह्यते ॥४३॥ काये पित्ते हस्तपादेषु श्लेष्मणि । काये श्लेष्मणि हस्तपादेषु पित्ते ॥४४॥
transliteration: Vidagdhe'nne rase dehe pittakaphāṭṭolbaṇe tathā | Ardhaṃ tapati dehasya śītaṃ cārdhaṃ prajāyate ||42|| Kāye pitte sthite śītaṃ hastapādeṣu jāyate | Kāye śleṣmaṇi pitte ca hastapādeṣu dahyate ||43|| Kāye pitte hastapādeṣu śleṣmaṇi | Kāye śleṣmaṇi hastapādeṣu pitte ||44||
commentary: When the Annarasa is over burnt in the body where Kapha and Pitta are already predominant, half of the body is warm and remaining half is cool. When Pitta is vitiated in the alimentary canal and Kapha in the extremities, the body is warm and hands and legs are cool. When vitiated Kapha is in the alimentary canal and Pitta in the extremities, the body is cool and extremities are felt warm. The commentator explains that warmth is due to Pitta and Kapha is the causative factor for the cool touch.

sanskrit_text: त्वक्स्थौ श्लेष्मानिलौ शीतमादौ जनयतो ज्वरो । तयोः प्रशान्तयोः पितमन्ते दाहं करोति च ॥४५॥ करोत्यादौ तथा पितं त्वक्स्थं दाहमतीव च । तस्मिन् प्रशान्ते त्वितरी कुरुतः शीतमन्ततः ॥४६॥ द्वावेती दाहशीतादिज्वरी संसर्गजौ स्मृती । दाहपूर्वस्तयोः कष्टः कृच्छ्रसाध्यतमश्च सः ॥४७॥
transliteration: Tvaksthau śleṣmānilau śītamādau janayato jvaro | Tayoḥ praśāntayoḥ pitamante dāhaṃ karoti ca ||45|| Karotyādau tathā pitaṃ tvaksthaṃ dāhamatīva ca | Tasmin praśānte tvitari kurutaḥ śītamantataḥ ||46|| Dvāvetī dāhaśītādijvarī saṃsargajau smṛtī | Dāhapūrvastayoḥ kaṣṭaḥ kṛcchrasādhyatamaśca saḥ ||47||
commentary: When vitiated Kapha and Vāta are seated in the skin, the fever starts with cold touch and at the end when these two pacify, burning sensation is felt due to Pitta. In the same way, Pitta which is seated in the skin, causes excessive burning sensation all over the body in the beginning of fever. When it pacifies, the remaining two (Kapha and Vāta) get momentum and cause cold touch. These two are called Dāhapūrva and Sītapūrva fevers. Dāhapūrva type is a troublesome disease with involvement of 2 dosas and very difficult for cure. The commentator explains that the Samsarga here is the connection of Saumya (soft-cool) and Agneya (fiery) Dosas.

sanskrit_text: रसस्थे गुरुता हृदयोत्क्लेशो ग्लानिश्छर्दिररुचिः सदनम् ॥४८॥ रक्तस्थे स्रवणं दाहो मोहश्छर्दिर्भ्रमः प्रलापः । कोठाः पिपासा च ॥४९॥ मांसस्थे जङ्घोत्क्लेशः पिपासा बहुमूत्रता च । ऊष्मा दाहो निपातनं ग्लानिः ॥५०॥ मेदःस्थे स्वेदो बहुः पिपासा मूर्च्छा प्रलापश्छर्दिः । दुर्गन्धता गात्रस्यारुचिः सदनं क्लमः ॥५१॥ अस्थिस्थे भेदः शब्दः श्वासोऽतीसारश्छर्दिः । अङ्गानामनवस्थानम् ॥५२॥ मज्जस्थे तमः प्रवेशो हिक्का कासः शीतं छर्दिः । अन्तर्दाहो महान् श्वासो मर्मच्छेदश्च ॥५३॥ शुक्रस्थे मरणमेव विद्यात् । शुक्रस्थे शिश्नस्तम्भो बहुशुक्रविसर्गश्च ॥५४॥
transliteration: Rasasthe gurutā hṛdayotkleśo glāniśchardiraruciḥ sadanam ||48|| Raktasthe sravaṇaṃ dāho mohaśchardirbhramaḥ pralāpaḥ | Koṭhāḥ pipāsā ca ||49|| Māṃsasthe jaṅghotkleśaḥ pipāsā bahumūtratā ca | Ūṣmā dāho nipātanaṃ glāniḥ ||50|| Medaḥsthe svedo bahuḥ pipāsā mūrcchā pralāpaśchardiḥ | Durgandhatā gātrasyāruciḥ sadanaṃ klamaḥ ||51|| Asthisthe bhedaḥ śabdaḥ śvāso'tisāraśchardīḥ | Aṅgānāmanavasthānam ||52|| Majjasthe tamaḥ praveśo hikkā kāsaḥ śītaṃ chardiḥ | Antardāho mahān śvāso marmacchedaśca ||53|| Śukrasthe maraṇameva vidyāt | Śukrasthe śiśnastambho bahuśukravisargaśca ||54||
commentary: Heaviness, nausea, exhaustion, vomiting, distaste and depression are the signs and symptoms when the fever is attached to the Rasa Dhātu. Dribbling of blood, burning sensation, delusion, vomiting, giddiness, irrelevant talk, bullae on the skin and thirst are seen when the fever is lodged in the Rakta. Squeezing sensation in the calf muscles, thirst, excessive defaecation and micturition, heat on the body, internal burning sensation, falling down and fatigue are the features of Mamsagata Jvara. Profuse sweat, thirst, syncope, irrelevant talk, vomiting, bad odour of the body, distaste, fatigue and intolerance are seen in fever seated in Medas. Breaking sensation in the bones, wheezing sounds in breathe, diarrhoea, vomiting, inability to keep up the bodily limbs are present in Asthi. Feeling of darkness, hiccup, cough, cold, vomiting, internal burning, severe dyspnoea and cutting pain in the vital parts are the signs and symptoms in Majjā. One will die when fever gets seated in Śukra; there will be rigidity in the penis and profuse flow of semen. The commentator explains that fever seated in Rasa, Rakta, Mamsa and Medas is curable, difficult in Asthi and Majjā, and incurable in Śukra.

sanskrit_text: वर्षाशरद्वसन्तेषु वाताद्यैः प्राकृतः क्रमात् । वैकृतोऽन्यः स दुःसाध्यः प्राकृतश्चानिलोद्भवः ॥५५॥
transliteration: Varṣāśaradvasanteṣu vātādyaiḥ prākṛtaḥ kramāt | Vaikṛto'nyaḥ sa duḥsādhyaḥ prākṛtaścānilodbhavaḥ ||55||
commentary: Fever that occurs in certain seasons is called Prākṛta Jvara: Vāta Jvara in Prāvṛt (rainy) season, Pitta Jvara in Sarat (moon-light) season and Kapha Jvara in Vasanta (spring) season are natural fevers. Other fevers are Vaikṛta (unnatural) and they are difficult to cure including the natural one caused by Vāta. The commentator explains that the other unnatural fevers mean Pitta Jvara and Kapha Jvara in rainy season, Vata Jvara and Kapha Jvara in moon-light season, Vata Jvara and Pitta Jvara in spring season.

sanskrit_text: वर्षासु मारुतः पित्तश्लेष्मभिः सह कुप्यति । शरदि पित्तं कफेन सह वसन्ते कफः पित्तवाताभ्याम् ॥५६-५७॥
transliteration: Varṣāsu mārutaḥ pittakaphābhyāṃ saha kupyati | Śaradi pittaṃ kaphena saha vasante kaphaḥ pittavātābhyām ||56-57||
commentary: In rainy season, Maruta (Vata) gets vitiated and causes fever with the association of Pitta and Slesma. Pitta, in the same way causes fever in Sarat (moon-light season) with the help of Kapha. Kapha is vitiated in Vasanta (spring season) and causes fever with the association of Vata and Pitta. The commentator explains that during Visarga Kala (the period in which Sun bestows the universe with strength), there is no fear of any complication by observing fasting.

sanskrit_text: यस्मिन् काले हि यो दोषः प्रकृत्या कुप्यति । तस्मिन् काले तज्जनितो ज्वरो जायते वर्धते च ॥५८॥
transliteration: Yasmin kāle hi yo doṣaḥ prakṛtyā kupyati | Tasmin kāle tajjanito jvaro jāyate vardhate ca ||58||
commentary: In a particular time that is congenial to the particular Dosa, the fever manifests or it increases. The commentator explains that during the period of aggravation of Vata, the fever caused by Vata is originated or increased, and the same is the case with the fevers of Pitta and Kapha.

sanskrit_text: अन्तर्वेगो ज्वरो यस्य दाहस्तीव्रस्तृषा महती । प्रलापः श्वासः संमोहः सन्ध्यस्थिरुग्भ्रमः ॥५९॥ अस्वेदो विबन्धश्च अन्तर्वेगज्वराकृतिः । बहिर्वेगस्तु यो ज्वरो बहिरुष्मा भवत्यल्पतृट्क इत्यादि ॥६०॥
transliteration: Antarvego jvaro yasya dāhastīvrastṛṣā mahatī | Pralāpaḥ śvāsaḥ saṃmohaḥ sandhyasthirugbhramaḥ ||59|| Asvedo vibandhaśca antarvegajvarākṛtiḥ | Bahirvegastu yo jvaro bahiruṣmā bhavatyalpatṛṭka ityādi ||60||
commentary: Internal burning sensation, excessive thirst, delirium, dyspnoea, giddiness, pain in the joints and bones, lack of sweating and constipation are the features of Antarvega Jvara (internal fever). Excessive heat on the body, thirst etc., are less in the body - these are the signs and symptoms of Bahirvega Jvara (external fever) and this is easily curable. The commentator explains that Mardava is lesser intensity of these symptoms, and Bahirvega fever is easily curable while Antarvega fever is difficult for cure.

sanskrit_text: लालाप्रसेको हृदयोत्क्लेशः स्तैमित्यमरोचकः ॥६१॥ तन्द्रालस्याविपाकास्यवैरस्यं गुरुगात्रता । क्षुत्स्वल्पता बहुमूत्रता स्तब्धता बलमन्दता ॥६२॥ आमज्वरस्य लिङ्गानि, न दद्यात्तत्र भेषजम् । भेषजं ह्यामदोषस्य भूयो ज्वलयति ज्वरम् ॥६३॥
transliteration: Lālāpraseko hṛdayotkleśaḥ staimityamarocakaḥ ||61|| Tandrālasya vipākās yavairasyaṃ gurugāt ratā | Kṣut svalpatā bahumūtratā stabdhatā balamandatā ||62|| Āmajvarasya liṅgāni, na dadyāttatra bheṣajam | Bheṣajaṃ hyāmadoṣasya bhūyo jvalayati jvaram ||63||
commentary: Dribbling of saliva, nausea, feeling of heaviness in the heart, drowsiness, lassitude, indigestion, distaste, heaviness in the body, loss of appetite, excessive urination, rigidity in the limbs and strong fever are the features of Ama Jvara. One should not give medicine in such condition, otherwise the medicine itself induces more fever (causes irregular fever). The commentator explains that 'Bhesaja' here means medicine other than food and drink, and in Ama Jvara, water boiled to half consistency along with six herbs is given.

sanskrit_text: ज्वरवेगोऽधिकस्तृष्णा प्रलापः श्वसनं भ्रमः । मलप्रवृत्तिरुत्क्लेशः पच्यमानस्य लक्षणम् ॥६४॥ क्षुत् क्षामता लघुत्वं च गात्राणां ज्वरमार्दवम् । दोषप्रवृत्तिरष्टाहो निरामज्वरलक्षणम् ॥६५॥
transliteration: Jvaravego'dhikastṛṣṇā pralāpaḥ śvasanaṃ bhramaḥ | Malapravṛttirutkleśaḥ pacyamānasya lakṣaṇam ||64|| Kṣut kṣāmatā laghutvaṃ ca gātrāṇāṃ jvaramārdavam | Doṣapravṛttiraṣṭāho nirāmajvaralakṣaṇam ||65||
commentary: Temperature, excessive thirst, delirium, dyspnoea and giddiness, passing of faeces and vomiting sensation are the symptoms of Pacyamana (digesting) fever. Appetite, weakness, lightness of the body, less temperature, movement of Dosas and (completion of) eight days are the features of Nirāma (digested) fever. The commentator explains that the Samata (association with indigestion) relates to two aspects: one of Rasa (chyle) and the other of Dosa. Rasasamata has symptoms like distaste, while Dosasamata features acute condition which ceases after 8 days.

sanskrit_text: हेतुभिर्बहुभिर्बलिभिर्ज्वरः स्याद्बहुलक्षणः । सर्वेन्द्रियविनाशश्च प्राणान्तकृदसाध्यः ॥६६॥ क्षीणस्य शूनस्य गम्भीरो दैर्घरात्रिकः । केशसीमन्तकृच्चापि ज्वरो हन्ति न संशयः ॥६७-६८॥ गम्भीरः श्वासकासाभ्यां विबद्धश्च ज्वरो हन्ति ॥६९॥ विषमो रात्रौ ज्वरो हन्ति क्षीणं रूक्षं च गम्भीरः । हन्ति ज्वरः ॥७०॥ विसंज्ञं पतन्तं मुह्यन्तं शीतादितोऽन्तरुष्णम् ॥७१॥ रोमहर्षयुक्तं रक्ताक्षं हृदि संघातशूलवन्तम् । वक्रयेण चैवोच्छ्वसितं तं ज्वरो हन्ति मानवम् ॥७२॥ हिक्काश्वासतृषायुक्तं मूढं विभ्रान्तलोचनम् । सन्तोच्छ्वासिनं क्षीणं नरं क्षपयति ज्वरः । हतप्रभेन्द्रियं क्षीणमरोचकनिधीडितम् । गम्भीरतीक्ष्णवेगं तं ज्वरितं परिवर्जयेत् ॥७३॥
transliteration: Hetubhirbahubhirbalibhirjvaraḥ syādbahulakṣaṇaḥ | Sarvendriyavināśaśca prāṇāntakṛd asādhyaḥ ||66|| Kṣīṇasya śūnasya gambhīro dairgharātrikaḥ | Keśasīmantakṛccāpi jvaro hanti na saṃśayaḥ ||67-68|| Gambhīraḥ śvāsakāsābhyāṃ vibaddhaśca jvaro hanti ||69|| Viṣamo rātrau jvaro hanti kṣīṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ ca gambhīraḥ | Hanti jvaraḥ ||70|| Visaṃjñaṃ patantaṃ muhyantaṃ śītādito'ntaruṣṇam ||71|| Romaharṣayuktaṃ raktākṣaṃ hṛdi saṃghātaśūlavantam | Vakrayeṇa caivocchvasitaṃ taṃ jvaro hanti mānavam ||72|| Hikkāśvāsatṛṣāyuktaṃ mūḍhaṃ vibhrāntalocanam | Santocchvāsinaṃ kṣīṇaṃ naraṃ kṣapayati jvaraḥ | Hataprabhendriyaṃ kṣīṇamarocakanidhīḍitam | Gambhīratīkṣṇavegaṃ taṃ jvaritaṃ parivarjayet ||73||
commentary: The fever caused by many and stronger aetiological factors, has wider symptoms, destroys all the organs of the body and takes away the life. The fever that affects the weak individual and those suffering from oedema; severe fever that continuously affects throughout night and that in which the hair forms parting on the scalp is incurable. The fever with internal burning sensation, associated with dyspnoea and cough and constipation is called Gambhira. The fever which is irregular, persists all through the night, affects the weak and very dry and which is serious, kills him. If one loses his senses, lies down or falls down frequently and suffers from outward cold and inner burning sensation, he will die with fever. If one suffers from horripilation, redness in the eyes, suffers from heavy pain in the heart and breathes through the mouth, the fever destroys him. The fever emaciates that individual who has hiccup, dyspnoea, thirst, senselessness, terrified looks, continuous heavy breathe and weakness. That individual suffering from fever should not be admitted for treatment who has lost his bodily lusture and senses, and suffer from weakness, distaste, severe and fast bouts of temperature.

topic_heading: Premonitory Symptoms of Relief of Fever
sanskrit_text: दाहः स्वेदो भ्रमस्तृष्णा कम्पो विद्भेदोऽसंज्ञता । कूजनं चास्य वैगन्ध्यमाकृतिर्ज्वरमोक्षणे ॥७४॥
transliteration: Dāhaḥ svedo bhramastṛṣṇā kampo vidbhedo'saṃjñatā | Kūjanaṃ cāsya vaigandhyamākṛtirjvaramokṣaṇe ||74||
commentary: Burning sensation, sweating, giddiness, thirst, trembling, passing of faeces, loss of sensation, making unclear sounds and stinking of the body are the features that are seen while fever relieves. The commentator explains that Kūjana is making unclear sounds, and Vāgbhata says that the Dosa, while detaching from the Dhātu, becomes strong and irritates them causing these symptoms.

sanskrit_text: स्वेदः स्रोतोविशुद्धिर्लघुता कण्डूश्च शिरसि । मुखोपदेहो जिह्वायाः क्षवथुर्भक्तकाङ्क्षा च ॥७५॥
transliteration: Svedaḥ srotoviśuddhirlaghutā kaṇḍūśca śirasi | Mukhopadeho jihvāyāḥ kṣavathurbhaktakāṅkṣā ca ||75||
commentary: Sweating, lightness of the body, itching sensation, ulceration in the mouth, sneezing and desire for food are the features of an individual who got relieved of fever. The commentator explains that sweating comes due to clarity in the channels, and the above symptoms are to be considered together to determine the complete relief of fever with no relapse.

sanskrit_text: गुर्वतिस्निग्धरूक्षोष्णद्रवस्थूलातिशीतलैः । विरुद्धाध्यशनाजीर्णैर्विषमैश्चापिभोजनैः ॥१॥ स्नेहाद्यैरतियुक्तैश्च मिथ्यायुक्तैर्विषैर्भयैः । शोकाद्दुष्टाम्बुमद्यातिपानैरसात्म्यतर्पणैः ॥२॥ जलाभिरमणैर्वेगविघातैः क्रिमिदोषतः । नृणां भवत्यतीसारो लक्षणं तस्य वक्ष्यते ॥३॥
transliteration: Gurvatisnigdharūkṣoṣṇadravasthūlātiśītalaiḥ | Viruddhādhyāśanājīrṇairviṣamaiścāpibhojanaiḥ ||1|| Sneghādyairatiyuktaishca mithyāyuktairviṣairbhayaiḥ | Śokāddduṣṭāmbumadyātipānairasātmyatarpaṇaiḥ ||2|| Jalābhiramaṇairvegavighātaiḥ krimidoṣataḥ | Nṛṇāṃ bhavatyatīsāro lakṣaṇaṃ tasya vakṣyate ||3||
commentary: Atīsāra (diarrhoea) is caused by foods that are heavy, excessively dry or oily, too warm, more liquid, too solid or too cold, incompatible; over eating, foods that cause indigestion, untimely food, indulging in over adoption of Sneha (oleation) procedures, improper cleansing, foods of poisonous nature; due to fear, grief, polluted water, excessive consumption of alcohol, non homologous foods and those not to be used in particular seasons, playing in water, by suppression of natural urges and due to worm-infestation. The commentator explains that Guru includes both quantity and quality heaviness, and Viruddha means incompatible combination of foods like milk and fish.

sanskrit_text: संशम्याग्निं प्रवृद्धोऽपां धातुरधः प्रणुतः सरति । सरत्यतीव गुदेन सोऽतिसार इत्युच्यते ॥४॥
transliteration: Saṃśamyāgniṃ pravṛddho'pāṃ dhātura dhaḥ praṇutaḥ sarati | Sarat yatīva gudena so'tisāra ity ucyate ||4||
commentary: The liquid factor of the body, on increasing in quantity, subdues the digestive fire and gets mixed with the faecal matter which is driven downwards by Vāta and passed out repeatedly. This is called diarrhoea (Atisāra) which is severe and of six types. The commentator explains that 'Apām Dhātu' includes chyle, water, urine, sweat, fat, Kapha, Pitta and Rakta (blood). The name Atisāra means 'it goes repeatedly in more quantity in the downward direction through the anus'.

sanskrit_text: हृन्नाभिगुदकुक्ष्यामसदनं वातवर्चोविबन्धः । विष्टम्भमाध्मानमजीर्णं चातीसारपूर्वरूपम् ॥५॥
transliteration: Hṛnnābhigudakukṣyāmasadanaṃ vātavarcovibandhaḥ | Viṣṭambhamādh mānamajīrṇaṃ cātīsārapūrvarūpam ||5||
commentary: Pinning sensation in the heart, navel, anus, abdomen and stomach; depression of the body-gait, obstruction of fart, constipation, flatulence and indigestion are the prodromata of diarrhoea. The commentator explains that Kuksi is a part of Udara (abdomen), hence it should not be considered as repetition. Obstruction of fart and constipation are seen when the Dosa and Dusya interact before the disease manifests.

sanskrit_text: रूक्षं फेनिलमल्पमलं सशब्दं सरुजं च । वातातिसारे विजानीयात् ॥६॥
transliteration: Rūkṣaṃ phenilamalpamalaṃ saśabdaṃ sarujaṃ ca | Vātātisāre vijānīyāt ||6||
commentary: The faecal matter is reddish in colour, froathy, dry and passed repeatedly in smaller quantities with pain and sound due to Vata. The commentator explains that though Vāta has no colour and shape by itself, the reddishness results due to the interaction of Doṣa and Dūṣya.

sanskrit_text: पीतं हरितं रक्ताभं तृण्मूर्च्छादाहपाकैः । पित्तातिसारे च ॥७॥
transliteration: Pītaṃ haritaṃ raktābhaṃ tṛṇmūrcchādāhapākaiḥ | Pittātisāre ca ||7||
commentary: The faeces is yellow, bluish or blood-red in colour. The patient has thirst, syncope, burning sensation and ulceration in diarrhoea caused by Pitta. The commentator explains that burning sensation is seen all over the body while Pāka (ulceration) is seen in the anus only.

sanskrit_text: शुक्लं घनं कफसंसृष्टं गन्धं शीतं रोमहर्षम् । कफातिसारे जानीयात् ॥८॥
transliteration: Śuklaṃ ghanaṃ kaphasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ gandhaṃ śītaṃ romaharṣam | Kaphātisāre jānīyāt ||8||
commentary: The faeces in diarrhoea due to Slesma is white in colour, solid in consistency, mixed with phlegm, has the smell of undigested stuff, cold in touch and the patient has horripilation. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Kapha type of diarrhoea.

sanskrit_text: सर्वदोषलिङ्गैर्युक्तं सन्निपातातिसारम् । विद्यादसाध्यं च ॥९॥
transliteration: Sarvadoṣaliṅgairyuktaṃ sannipātātisāram | Vidyādasādhyaṃ ca ||9||
commentary: Diarrhoea caused by Tridosas has the faecal matter which looks like fat of the pig and/or meat-washed water associated with the signs and symptoms of all the three Dosas and it is difficult for cure. The commentator explains that this is the most severe form of diarrhoea.

sanskrit_text: तैस्तैर्भर्वैः शोचतोऽत्यल्पाशनस्य बाष्पोष्मा वै वह्निमाविश्य जन्तोः । कोष्ठं गत्वा क्षोभयेतस्य रक्तं तच्चाधस्तात् काकणन्तीप्रकाशम् ॥१०॥
transliteration: Taistairbharvaiḥ śocato'tyalpāśanasya bāṣpoṣmā vai vahnimāviśya jantoḥ | Koṣṭhaṃ gatvā kṣobhayet asya raktaṃ taccādhastāt kākaṇantīprakāśam ||10||
commentary: Due to certain reasons, the griefing individual takes a little quantity of food and the heat generated through his tears, gets to the digestive fire and reaches the alimentary canal and ultimately disturbs the blood. The blood which is in the colour of Kākananti (abrus precatorious seed) passes out blank or mixed with faecal matter with or without smell. This type of diarrhoea is difficult for management. The commentator explains that this is difficult to cure because without alleviating the grief, it cannot be managed with drugs alone.

sanskrit_text: अज्ञाजीर्णात् प्रदूता क्षोभयन्तः कोष्ठं दोषा धातुसंघान्मलांश्च । नानावर्णं नैकशः सारयन्ति शूलोपेतं षडमेनं वदन्ति ॥११॥
transliteration: Ajñājīrṇāt pradūtā kṣobhayantaḥ koṣṭhaṃ doṣā dhātusaṃghānm lāṃśca | Nānāvarṇaṃ naikaśaḥ sārayanti śūlopetaṃ ṣaḍamenaṃ vadanti ||11||
commentary: Disturbed by the indigested food, the Dosas move faster irritating the alimentary canal, Dhātus and Malas and cause multicoloured-repeated defaecation with pain which is called Āmātisāra, the sixth variety. The commentator explains that in this type of diarrhoea, the undigested food is the causative factor, and Pradrutāh means running in different directions.

topic_heading: Characteristics of Ama and Pakva Stool
sanskrit_text: संसृष्टं विष्टभ्य दोषैस्तु न्यस्तमप्स्ववसीदति । पुरीषं भृशदुर्गन्धि पिच्छलं चामसंज्ञितम् ॥१२॥ एतान्येव तु लिङ्गानि विपरीतानि यस्य वै । लाघवं च विशेषेण तस्य पक्वं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥१३॥
transliteration: Saṃsṛṣṭaṃ viṣṭabhya doṣaistu nyastamap svavasīdati | Purīṣaṃ bhṛśadurgandhi picchalaṃ cāmasaṃjñitam ||12|| Etānyeva tu liṅgāni viparītāni yasya vai | Lāghavaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa tasya pakvaṃ vinirdiśet ||13||
commentary: The faecal matter, when it is afflicted by Dosas sinks in water, has very bad odour and sticky in consistency and is known as Ama-undigested or incompletely formed. The one without Dosa-affliction has opposite qualities to the above and it has lightness in particular. This is to be considered as digested or formed stool. The commentator explains that sinking in water in unformed stool is due to heaviness of Ama, and the sticky nature is also due to Ama.

sanskrit_text: पक्वजाम्बवसंकाशं यकृत्खण्डनिभं घृतादिवेशवारमांसधावनतोयाभम् । कृष्णं च मेचकं च कर्बुरं चन्द्रकोपगतं घनं कुणपं मस्तुलुङ्गाभं कुशितं च ॥१४-१६॥ तृष्णा दाहस्तमः प्रवेशः श्वासो हिक्का पार्श्वास्थिरुक् मूर्च्छा संमोहः प्रलापः पाकश्च गुदे ॥१७-१८॥ असंवृतगुदं क्षीणं दुराध्मातमुपद्रुतम् । गतेष्माणमतिसारिणं विशेषेण विवर्जयेत् ॥१९॥
transliteration: Pakvajāmbavasaṃkāśaṃ yakṛtkhaṇḍanibhaṃ ghṛtādeśavāramāṃsadhāvanatoyābham | Kṛṣṇaṃ ca mecakaṃ ca karburaṃ candrakopagataṃ ghanaṃ kuṇapaṃ mastuluṅgābhaṃ kuśitaṃ ca ||14-16|| Tṛṣṇā dāhastamaḥ praveśaḥ śvāso hikkā pārśvāsthiruk mūrcchā saṃmohaḥ pralāpaḥ pākaśca gude ||17-18|| Asaṃvṛtagudaṃ kṣīṇaṃ durādh mātamupadrutam | Gateṣmāṇam atisāriṇaṃ viśeṣeṇa vivarjayet ||19||
commentary: If the stool looks like ripened fruit of Jambu, a piece of liver, thin in consistency like ghee, oil, fat, bone-marrow, meat-preparation, milk, curds, meat washed water, black, reddish, collyrium, greasy, multi-coloured, with lusture, very thick, has an odour of a dead-body, looks like the brain contents, has good odour and putrified and if the patient suffers with thirst, burning sensation, feeling of darkness, dyspnoea, hiccup, pain in the flanks and bones, syncope, restlessness, delusion, ulceration in the anus and delirium, the physician should leave away such an individual. If the elasticity of anus is lost, the individual becomes emaciated, suffers from severe flatulence, anus becomes ulcerated and the body temperature goes down, such patient of diarrhoea should not be taken for treatment. The commentator explains that these are the signs of incurability in diarrhoea.

sanskrit_text: पित्तकृन्ति यदाऽत्यर्थं द्रव्याण्यश्नाति पैतिके । तदोपजायतेऽ भीक्ष्णं रक्तातीसार उल्बणः ॥२०॥
transliteration: Pittakṛnti yadā'tyarthaṃ dravyāṇyaśnāti paitike | Tadopajāyate' bhīkṣṇaṃ raktātīsāra ulbaṇaḥ ||20||
commentary: If a patient suffering from Pitta type of Atisāra indulges in foods and habits affluently that increase Pitta, he will be afflicted by severe diarrhoea of blood. The commentator explains that this is not a separate type but a severe condition of Pitta type of diarrhoea.

sanskrit_text: वातात्प्रवाहिका सरुजा पित्तात्सदाहा कफात्सकफा । रक्तात्सरक्ता च ॥२१॥
transliteration: Vātātpravāhikā sarujā pittātsadāhā kaphātsakaphā | Raktātsaraktā ca ||21||
commentary: Vāta type of Pravāhikā is characterised by painful defaecation. Burning sensation is perceived in Pitta type and more of Kapha is seen in Kapha type of Pravāhikā. In Śoṇita (Rakta) variety, blood is passed along with defaecation. The commentator explains that Kapha type of Pravāhikā is attributed to oily type of aetiological factors while Vāta type to dry ones.

sanskrit_text: स्निग्धैर्निमित्तैः कफजा रूक्षैर्वातजा । पित्तरक्तजा तूष्णतीक्ष्णैः ॥२२॥
transliteration: Snigdhairnimittaiḥ kaphajā rūkṣairvātajā | Pittaraktajā tūṣṇatīkṣṇaiḥ ||22||
commentary: Kapha type of Pravāhikā is attributed to the oily type of aetiological factors while Vata type to dry ones. Pitta and Rakta types are caused by fast and warm factors. The commentator explains that when Pravāhikā itself is caused by Vata, the doshic varieties are classified based on predominance.

sanskrit_text: मूत्रं च वायुं च गुदेन मुञ्चतो यस्य न मुञ्चति । स सम्यग्विपच्यते चाग्निर्लघुता च भवत्युदरामये ॥२३॥
transliteration: Mūtraṃ ca vāyuṃ ca gudena muñcato yasya na muñcati | Sa samyagvipacyate cāgnirlaghutā ca bhavatyudarāmaye ||23||
commentary: If one does not defecate while passing urine and fart, his digestive fire is kindled properly and feels lightness in the alimentary canal, it should be understood that his abdominal disease (diarrhoea, in this context) is alleviated. The commentator explains that cure of diarrhoea does not imply constipation which is caused by obstruction of Vāta or abdominal bloating.

topic_heading: Aetiology, Pathogenesis and Common Symptomatology of Sprue
sanskrit_text: दोषा मूर्च्छिता ग्रहणीं प्रदूष्य भुक्तमाहारमामं पक्वं वा सरुजं पूतिमुञ्चन्ति । वातेन विबद्धं पित्तेन विरिक्तम् ॥१-३॥
transliteration: Doṣā mūrcchitā grahaṇīṃ pradūṣya bhuk tamāhāramāmaṃ pakvaṃ vā sarujaṃ pūtimuñcanti | Vātena vibaddhaṃ pittena viriktam ||1-3||
commentary: The vitiated Dosas afflict the Grahaṇī (duodenum) and cause it to expel the ingested food either undigested or digested with pain and bad odour. When Vāta is predominant the stool is hard in consistency, while it is loose in case of Pitta predominance. Grahani is the seat of digestive fire, situated above the umbilicus, between the Pakvāśaya (intestines) and Āmāśaya (stomach). The commentator explains that Grahani is called so as it takes or receives food.

sanskrit_text: पूर्वरूपं तु तस्येदं तृष्णाऽऽलस्यं बलक्षयः । विदाहोऽन्नस्य पाकश्च चिरात् कायस्य गौरवम् ॥४॥
transliteration: Pūrvarūpaṃ tu tasyedaṃ tṛṣṇā''lasyaṃ balakṣayaḥ | Vidāho'nnasya pākaśca cirāt kāyasya gauravam ||4||
commentary: Thirst, lassitude, weakness, improper digestion, delay in digestion and heaviness of the body are the premonitory symptoms of this disease. The commentator explains that weak digestive fire results in improper and delayed digestion, and heaviness in the body is due to Āma.

sanskrit_text: कटुतिक्तकषायातिरूक्षसंदुष्टभोजनैः । प्रमिताशनानशनात्यध्ववेगनिग्रहमैथुनैः ॥५-६॥ वातः प्रकुप्याग्निमुपहत्य रोगं करोति । स दुःखेन पचत्यन्नं विदह्यमानम् । स्तब्धगात्रः शुष्कास्यकण्ठोऽरुचितृड्णामः कर्णनादः पार्श्वोरुवङ्क्षणग्रीवारुक् । सरुग्विण्मूत्रता हृद्रुक् क्षयो दौर्बल्यमरुचिः । गुदे छेदो रसानामभिलाषः । चित्तसाद आध्मानं पाकान्ते च सुखम् । वातगुल्महृद्रोगप्लीहसंशयः । कासश्वासयुक्तः । शब्दवत् फेनिलं द्रवं रूक्षमल्पमलं मुहुर्मुञ्चति ॥७-१०॥
transliteration: Kaṭutiktakaṣāyātirūkṣasaṃduṣṭabhojanaiḥ | Pramitāśanānaśanā tyadhvaveganigrahamaithunaiḥ ||5-6|| Vātaḥ prakupyāgnimupahatya rogaṃ karoti | Sa duḥkhena pacatyannaṃ vidahyamānam | Stabdhagātraḥ śuṣkāsyakaṇṭho'rucitṛḍṇāmaḥ karṇanādaḥ pārśvoruvaṅkṣaṇagrīvāruk | Sarugviṇmūtratā hṛduk kṣayo daurbalyamaruciḥ | Gude chedo rasānāmabhilāṣaḥ | Cittasāda ādh mānaṃ pākānte ca sukham | Vātagulmahṛdrog aplīhasaṃśayaḥ | Kāsaśvāsayuktaḥ | Śabdavat phenilaṃ dravaṃ rūkṣamalpamalaṃ muhurmuñcati ||7-10||
commentary: By indulging in consumption of pungent, bitter, astringent, over dried and vitiated foods, limited food, skipping meal, walking more distances, over suppression of natural urges and participating in repeated coitus, Vāta is vitiated and encroaches the digestive fire to cause diseases. That individual will be able to digest the food with difficulty. The digestion gets sour. He will have rigid body, dryness in the mouth and throat, loss of appetite, thirst, darkness, sounds in the ears, severe pain in the flanks, thighs, groins, neck, painful defaecation, pain in the heart, emaciation, weakness, distaste, cutting pain in the anus, desire to take foods of all tastes, depression of the mind, flatulence during and after digestion and feeling of well being immediately after eating. He is doubted for suffering from Vāta gulma, Hrdroga and Plīhā. He will be suffering from cough and dyspnoea. He has painful noisy, froathy, liquid and dry thin and unformed defaecation repeatedly. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Vata type of Grahaniroga.

sanskrit_text: कट्वजीर्णविदाह्यम्लक्षाराद्यैः पित्तमुल्बणम् । आप्लावयद्धन्त्यनलं जलं तप्तमिवानलम् ॥११॥ सोऽजीर्णं नीलपीताभं पीताभः सायं द्रवम् । पूत्यम्लोद्गारहृत्कण्ठदाहारुचितृड्दितः ॥१२॥
transliteration: Kaṭvajīrṇavidāhyamlakṣārādyaiḥ pittamulbaṇam | Āplāvayaddhant yanalaṃ jalaṃ taptamivānalam ||11|| So'jīrṇaṃ nīlapītābhaṃ pītābhaḥ sāyaṃ dravam | Pūtyamlodgārahṛtkaṇṭhadāhārucitṛḍditaḥ ||12||
commentary: On consuming pungent, over-burnt, sour and alkali foods, the Pitta becomes more in quantity and over powers the digestive fire by making it more wet as the hot water also extinguishes the fire. The individual becomes yellowish in colour and defaecates undigested (unformed) bluish yellow and liquid faecal matter. He has stinking sour belchings, burning sensation in heart and throat, distaste and thirst. The commentator explains that Vidāhi means those which cause over burning, and Kṣāra is alkali prepared with Apāmārga and Yavakṣāra.

sanskrit_text: गुर्वतिस्निग्धशीतादिभोजनादतिभोजनात् । भुक्तमात्रस्य च स्वपाद्धन्त्यग्निं कुपितः कफः ॥१३॥ तस्यान्नं पच्यते दुःखं हल्लासच्छर्दिरोचकाः । आस्योपदेहमाधुर्यं कासच्छीवनपीनसाः ॥१४॥ हृदयं मन्यते स्त्यानमुदरं स्तिमितं गुरु । दुष्टो मधुर उद्गारः सदनं स्त्रीच्छहर्षणम् ॥१५॥ भिन्नामश्लेष्मसंसृष्टगुरुवर्चःप्रवर्तनम् । अरुचेरपि दौर्बल्यमालस्यं च कफात्मके ॥१६॥
transliteration: Gurvatisnigdhaśītādibhojanādatibhojanāt | Bhukta mātrasya ca svapāddhantyagniṃ kupitaḥ kaphaḥ ||13|| Tasyānnaṃ pacyate duḥkhaṃ hallāsaśchardirocakāḥ | Āsyopadehamādhuryaṃ kāsaśchīvanapīnasāḥ ||14|| Hṛdayaṃ manyate styānam udaraṃ stimitaṃ guru | Duṣṭo madhura udgāraḥ sadanaṃ strīcchaharṣaṇam ||15|| Bhinnāmāśleṣmasaṃsṛṣṭaguruvarcaḥpravartanam | Arucerapi daurbalyamālasyaṃ ca kaphātmake ||16||
commentary: Kapha which is increased by heavy, very oily and very cold foods, over-eating and sleeping immediately after eating, destroys the digestive fire. That individual's diet is digested with difficulty; he has nausea, vomiting, distaste, sticky sensation and sweetness in the mouth, cough, salivation, corryza, gripping sensation in the heart, heaviness and stability in the abdomen, sweet and stinking belchings, loss of appetite, no desire for the company of women, defaecation of broken, accompanied by phlegm and heavy in nature, weakness without emaciation and lassitude. The commentator explains that sleep here means day-sleep, which increases Kapha and destroys digestive fire.

sanskrit_text: पृथग्वातादिनिर्दिष्टहेतुलिङ्गसमागमे । त्रिदोषं निर्दिशेदेवं तेषां वक्ष्यामि भेषजम् ॥१७॥
transliteration: Pṛthagvātādinirdiṣṭahetuliṅgasamāgame | Tridoṣaṃ nirdiśedevaṃ teṣāṃ vakṣyāmi bheṣajam ||17||
commentary: If the aetiology and symptomatology given to the Vāta etc. Doṣas are seen together, that condition is called Tridoṣaja (of combination of all the Doṣas). The commentator explains that when Grahaṇī is vitiated, the Vahni (digestive fire) which is seated in that organ is also vitiated. That is why dysfunction of digestive fire is also labelled as disease of the duodenum.

sanskrit_text: दोषं सामं निरामं च विद्यादत्रातिसारवत् ॥१८॥ लिङ्गैरसाध्यो ग्रहणीविकारो यैस्तैरतीसारगदो न सिध्येत् । वृद्धस्य नूनं ग्रहणीविकारो हत्वा तनुं नैव निवर्तते च ॥१९॥
transliteration: Doṣaṃ sāmaṃ nirāmaṃ ca vidyādatrātisāravat ||18|| Liṅgairasādhyo grahaṇīvikāro yaistairatīsāragado na sidhyet | Vṛddhasya nūnaṃ grahaṇīvikāro hatvā tanuṃ naiva nivartate ca ||19||
commentary: The digested and undigested conditions in this disease are to be known as in diarrhoea. The incurability of Grahaṇīroga is also same as Atīsāra. If an old person is afflicted by Grahaṇīroga, it will not leave even after killing him. The commentator explains that the Sāma and Nirāma stages of the Dosas mentioned in Atīsāra is applicable in Grahaṇīroga also.

sanskrit_text: पृथग्दोषैः समस्तैश्च शोणितात् सहजानि च । अर्शांसि षट्प्रकाराणि विद्याद् गुदवलित्रये ॥१॥
transliteration: Pṛthagdoṣaiḥ samastaiśca śoṇitāt sahajāni ca | Arśāṃsi ṣaṭprakārāṇi vidyād gudavalitraye ||1||
commentary: Arśas (piles) which occur in the three rings of the anus, are of six types: one due to each of the three Dosas, one due to all of them, one due to blood and one due to Sahaja (congenital affliction). The commentator explains that Arśa is so named because it tortures the individuals like the enemy does. Sahaja are that type of piles which are existing by birth due to genital affliction that affects the anus during formulation of zygote itself.

sanskrit_text: दोषास्त्वग्मांसमेदांसि संदूष्य विविधाकृतीन् । मांसाङ्कुरानपानादौ कुर्वन्त्यर्शांसि तान्गुणाः ॥२॥
transliteration: Doṣāstv agmāṃsamedāṃsi saṃdūṣya vividhākṛtīn | Māṃsāṅkurānapānādau kurvantyarśāṃsi tānguṇāḥ ||2||
commentary: Vāta etc. Dosas aggravate and vitiate the skin, muscle and fat in the body and cause muscular sprouts of various shapes in the anus etc., known as Arśāṇsi (piles). The commentator explains that Rakta (blood) is also included along with skin and muscle as the vitiated factors. Apāna is anus. By adding Ādi, the extra growth of muscle occurring in nose etc. are also to be taken.

topic_heading: Aetiology of Vāta Type of Piles
sanskrit_text: कषायकटुतिक्तानि रूक्षशीतलघूनि च । प्रमिताल्पाशनं तीक्ष्णं मद्यं मैथुनसेवनम् ॥३॥ लङ्घनं देशकालौ च शीतौ व्यायामकर्म च । शोको वातातपस्पर्शो हेतुर्वातार्शसां मतः ॥४॥
transliteration: Kaṣāyakaṭutiktāni rūkṣaśītalaghūni ca | Pramitālpāśanaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ madyaṃ maithunasevanam ||3|| Laṅghanaṃ deśakālau ca śītau vyāyāmakarma ca | Śoko vātātapasparśo heturvātārśasāṃ mataḥ ||4||
commentary: Foods of astringent, pungent and bitter taste, dry, cold and light in quality, very low quantity, strong alcohols, coitus, skipping food, cold places and cold seasons, strenuous exercises, grief and exposure to wind and heat are the causative factors for Vāta type of Arśas (piles). The commentator explains that Pramitam means very low quantity of food.

topic_heading: Aetiology of Pitta Type of Piles
sanskrit_text: कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णक्षारतीक्ष्णविदाहिभिः । आमपक्वान्नपानैश्च कोपं याति पितं ततः ॥५॥ मद्यैर्मूत्रैश्च सुराभिश्च कोपं याति पितं ततः । कोपयत्याशु रक्तं च ततः कुर्यादर्शांसि च ॥६॥
transliteration: Kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇakṣāratīkṣṇavidāhibhiḥ | Āmapakvān napānaiśca kopaṃ yāti pitaṃ tataḥ ||5|| Madyairmūtraiśca surābhiśca kopaṃ yāti pitaṃ tataḥ | Kopayatyāśu raktaṃ ca tataḥ kuryādarśāṃsi ca ||6||
commentary: Pungent, sour, salty, very hot, alkali, fast, burning foods, both raw and cooked foods and drinks cause Pitta aggravation. Alcohol, urine and fermented drinks also aggravate Pitta, which in turn vitiates blood and causes piles. The commentator explains that these are the causative factors for Pitta type of piles.

topic_heading: Aetiology of Śleṣma Type of Piles
sanskrit_text: मधुरस्निग्धशीतानि गुरूण्यामलकानि च । दिवास्वप्नं शय्यासनसुखैरतिः प्रायशः ॥७॥ पुरोवातोऽचिन्तनं च श्लेष्मार्शसां हेतवः ॥८॥
transliteration: Madhurasnigdhaśītāni gurūṇyāmalakāni ca | Divāsvapnaṃ śayyāsanasukhairatiḥ prāyaśaḥ ||7|| Purovāto'cintanaṃ ca śleṣmārśasāṃ hetavaḥ ||8||
commentary: Sweet, oily, cold and heavy foods, excessive indulgence in comfortable beds and seats, day-sleep, exposure to easterly winds and lack of mental engagement are the causative factors of Śleṣma (Kapha) type of piles. The commentator explains that these factors increase Kapha and cause piles.

sanskrit_text: हेतुलक्षणसंसर्गाद्विद्याद् द्वन्द्वोल्बणानि च । सर्वो हेतुस्त्रिदोषाणां सहजैर्लक्षणं समम् ॥९॥
transliteration: Hetulakṣaṇasaṃsargādvidyād dvandvolbaṇāni ca | Sarvo hetustridoṣāṇāṃ sahajairlakṣaṇaṃ samam ||9||
commentary: If the aetiology and symptomatology of any two of the three Dosas is seen combined, it is to be understood as Dvandva (dual Dosa) affliction. If all the aetiological factors of all of the three Dosas lead to this disease, it is called Tridosa Arśa. The symptomatology of this condition is equal to that of Sahajārśas (congenital piles). The commentator explains that Sahaja type of piles have features like being awkward, rough, pale reddish, and the patient is emaciated with weak voice.

topic_heading: Symptomatology of Vāta Type of Piles
sanskrit_text: वातोल्बणान्यरूक्षाणि विवर्णान्यल्पपिच्छिलानि । परुषाणि विषमाणि कुण्ठानि विवृताग्राणि । बिम्बीखर्जूरबदरकार्पासकदम्बसर्षपाकाराणि । शिरःपार्श्वांसकटीजंघावङ्क्षणरुक् । क्षवथूद्गारविबन्धहृद्ग्रहारोचकाः । शर्करावत् सशब्दं सफेनं सकफं मुञ्चति । गुल्मप्लीहाश्ठीलाश्च भवन्ति । त्वङ्गनखविण्मूत्रनेत्रवक्त्राणि कृष्णानि भवन्ति ॥१०-१५॥
transliteration: Vātolbaṇānyarūkṣāṇi vivarṇānyalpapicchilāni | Paruṣāṇi viṣamāṇi kuṇṭhāni vivṛtāgrāṇi | Bimbīkhārjūrabadarakārpāsakadambasarṣapākārāṇi | Śiraḥpārśvāṃsakaṭījaṅghāvaṅkṣaṇaruk | Kṣavathūdgāravibandhahṛdgrahārocakāḥ | Śarkarāvat saśabdaṃ saphenaṃ sakaphaṃ muñcati | Gulmaplīhāśṭhīlāśca bhavanti | Tvaṅganakhaviṇmūtranetravaktrāṇi kṛṣṇāni bhavanti ||10-15||
commentary: The piles caused by aggravated Vāta are dry, with pinning sensation, thin in consistency, blackish red in colour, rigid, have no exudation, harsh, coarse, irregular in shape and size, bent, poignant and cracked at end. They look like fruits of bimbi, dates, zyziphus, cotton, kadamba and some are small like mustard seeds. The patient suffers from severe pain in head, flanks, scapula, low-back, thighs and groins. He also has sneezing, belching, constipation, gripping pain in the heart and anorexia. He defaecates stone-like stool with sounds, pain, froath and mucous. The patient also has gulma, splenomegaly and asthila. His skin, nails, faeces, urine, eyes and face turn to black colour. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Vata type of piles.

topic_heading: Symptomatology of Pitta Type of Piles
sanskrit_text: पित्तोल्बणानि नीलानि तनून्यसृक्स्रावीणि विस्राणि । तनवो मृदवः श्लथाः पित्तदाहमूर्च्छातृड्भ्रमप्रलापैः सह । हरितपीतहारिद्रवर्णानि त्वङ्गनखादीनि भवन्ति ॥१६-१८॥
transliteration: Pittolbaṇāni nīlāni tanūnyasṛksrāvīṇi visrāṇi | Tanavo mṛdavaḥ ślathāḥ pittadāhamūrcchātṛḍbhramapralāpaiḥ saha | Haritapītahāridravarṇāni tvaṅganakhādīni bhavanti ||16-18||
commentary: Piles caused by Pitta are bluish, thin, with liquid, bluish, yellowish, bloody and unformed stool. They are small, soft and hanging. The patient has burning sensation, syncope, thirst, giddiness and delirium. His skin, nails, faeces, urine, eyes and face become green, yellow or turmeric-like in colour. The commentator explains that burning sensation to delusion are considered as complications.

topic_heading: Symptomatology of Śleṣma Type of Piles
sanskrit_text: श्लेष्मोल्बणा महामूला घना मन्दरजः सिताः । उत्सन्नोपचितस्निग्धस्तब्धवृत्तगुरुस्थिराः ॥१९॥ पिच्छिलाः स्तिमिताः श्लक्ष्णाः कण्ड्वाढ्याः स्पर्शनप्रियाः । करीरपनसास्थ्याभाः गोस्तनसन्निभाः ॥२०॥ वङ्क्षणानाहिनः पायुर्वस्तिनाभिविकर्षिणः । सश्वासकासहल्लासप्रसेकारुचिपीनसाः ॥२१॥ मेहकृच्छ्रशिरोजाड्यशिशिरज्वरकारिणः । क्लैब्याग्निमान्द्यच्छर्दिरामप्रायविकारदाः ॥२२॥ वसाभकफप्रायपुरीषाः सप्रवाहिकाः । न स्रवन्ति न भिद्यन्ते पाण्डुस्निग्धत्वगादयः ॥२३॥
transliteration: Śleṣmolbaṇā mahāmūlā ghanā mandarajaḥ sitāḥ | Utsannopacitasnigdha stabdhavṛttagurusthirāḥ ||19|| Picchilāḥ stimitāḥ ślakṣṇāḥ kaṇḍvāḍhyāḥ sparśanapriyāḥ | Karīrapanasāsthyābhāḥ gostanasannibhāḥ ||20|| Vaṅkṣaṇānāhinaḥ pāyurvastinābhivikarṣiṇaḥ | Saśvāsakāsahallāsaprasekārucipīnasāḥ ||21|| Mehakṛcchraśirojāḍyaśiśirajvarakāriṇaḥ | Klaibyāgnimāndyachardirāmaprāyavikāradāḥ ||22|| Vasābhakaphaprāyapurīṣāḥ sapravāhikāḥ | Na sravanti na bhidyante pāṇḍusnigdhatvagādayaḥ ||23||
commentary: The piles caused by Śleṣmā are deep rooted, thick, white in colour raising high, bulky, oily, straight, round in shape, heavy, static, slow, smooth, having more pruritus, the individual feels happy by touching them, look like the seeds of Karīra, Panasa and udder of a cow. They cause swelling in the groin, pulling sensation in the anus, bladder and navel. The individual will have dyspnoea, cough, nausea, salivation, distaste, corryza, excessive urination, difficult urination, headache, cold-fever, impotency, weak digestive fire and other diseases of Āma origin. He defaecates fat-like faeces along with mucous with effort. The piles have no exudation nor they break open. The patient has pale and oily skin. The commentator explains that heaviness is caused to the patient by the existence of these piles.

sanskrit_text: रक्तोल्बणा यदा कीलाः पित्ताकृतिसमन्विताः । वटाङ्कुरगुञ्जाविद्रुमसन्निभाः ॥२४॥ गाढविट्पीडिता दुष्टमुष्णं रक्तं स्रवन्ति । अतिप्रवृत्त्या तस्य भेकाभः पुरुषः ॥२५॥ दुःखैः शोणितक्षयसम्भवैः । बलोत्साहौजांसि हतानि कलुषेन्द्रियश्च ॥२६॥
transliteration: Raktolbaṇā yadā kīlāḥ pittākṛtisamanvitāḥ | Vaṭāṅkuraguñjāvidrumasannibhāḥ ||24|| Gāḍhaviṭpīḍitā duṣṭamuṣṇaṃ raktaṃ sravanti | Atipravṛttyā tasya bhekābhaḥ puruṣaḥ ||25|| Duḥkhaiḥ śoṇitakṣayasaṃbhavaiḥ | Balotsāhaujāṃsi hatāni kaluṣendriyaśca ||26||
commentary: The piles arising due to aggravation of Rakta (blood) are similar to those of Pitta origin. They look like tender twigs of banyan tree, Guñja and Vidruma. They exudate vitiated and warm blood on being pressurised by hard stool. Due to excessive loss of blood, the individual becomes like a frog and suffers from diseases caused due to diminished blood. His lusture, strength and aptitude, his Ojus are lost and his organs become turbid. The commentator explains that Bhekābha means looks yellow like a frog in the rainy season.

topic_heading: Association of Vāta and Kapha in Bleeding Piles
sanskrit_text: विट् श्यावं कठिनं रूक्षमधोवायुर्न वर्तते । तनु चारुणवर्णं च फेनिलं चासृगर्शसाम् ॥२७॥ कट्यूरुगुदशूलं च दौर्बल्यं यदि चाधिकम् । तत्रानुबन्धो वातस्य हेतुर्यदि च रूक्षणम् ॥२८॥ शिशिरं श्वेतपीतं च विट् स्निग्धं गुरु शीतलम् । यद्यर्शसां घनं चासृक् तनुमत् पाण्डु पिच्छलम् ॥२९॥ गुदं सपिच्छं स्तिमितं गुरु स्निग्धं च कारणम् । श्लेष्मानुबन्धो विज्ञेयस्तत्र रक्तार्शसां बुधैः ॥३०॥
transliteration: Viṭ śyāvaṃ kaṭhinaṃ rūkṣamadhovāyurna vartate | Tanu cāruṇavarṇaṃ ca phenilaṃ cāsṛgarśasām ||27|| Kaṭyūrugudaśūlaṃ ca daurbalyaṃ yadi cādhikam | Tatrānubandho vātasya heturyadi ca rūkṣaṇam ||28|| Śiśiraṃ śvetapītaṃ ca viṭ snigdhaṃ guru śītalam | Yadyarśasāṃ ghanaṃ cāsṛk tanumat pāṇḍu picchalam ||29|| Gudaṃ sapicchaṃ stimitaṃ guru snigdhaṃ ca kāraṇam | Śleṣmānubandho vijñeyastatra raktārśasāṃ budhaiḥ ||30||
commentary: There are two types of Raktārśas (bleeding piles). One, associated with Śleṣma (Kapha) and the other, with Māruta (Vāta). The faeces is blackish dry and hard. The fart is not passed freely. The blood coming out of piles is thin reddish in colour and froathy. There is pain in the low-back, thighs and anus and extreme weakness due to association of Vāta and also due to dry aetiological factors. The piles are loose and faeces is whitish yellow in colour, oily, heavy and cold. The blood is thick, thready, pale and sticky. And the anus is sticky and stable, when Kapha is associated with Raktārśas when heavy and oily aetiological factors are involved. The commentator explains that Pittānubandha is not mentioned here because the qualities of Rakta and Pitta are almost equal.

sanskrit_text: विष्टम्भोऽस्य दौर्बल्यं कुक्षेराटोप एव च । कासोऽतिभूतार्बाहुल्यं सविश्वसादोऽल्पविट्कता ॥३१॥ ग्रहणीदोषपाण्डुत्वे शङ्का चोदरस्य च । पूर्वरूपाणि निर्दिष्टान्यर्शसामभिवृद्धये ॥३२॥
transliteration: Viṣṭambho'sya daurbalyaṃ kukṣerāṭopa eva ca | Kāso'tibhūtārbāhulyaṃ saviśvasādo'lpaviṭkatā ||31|| Grahaṇīdoṣapāṇḍutve śaṅkā codarasya ca | Pūrvarūpāṇi nirdiṣṭānyarśasāmabhivṛddhaye ||32||
commentary: Indigestion, weakness, sounds in the abdomen, emaciation, over belching, pain in the calf-muscles, less amount of faeces in defaecation and doubt of sprue, anaemia and abdominal disorders are the premonitory symptoms of Arśas (piles). The commentator explains that Viṣṭambha is due to disturbed Vāta, and Atopa is bubbling sounds. Over belchings are due to restriction of downward movement of Vata.

topic_heading: Role of Piles in Troubling the Whole Body
sanskrit_text: अर्शांसि बहुव्याधिकराणि कृच्छ्राणि च । तस्मादर्शसि चिकित्स्या बुद्ध्या प्रयत्नतः ॥३३-३४॥
transliteration: Arśāṃsi bahuvyādhikarāṇi kṛcchrāṇi ca | Tasmādarśasi cikitsyā buddhyā prayatnataḥ ||33-34||
commentary: The five varieties of each of the three Dosas and three of the anal rings are all vitiated when piles are originated. That is why piles are considered to be tough, causing many other diseases and probably they are difficult to cure. The commentator explains that the various complications caused by piles are Agnimāndya etc., and the word 'Prāya' indicates their difficulty in cure and sometimes easy curability.

sanskrit_text: बाह्यायां तु वलौ जातान्येकदोषोत्स्वणानि च । अर्शांसि सुखसाध्यानि न चिरोत्पिततानि च ॥३५॥ द्वन्द्वजानि द्वितीयायां वलौ यान्याश्रितानि च । कृच्छ्रसाध्यानि तान्याहुः परिसंवत्सराणि च ॥३६॥ सहजानि त्रिदोषाणि यानि चाभ्यन्तरां वलिम् । जायन्तेऽर्शांसि संश्रित्य तान्यसाध्यानि निर्दिशेत् ॥३७॥
transliteration: Bāhyāyāṃ tu valau jātānyekadoṣotsvaṇāni ca | Arśāṃsi sukhasādhyāni na cirotpit atāni ca ||35|| Dvandvajāni dvitīyāyāṃ valau yānyāśritāni ca | Kṛcchrasādhyāni tānyāhuḥ parisaṃvatsarāṇi ca ||36|| Sahajāni tridoṣāṇi yāni cābhyantarāṃ valim | Jāyante'rśāṃsi saṃśritya tānyasādhyāni nirdiśet ||37||
commentary: Piles originating in the external ring of the anus, having single Dosa-predominance and having short duration are easily curable. Piles having dual Dosa involvement, originating from the second ring and those having more than one year of duration are difficult for cure. Congenital piles, those with involvement of Tridosa-vitiation and those seated in the internal ring of the anus are to be labelled as Asādhyā (incurable). The commentator explains that incurable may become maintainable if the individual has longevity and active digestive fire, otherwise it becomes highly incurable.

sanskrit_text: याप्यत्वमसाध्यस्यापि स्यादायुर्बलाग्निबलात् । अन्यथा प्रत्याख्येयः ॥३८॥
transliteration: Yāpyatvamasādhyasyāpi syādāyurbalāgnibalāt | Anyathā pratyākhyeyaḥ ||38||
commentary: The incurable may become maintainable (prolongable) if the individual has longevity, manages the problem with prominent quadraped of the treatment aspect (physician, drug, nurse and money) and his digestive fire is active, otherwise it becomes highly incurable. The commentator explains that incurable is of two types: Yāpya (that can be prolonged) and Pratyākhyeya (highly incurable).

sanskrit_text: हस्तपादमुखनाभिगुदमेढ्रशोथः । हृन्नाभिपार्श्वरुक् चासाध्यत्वम् ॥३९॥ हृन्नाभिपार्श्वरुक् संमोहश्छर्दिः सर्वाङ्गरुक् ज्वरस्तृष्णा गुदपाकश्च ॥४०॥ तृष्णारोचकतीव्रवेदनातिसारशोथैर्युक्तं हन्ति ॥४१॥
transliteration: Hastapādamukhanābhigudameḍhraśothaḥ | Hṛnnābhipārśvaruk cāsādhyatvam ||39|| Hṛnnābhipārśvaruk saṃmohaśchardīḥ sarvāṅgaruk jvarastṛṣṇā gudapākaśca ||40|| Tṛṣṇārocakatīvravedanātisāraśothairyuktaṃ hanti ||41||
commentary: Swelling in the hands, legs, face, navel, anus and in the testes and pain in the heart and flanks are indicative of incurability of a patient of piles. Pain in the heart and flanks, delusion, vomiting, pain all over the body, fever, thirst and ulcerating in the anus kill the piles-patient. If the piles are associated with thirst, distaste, severe pain, over bleeding, oedema and diarrhoea, they will kill the patient. The commentator explains that these are the complications that lead to death.

sanskrit_text: मेढ्यादिव्यपि वक्ष्यन्ते यथास्वं, नाभिजानि च । गण्डूपदास्यरूपाणि पिच्छिलानि मृदूनि च ॥४२॥
transliteration: Meḍhyādivyapi vakṣyante yathāsvaṃ, nābhijāni ca | Gaṇḍūpadāsy arūpāṇi picchilāni mṛdūni ca ||42||
commentary: The Arśa (muscular sprouts) occurring on penis, nose, eye and the ear will be explained along with other diseases of these organs. The ones originating in the navel look like the face of Gandūpada Kṛmi, sticky and soft. The commentator explains that these are the muscular sprouts occurring in places other than the anus.

sanskrit_text: व्यानो गृहीत्वा श्लेष्माणं करोत्यर्शस्त्वचो बहिः । कीलोपमं स्थिरखरं चर्मकीलं तु तद्विदुः ॥४३॥ वातेन तोदपारुध्यं पित्तादिसतवर्किता । श्लेष्मणा स्निग्धता चास्य ग्रथितत्वं सवर्णता ॥४४॥
transliteration: Vyāno gṛhītvā śleṣmāṇaṃ karotyarśastvaco bahiḥ | Kīlopamaṃ sthirakharaṃ carmakīlaṃ tu tadviduḥ ||43|| Vātena todapārudhyaṃ pittādisatavarkitā | Śleṣmaṇā snigdhatā cāsya grathitatvaṃ savarṇatā ||44||
commentary: The Vyāna variety of Vāta takes along with it, the Śleṣmā and causes nail shaped stable and coarse sprouts on the skin which are known as Carmakīla (warts). In Carmakīla, there will be pinning sensation and hardness when Vāta is predominant, blackishness in Pitta predominance, oiliness, solidity and equal colour with skin in warts when Śleṣmā is dominating. The commentator explains that Savarnatā is the same colour as the skin.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: मन्दस्तीक्ष्णो विषमः समश्चेति चतुर्विधः । कफपित्तानिलाधिक्यात्साम्याज्जाठरोऽनलः ॥१॥
transliteration: Mandastīkṣṇo viṣamaḥ samaśceti caturvidhaḥ | Kaphapittānilādhikyātsāmyājjāṭharo'nalaḥ ||1||
commentary: The Jatharagni (digestive fire) is of four types: Manda (mild), due to predominance of Kapha; Tīkṣṇa (fast), due to Pitta; Viṣama (irregular), due to Vata aggravation; and Sama (balanced), due to equilibrium in the Tridosa. The commentator explains that as Mandagni cannot be managed easily, it is enumerated first. The word Jathara is used here to rule out fire of Dhatus and Bhutas.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
topic_heading: Diseases Caused by Different Agni Types
sanskrit_text: विषमो वातजानुरोगांस्तीक्ष्णः पित्तनिमित्तजान् । करोत्यग्निस्तथा मन्दो विकारान्कफसम्भवान् ॥२॥ समाग्निरमिताशितमात्रासम्यगिव पच्यते । स्वल्पाऽपि नैव मन्दाग्निना विषमाग्निना तु देहिनः ॥३॥ कदाचित्पच्यते सम्यक् कदाचिन्न विपच्यते । मात्राऽतिमात्राऽप्यशितं सुखं यस्य विपच्यते । तीक्ष्णाग्निरिति तं विद्यात्, समाग्निस्तु श्रेष्ठ उच्यते ॥४॥
transliteration: Viṣamo vātajānurogāṃstīkṣṇaḥ pittanimittajān | Karotyagnistathā mando vikārānkaphasambhavān ||2|| Samāgnir amitāśitamātrā samyagiva pacyate | Svalpā'pi naiva mandāgninā viṣamāgninā tu dehinā ||3|| Kadācit pacyate samyak kadācinna vipacyate | Mātrātimātrā'py aśitaṃ sukhaṃ yasya vipacyate | Tīkṣṇāgniriti taṃ vidyāt, samāgnistu śreṣṭha ucyate ||4||
commentary: The Viṣama type of digestive fire causes Vata diseases, Tīkṣṇa causes Pitta diseases, and Manda causes Kapha diseases. The Sama Agni digests food consumed in limited quantity. Mandagni cannot digest even smaller quantity of food. The irregular type sometimes digests properly and sometimes does not. The digestive fire that digests food in whatever quantity is Tīkṣṇa. Sama is the best. The commentator explains that Viṣama Agni causes some of the eighty Vata diseases, Tīkṣṇa causes some of the forty Pitta diseases, and Manda causes some of the twenty Kapha diseases.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: आमं विदग्धं विष्टब्धं कफपित्तानिलैस्त्रिभिः । अजीर्णं केचिदिच्छन्ति चतुर्थं रसशेषतः ॥५॥ अजीर्णं पञ्चमं केचिद्दिनपाकि च वदन्ति । षड्जमाजीर्णं प्राकृतं प्रतिवासरम् ॥६॥
transliteration: Āmaṃ vidagdhaṃ viṣṭabdhaṃ kaphapittānilaistribhiḥ | Ajīrṇaṃ kecidicchanti caturthaṃ rasaśeṣataḥ ||5|| Ajīrṇaṃ pañcamaṃ keciddinapāki ca vadanti | Ṣaḍjamājīrṇaṃ prākṛtaṃ prativāsaram ||6||
commentary: Due to aggravated Kapha, Pitta and Vāta, respectively, Āma (indigestion due to undigested food), Vidagdha (indigestion due to over secretion of Pitta) and Viṣṭabdha (indigestion due to constipation) types of Ajīrṇa (indigestion) takes place. Some scholars add the fourth one: Rasaseśājīrṇa (indigestion causing incomplete formation of chyle). The fifth one is Dinapākī (indigestion in which food takes next day for complete digestion) which is not harmful. The sixth one is Prativāśara (that affects everybody, everyday) which is natural and not troublesome. The commentator explains that Rasaseśājīrṇa is caused by reminiscence of food in the chyle.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: अत्यम्बुपानाद्विषमाशनाच्च वेगानां सन्धारणाद्विपरीतशय्यासनात् । ईर्ष्याभयक्रोधपरिप्लुतेन न जीर्यत्यन्नं लघु चापि केषांचित् ॥७-८॥ अतिचिन्ताशोकभयक्रोधायासातिनिद्राजागरणैश्च । लघ्वपि चान्नं न जीर्यति केषांचित् ॥९॥
transliteration: Atyambupānādviṣamāśanācca vegānāṃ sandhāraṇādviparītaśayyāsanāt | Īrṣyābhayakrodhapariplu tena na jīryat yannaṃ laghu cāpi keṣāṃcit ||7-8|| Aticintāśokabhayakrodhāyāsātinidrājāgaraṇaiśca | Laghvapi cānnaṃ na jīryati keṣāṃcit ||9||
commentary: Food will not be digested properly due to excessive drinking of water, irregular eating, suppression of natural urges, reversal sleeping habits, envy, fear, anger, greed, pain, agony and hatred. Even if the food is consumed in limited quantity and in consumable form, it will not be digested due to over thinking, grief, anger, fear, agony, over sleep and awakening during nights. The commentator explains that the word 'Api' implies that foods of oily and warm nature along with lightness for digestion also fail to be digested due to psychological disturbances.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: तत्रामे गुरुतोत्क्लेदः शोथो गण्डाक्षिकूटगः । उद्गारश्च यथाभुक्तमविदग्धः प्रवर्तते ॥१०॥ विदग्धे भ्रमतृण्मूर्च्छाः पित्ताच्च विविधा रुजः । उद्गारश्च सधूमाम्लः स्वेदो दाहश्च जायते ॥११॥ विष्टब्धे शूलमाध्मानं विविधा वातवेदनाः । मलवाताप्रवृत्तिश्च स्तम्भो मोहोऽङ्गपीडनम् ॥१२॥
