transliteration: Tatrāme gurutotkle daḥ śotho gaṇḍākṣikūṭagaḥ | Udgāraśca yathābhuktamavidagdhaḥ pravartate ||10|| Vidagdhe bhramatṛṇmūrcchāḥ pittācca vividhā rujaḥ | Udgāraśca sadhūmāmlaḥ svedo dāhaśca jāyate ||11|| Viṣṭabdhe śūlamādh mānaṃ vividhā vātavedanāḥ | Malavātāpravṛttiśca stambho moho'ṅgapīḍanam ||12||
commentary: In Āmājīrṇa (indigestion due to Kapha): heaviness, nausea, oedema in the cheeks and around the eye-ball, and eructations as per the ingested food without sourness. In Vidagdhañjīrṇa (indigestion due to Pitta): giddiness, thirst, syncope, various Pitta troubles, eructations with smoke and sour liquid, sweating and burning sensation. In Viṣṭabdhañjīrṇa (indigestion due to Vāta): pain, flatulence, various Vāta diseases, constipation and blockage of fart, rigidity, delusion and pain in the body. The commentator explains that swelling in cheeks and around the eye ball is the special effect of this disease.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: मूर्च्छा प्रलापो वमथुः प्रसेकः सदनं भ्रमः । उपद्रवा भवन्त्येते मरणं चाप्यजीर्णतः ॥१३॥
transliteration: Mūrcchā pralāpo vamathuḥ prasekaḥ sadanaṃ bhramaḥ | Upadravā bhavantye te maraṇaṃ cāpyajīrṇataḥ ||13||
commentary: Syncope, delirium, vomiting, dribbling of saliva, depression and giddiness are the complications of indigestion. Death may also occur due to this disease. The commentator explains that death occurs due to heavy or chronic indigestion.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: अनात्मवन्तः पशुवद्भुञ्जते येऽप्रमाणतः । रोगानीकस्य ते मूलमजीर्णं प्राप्नुवन्ति हि ॥१४॥
transliteration: Anātmavantaḥ paśuvad bhuñjate ye'pramāṇataḥ | Rogānīkasya te mūlam ajīrṇaṃ prāpnuvanti hi ||14||
commentary: Those who eat like animals in high doses without considering their own capacity, get indigestion which is the root-cause of innumerable diseases. The commentator explains that Anātmavanta are those who have indecent mind and due to greed are desirous of temporary satisfaction.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
topic_heading: Origination of Visūcī, Alasaka and Vilambikā
sanskrit_text: अजीर्णादामविष्टब्धं विदग्धं च यदीरितम् । विसूच्यलसकौ तस्माद्भवेच्चापि विलम्बिका ॥१५॥
transliteration: Ajīrṇādāmaviṣṭabdhaṃ vidagdhaṃ ca yadīritam | Visūcy alasakau tasmādbhaveccāpi vilambikā ||15||
commentary: From the three types of indigestions i.e. Āma, Vidagdha and Viṣṭabdha, Visūcī, Alasaka and Vilambikā are originated. The commentator explains that Visūcī is originated from Āmājīrṇa, Alasaka from Viṣṭabdha, and Vilambikā from Vidagdha.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: सूचीभिरिव गात्राणि तुदन् संतिष्ठतेऽनिलः । यत्राजीर्णेन सा वैद्यैर्विसूचीति निगद्यते ॥१६॥ न तां परिमिताहारा लभन्ते विदितागमाः । मूढास्तामजितात्मानो लभन्तेऽशनलोलुपाः ॥१७॥
transliteration: Sūcībhiriva gātrāṇi tudan saṃtiṣṭhate'nilaḥ | Yatrājīrṇena sā vaidyairvisūcīti nigadyate ||16|| Na tāṃ parimitāhārā labhante viditāgamāḥ | Mūḍhāstāmajitātmāno labhante'śanalolupāḥ ||17||
commentary: The condition caused by indigestion in which Vāta creates pricking pain all over the body is known as Visūcī. Those who take limited food due to their knowledge of Ayurveda will not be afflicted by this disease. The innocent who have no control on themselves with their greed for food, suffer from this ailment. The commentator explains that the name Visūcī comes from the comparison of the pain to pricking by needles.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: मूर्च्छाऽतिसारो वमथुः पिपासा शूलो भ्रमोद्वेष्टनजृम्भदाहाः । वैवर्ण्यकम्पौ हृदये रुजश्च भवन्ति तस्यां शिरसश्च भेदः ॥१८॥
transliteration: Mūrcchā'tisāro vamathuḥ pipāsā śūlo bhramodveṣṭanajṛmbhadāhāḥ | Vaivarṇyakampau hṛdaye rujaśca bhavanti tasyāṃ śirasaśca bhedaḥ ||18||
commentary: Visūcī is characterised by syncope, diarrhoea, vomiting, thirst, pain (in the abdomen), giddiness, squeezing pain in the hands and legs, yawning, burning sensation, discolouration, trembling, pain in the heart and pain in the head. The commentator explains that both vomiting and diarrhoea are present in this disease.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: कुक्षिरानह्यतोऽत्यर्थं प्रताम्येत् परिकूजति । निरुद्धो मारुतश्चैव कुक्षावुपरि धावति ॥१९॥ वातवर्चोनिरोधश्च यस्यात्यर्थं भवेदपि । तस्यालसकमाचष्टे तृष्णोद्गारौ च यस्य तु ॥२०॥
transliteration: Kukṣirānahyato'tyarthaṃ pratāmyet parikūjati | Niruddho mārutaścaiva kukṣāvupari dhāvati ||19|| Vātavarchonirodhaśca yasyātyarthaṃ bhavedapi | Tasyālasakamācaṣṭe tṛṣṇodgārau ca yasya tu ||20||
commentary: The patient has severe bloating of the stomach, syncope, groaning; Vāta which is obstructed moves above the stomach causing obstruction of fart and faeces, thirst and eructations are the signs and symptoms of Alasaka (lethargy of food). The commentator explains that Alasaka is so named because of the non-movement of Dosas. The food is settled in the stomach without going upward or downwards and does not get digested.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
sanskrit_text: दुष्टं तु भुक्तं कफमारुताभ्यां प्रवर्तते नोर्ध्वमधश्च यस्य । विलम्बिकां तां भृशदुश्चिकित्स्यामाचक्षते शास्त्रविदः पुराणाः ॥२१॥
transliteration: Duṣṭaṃ tu bhuktaṃ kaphamārutābhyāṃ pravartate nordhvamadhaśca yasya | Vilambikāṃ tāṃ bhṛśaduścikitsyāmācakṣate śāstravidaḥ purāṇāḥ ||21||
commentary: The ingested food, when vitiated by Kapha and Vāta does not either move upwards or downwards. Such condition is called Vilambikā which is very tough for management according to learned people. The commentator explains that the difference between Alasaka and Vilambikā is that pain etc. are severe in Alasaka while it is not so severe in Vilambikā.

chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
topic_heading: Role of Āma in Causing Diseases
sanskrit_text: यत्र यत्र स्थितं चामं तत्र तत्र भवन्ति रोगाः । आममेव हि सर्वेषां रोगाणां मूलमुच्यते ॥२२॥
transliteration: Yatra yatra sthitaṃ cāmaṃ tatra tatra bhavanti rogāḥ | Āmameva hi sarveṣāṃ rogāṇāṃ mūlamucyate ||22||
commentary: In whichever part of the body, the Āma gets lodged, it will cause diseases of the Dūṣya that originally exists in that place along with the qualities of Āma. The commentator explains that this verse describes the role of Ama in causing various diseases.

sanskrit_text: क्रिमयश्च द्विधा प्रोक्ता बाह्याभ्यन्तरभेदतः । बहिर्मलकफासृग्विड्जन्मभेदाच्चतुर्विधाः ॥१॥ नामतो विंशतिविधाः । बाह्यास्तत्र मलोच्छवाः ॥
transliteration: Krimayaśca dvidhā proktā bāhyābhyantarabhedataḥ | Bahirmalakaphāsṛgviḍjanmabhedāccaturvidhāḥ ||1|| Nāmato viṃśatividhāḥ | Bāhyāstatra malocchavāḥ ||
commentary: Krimis (worms) are of two varieties: Bāhya (external) and Ābhyantara (internal). They are again classified into four types as per origin: born out of external impurities, Kapha, Rakta (blood) and faecal matter. These worms are twenty in number. The external ones are born out of impurities. The commentator explains that the external worms are born out of impurities that get deposited on the skin (sweat etc.), and internal ones are born in the Āmāsāya (stomach) etc.

sanskrit_text: तिलप्रमाणसंस्थानवर्णाः केशाच्चराश्रयाः । बहुपादाश्च सूक्ष्माश्च यूका लिक्षाश्च नामतः ॥२-३॥ द्विधा ते कोठपिडकाकण्डूगण्डान् प्रकुर्वन्ति ॥
transliteration: Tilapramāṇasaṃsthānavarṇāḥ keśāccarāśrayāḥ | Bahupādāśca sūkṣmāśca yūkā likṣāśca nāmataḥ ||2-3|| Dvidhā te koṭhapiḍakākaṇḍūgaṇḍān prakurvanti ||
commentary: The external worms are of sesame seed in size, shape and colour which dwell on hair and garments. They have many legs and are very small in size. Yūka and Likṣā are the two names respectively given to them (lice). They cause urticarial patches, pustules on the skin, pruritus (itching sensation) and tumours on the skin. The commentator explains that these are the external worms that cause skin problems.

sanskrit_text: मधुरस्निग्धशीतगुरुभोजनात् । कफः प्रकुप्यति क्रिमीन् जनयति ॥४॥
transliteration: Madhurasnigdhaśītagurubhojanāt | Kaphaḥ prakupyati krimīn janayati ||4||
commentary: By consuming sweet, oily, cold and heavy foods, Kapha gets aggravated and causes worm-infestation. The commentator explains that the aetiology of worm-infestation is based on the origin of worms.

sanskrit_text: कफजा आमाशयस्थाः । द्विविधास्ते स्थूलाः सूक्ष्माश्च । तत्र स्थूलाः । कच्छपादयो दश । सूक्ष्माः षट् । नामतस्ते । कच्छपः ककण्डकः सूर्यः सोमः किर्मिरः क्रकर इति पञ्च । सूक्ष्माः । कुण्डलिनी वालिनी ज्वरवाहिनी बाह्यान्त्रिका नानान्त्रिका कृमिः । एते कफजाः षोडश । तेषां लक्षणम् । कच्छपः कफमेदोवाहिनी कृन्तनादीनि करोति । ककण्डकः कफकण्डूकरः । सूर्यः सोमः किर्मिरः क्रकरश्च । एते कफजाः ॥५-१०॥
transliteration: Kaphajā āmāśayasthāḥ | Dvidhāste sthūlāḥ sūkṣmāśca | Tatra sthūlāḥ | Kacchapādayo daśa | Sūkṣmāḥ ṣaṭ | Nāmata ste | Kacchapaḥ kakaṇḍakaḥ sūryaḥ somaḥ kirmiraḥ krakara iti pañca | Sūkṣmāḥ | Kuṇḍalinī vālinī jvaravāhinī bāhyāntrikā nānāntrikā kṛmiḥ | Ete kaphajāḥ ṣoḍaśa | Teṣāṃ lakṣaṇam | Kacchapaḥ kaphamedovāhinī kṛntanādīni karoti | Kakaṇḍakaḥ kaphakaṇḍūkaraḥ | Sūryaḥ somaḥ kirmiraḥ krakaraśca | Ete kaphajāḥ ||5-10||
commentary: The worms of Kapha origin are seated in the Amāsaya. They are of two types: gross and subtle. The gross ones are ten, and the subtle ones are six. The gross worms are named Kacchapa, Kakaṇḍaka, Sūrya, Soma, Kirmira, Krakara etc. The subtle ones are Kuṇḍalinī, Vālinī, Jvaravāhinī, Bāhyāntrikā, Nānāntrikā, Kṛmi. These sixteen worms are of Kapha origin. Their features: Kacchapa carries Kapha and Medas and causes cutting sensation. Kakaṇḍaka causes itching due to Kapha. The commentator explains that these worms cause various symptoms based on their nature and location.

sanskrit_text: रक्तवाहिसरास्थानरक्तजा जन्तवोऽणवः । अपादा वृत्तताम्राश्च सौक्ष्म्यात् केचिददर्शनाः ॥११॥ केशादा रोमविध्वंसा रोमद्वीपा उदुम्बराः । षट् ते कुष्ठैककर्माणः सहसौरसमातरः ॥१२॥
transliteration: Raktavāhisarāsthānaraktajā jantavo'ṇavaḥ | Apādā vṛttatāmrāśca saukṣmyāt kecidadarśanāḥ ||11|| Keśādā romavidhvaṃsā romadvīpā udumbarāḥ | Ṣaṭ te kuṣṭhaikakarmāṇaḥ sahasaurasamātaraḥ ||12||
commentary: The worms originated from blood exist in sources of blood in the body. They are very small in size, without legs, round, coppery in colour and some of them are not perceivable to the naked eye. They are named as Keśāda, Romavidhvaṃsa, Romadvīpa, Udumbara, Saurasa and Mātṛ. These six cause only Kuṣṭha (leprosy, the dreaded skin disease). The commentator explains that all skin diseases are caused with the involvement of Vāta, Pitta, Śleṣma and Krimi.

sanskrit_text: पक्वाशये पुरीषोत्था जायन्तेऽधोविसर्पिणः । प्रवृद्धाः स्युर्भवेयुश्च ते यदाऽऽमाशयोन्मुखाः ॥१३॥ तदाऽऽस्योद्गारनिःश्वासा विड्गन्धानुविधायिनः । पृथुवृत्ततनुस्थूलाः श्यावपीतसितासिताः ॥१४॥ ते पञ्च नाम्ना कृमयः ककेश्कमकेश्काः । सौसुरादाः सशूलाख्या लेलिहा जनयन्ति हि ॥१५॥
transliteration: Pakvāśaye purīṣotthā jāyante'dhovisarpiṇaḥ | Pravṛddhāḥ syurbhaveyuśca te yadā''māśayonmukhāḥ ||13|| Tadā''syodgāraniḥśvāsā viḍgandhānuvidhāyinaḥ | Pṛthuvṛttatanusthūlāḥ śyāvapītasitāsitāḥ ||14|| Te pañca nāmnā kṛmayaḥ kakeśkamakeśkāḥ | Sausurādāḥ saśūlākhyā lelihā janayanti hi ||15||
commentary: The worms originated from faeces exist in the Pakvāśaya. They move downwards. When they become aggravated and move towards the Āmāśaya, the mouth, eructations and respiration get the smell of faeces. They are of various shapes: broad, round, thin, gross, blackish, yellow, white and black. The five named worms are Kakeśka, Makeśka, Sausurāda, Śūlākhyā and Lelihā. The commentator explains that these worms cause diseases like abdominal pain, distaste, etc.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: पाण्डुरोगाः स्मृताः पञ्च वातपित्तकफैक्ष्यः । चतुर्थः सन्निपातेन पञ्चमो भक्षणान्मृदः ॥१॥
transliteration: Pāṇḍurogāḥ smṛtāḥ pañca vātapittakaphaikṣyaḥ | Caturthaḥ sannipātena pañcamo bhakṣaṇānmṛdaḥ ||1||
commentary: Pāṇḍu (anaemia) is of five types: due to Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, the fourth due to Sannipāta (combined aggregation of all the three Dosas), and the fifth one due to eating soil. The commentator explains that the fifth type, caused by eating soil, is separately enumerated to specify the treatment aspect, though the soil eating in turn aggravates the Dosa itself.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: विपरीतगुणान्नान्नपानानि च विविधानि । वेगविधारणमतिव्यायामम् । विरुद्धाशनमजीर्णं च । क्षाराम्लकटुकातिसेवनम् । अत्युष्णशीतसेवनम् ॥२-३॥
transliteration: Viparītaguṇānnānn apānāni ca vividhāni | Vegavidhāraṇamativyāyāmam | Viruddhāśanamajīrṇaṃ ca | Kṣārāmlakaṭukātisevanam | Atyuṣṇaśītasevanam ||2-3||
commentary: The aetiology of Pāṇḍu includes: foods of opposite qualities, suppression of natural urges, excessive exercise, incompatible foods, indigestion, excessive consumption of alkali, sour and pungent foods, and excessive exposure to heat and cold. The commentator explains that these factors vitiate the Dosas and cause anaemia.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: पूर्वरूपं तु पाण्डोः । त्वचि सौषिर्यं कृष्णता च । मूत्रपुरीषे च पीतता । नखानां च शुक्लता । गात्राणां च गौरवम् । अरुचिर्वैवर्ण्यम् ॥४॥
transliteration: Pūrvarūpaṃ tu pāṇḍoḥ | Tvaci sauṣiryaṃ kṛṣṇatā ca | Mūtrapurīṣe ca pītatā | Nakhānāṃ ca śuklatā | Gātrāṇāṃ ca gauravam | Arucirvaivarṇyam ||4||
commentary: The premonitary symptoms of Pāṇḍu are: roughness of skin, blackish discolouration, yellowishness in urine and faeces, whitishness of nails, heaviness of the body, distaste and discolouration. The commentator explains that these are the early signs of anaemia.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: वातात् पाण्डुः कृष्णरूक्षः । पित्तात्पीतहरितः । कफात्शुक्लस्निग्धः । सन्निपातात्सर्वलिङ्गः । मृद्भक्षणात्पाण्डुरोगः कषायाम्लकटुसेवनात् ॥५-६॥
transliteration: Vātāt pāṇḍuḥ kṛṣṇarūkṣaḥ | Pittātpītaharitaḥ | Kaphātśuklasnigdhaḥ | Sannipātātsarvāliṅgaḥ | Mṛdbhakṣaṇātpāṇḍurogaḥ kaṣāyāmlakaṭusevanāt ||5-6||
commentary: Pāṇḍu caused by Vāta is blackish and dry. Caused by Pitta is yellowish-green. Caused by Kapha is whitish and oily. Caused by Sannipāta has all the above symptoms. The commentator explains that the symptoms of Pāṇḍu caused by eating soil are due to the specific taste of the soil consumed.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: मृत्तिकाभक्षणात्कषायरसा मृत्तिका वातं कोपयति । ऊषरा पित्तम् । मधुरा कफम् । तस्मात्कषायमृत्तिकाभक्षणाद्वातपित्तकोपः । ऊषरात्पित्तकफकोपः । मधुरात्कफवातकोपः । सन्निपातस्तु त्रिदोषजः ॥७-८॥
transliteration: Mṛttikābhakṣaṇātkaṣāyarasā mṛttikā vātaṃ kopayati | Ūṣarā pittam | Madhurā kapham | Tasmātkaṣāyamṛttikābhakṣaṇādvātapittakopaḥ | Ūṣarātpittakaphakopaḥ | Madhurātkaphavātakopaḥ | Sannipātastu tridoṣajaḥ ||7-8||
commentary: Eating soil: astringent taste soil aggravates Vāta, alkaline soil aggravates Pitta, and sweet soil aggravates Kapha. Thus, astringent soil causes Vata-Pitta aggravation; alkaline soil causes Pitta-Kapha aggravation; sweet soil causes Kapha-Vata aggravation. Sannipāta is caused by all three Dosas. The commentator explains that due to the dry nature of the soil, it will not be digested properly and diminishes the strength of the organs.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: मृत्तिका रूक्षत्वात्स्रोतांसि रुन्धति । बलवर्णं च हरति । तेजोवीर्यौजांसि च क्षिणोति । अग्निं च हन्ति ॥९-१०॥
transliteration: Mṛttikā rūkṣatvātsrotāṃsi rundhati | Balavarṇaṃ ca harati | Tejovīryaujāṃsi ca kṣiṇoti | Agniṃ ca hanti ||9-10||
commentary: Due to the dry nature of the soil, it fills in the channels and blocks them. It diminishes the strength, lusture, valour, potency and the essential vital substance (Ojus) of the body and immediately destroys the digestive fire. The commentator explains that Bala is the functioning capacity, Teja is lusture, and Virya is potency.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
topic_heading: Symptomatology of Pāṇḍu Caused by Eating Soil
sanskrit_text: शूनाक्षिकूटगण्डभ्रूलिङ्गनाभिमेढ्रः । क्रिमिकोष्ठता । रक्तकफयुक्तं विट् सकृत् । मुहुर्मुञ्चति ॥११॥
transliteration: Śūnākṣikūṭagaṇḍabhrūliṅganābhimedhraḥ | Krimikoṣṭhatā | Raktakaphayuktaṃ viṭ sakṛt | Muhurmuñcati ||11||
commentary: The individual suffering from Pāṇḍu caused by eating soil has swelling around the eye, cheeks, eye-brows, legs, navel and genital organ. There is worm infestation in the alimentary canal. He defecates blood and phlegm along with faecal matter repeatedly. The commentator explains that Krimikoṣṭhatā (worm infestation) is a general feature in all Pāṇḍu varieties.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: पाण्डुरोगश्चिरोत्पन्नः खरीभूतो न सिध्यति । कालप्रकर्षाच्छूनानां यो वा पीतानि पश्यति ॥१२॥ बद्धाल्पहरितं सकफं योऽतिसारयेत । दीनः श्वेतातिदग्धाङ्गच्छर्दिमूर्च्छातृड्दितः ॥१३॥ सनास्त्यसृग्विक्षयाद्यश्च पाण्डुः श्वेतत्वमाप्नुयात् । पाण्डुदन्तनखनेत्रो यस्तु पाण्डुनेत्रश्च यो भवेत् । पाण्डुसंघातदर्शी च पाण्डुरोगी विनश्यति ॥१४॥ अन्तेषु शूनं परिहीणमध्यं स्तानं तथाऽन्तेषु च मध्यशूनम् । गुदे च शिश्न्योश्च शूनं प्रताम्यन्तमसंज्ञकल्पम् । विवर्जयेत्पाण्डुकिनं यशोऽर्थं तथाऽतिसारज्वरपीडितं च ॥१५॥
transliteration: Pāṇḍurogaścirotpannaḥ kharībhūto na sidhyati | Kālaprakarṣācchūnānāṃ yo vā pītāni paśyati ||12|| Baddhālpaharitaṃ sakaphaṃ yo'tisārayet | Dīnaḥ śvetātidagdhāṅgacchardimūrcchātṛḍditaḥ ||13|| Sanāstyasṛgvikṣayādyāśca pāṇḍuḥ śvetatvamāpnuyāt | Pāṇḍudantanakhanetro yastu pāṇḍunetraśca yo bhavet | Pāṇḍusaṃghātadarśī ca pāṇḍurogī vinaśyati ||14|| Anteṣu śūnaṃ parihīṇamadhyaṃ sthānaṃ tathā'nteṣu ca madhyaśūnam | Gude ca śiśnyośca śūnaṃ pratāmyantama saṃjñakalpam | Vivarjayetpāṇḍukinaṃ yaśo'rthaṃ tathā'tisārajvarapīḍitaṃ ca ||15||
commentary: Chronic Pāṇḍu will not be cured. If oedema persists for a long time and the individual sees everything in yellow colour will also not be cured. The one who defaecates solid greenish faecal matter along with phlegm in smaller quantities will not survive. Who looks grief stricken, suffers from vomiting, syncope and thirst and whose body appears as if painted with white colour will also not survive. One who becomes white from pale due to loss of blood will also not survive. That individual suffering from Pāṇḍu will also not survive who has teeth, nails and eyes appearing in pale colour and who sees everything as if they are in pale colour. That individual suffering from Pāṇḍu should not be taken for treatment who has swelling in the extremities and emaciation of centre part of the body and vice-versa, and has swelling in the anus, penis and testes, who is very weak and looks like dead one. That Pāṇḍu patient also should be discarded who suffers from fever and diarrhoea. The commentator explains that these are the signs of incurability.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: पाण्डुरोगी तु योऽत्यर्थं पित्तलानि निषेवते । तस्य पित्तमसृङ्मांसं दग्ध्वा रोगाय कल्पते ॥१६॥ हारिद्रनेत्रः स भृशं हारिद्रत्वग्मुखाननः । रक्तपीतशकृन्मूत्रो भेकवर्णो हतेन्द्रियः ॥१७॥ अल्पाग्निरल्पभोक्ता च शीतवातातपप्रियः । पिपासारुचिहृल्लासतन्द्रादाहसमन्वितः ॥१८॥
transliteration: Pāṇḍurogī tu yo'tyarthaṃ pittalāni niṣevate | Tasya pittamasṛṅmāṃsaṃ dagdhvā rogāya kalpate ||16|| Hāridranetraḥ sa bhṛśaṃ hāridratvagmukhānanaḥ | Raktapītaśakṛnmūtro bhekavarṇo hatendriyaḥ ||17|| Alpāgnir alpabhoktā ca śītavātātapapriyaḥ | Pipāsārucihṛllāsatandrādāhasamanvitaḥ ||18||
commentary: If a Pāṇḍurogī (anaemic patient) excessively indulges in Pitta-increasing foods, his Pitta burns the blood and muscles causing jaundice. He has yellowish eyes, yellowish skin and face, reddish-yellow faeces and urine, looks like a frog, has weakened sense organs, weak digestive fire, eats little, likes cold, wind and sun, and suffers from thirst, distaste, nausea, drowsiness and burning sensation. The commentator explains that Kāmala is caused by the burning of blood and muscles by aggravated Pitta.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: हारिद्रश्यावविण्मूत्रः शोफी चेद्बधिरो भवेत् । रक्ताक्षमुखच्छर्दिविण्मूत्रो मुहुर्मुहः ॥१९॥ दाहारुचिपिपासाध्मानभ्रममोहारतिभिः । क्षीणेन्द्रियो विनश्यति ॥२०॥
transliteration: Hāridraśyāvaviṇmūtraḥ śophī cedbadhiro bhavet | Raktākṣamukhacchardiviṇmūtro muhurmuhuḥ ||19|| Dāhārucipipāsādhmānabhramamohāratibhiḥ | Kṣīṇendriyo vinaśyati ||20||
commentary: The jaundice-patient who develops black and yellow colour in faeces and urine and swelling all over the body; or red colour in the eyes, mouth, vomit, faeces and urine and faints frequently; and the one who suffers from burning sensation, distaste, thirst, bloating of the abdomen, dizziness, delusion, loss of appetite and loss of senses will die. The commentator explains that these are the signs of incurability.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: छर्द्यरुचिहृल्लासज्वरग्लानिश्वासकासातिसारैः । कुम्भकामला न सिध्यति ॥२१॥
transliteration: Chardyarucihṛllāsajvaraglāniśvāsakāsātisāraih | Kumbhakāmalā na sidhyati ||21||
commentary: If a patient of Kumbhakāmala has vomiting, distaste, nausea, fever, fatigue, dyspnoea, cough and diarrhoea, he will not survive. The commentator explains that Kumbhakāmala is an advanced stage of jaundice with severe complications.

chapter_title: Pāṇḍu, Kāmala, Kumbhakāmala and Halīmaka Nidānam
sanskrit_text: यदा पाण्डोर्हरितश्याववर्णस्य बलोत्साहक्षयः । तन्द्रालस्याल्पज्वरस्त्रीच्छाहर्षाभावः । अङ्गमर्दो दाहस्तृष्णारुचिभ्रमाः । स वातपित्तकोपजं हलीमकम् ॥२२-२३॥
transliteration: Yadā pāṇḍorharitaśyāvavarṇasya balotsāhakṣayaḥ | Tandrālas yālpajvarastrīcchāharṣābhāvaḥ | Aṅgamardo dāhastṛṣṇārucibhramāḥ | Sa vātapittakopajaṃ halīmakam ||22-23||
commentary: When the individual suffering from Pāṇḍu develops green or bluish-yellow colour, diminishing of strength and enthusiasm, suffers from drowsiness, loss of appetite, mild fever, lack of desire for women, pain all over the body, burning sensation, thirst, distaste and giddiness, he should be considered as suffering from Halīmaka which is caused by Vata-Pitta vitiation. The commentator explains that Halīmaka is the advanced stage of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit_text: घर्मव्यायामशोकाध्वव्यवायैरतिसेवितैः । तीक्ष्णोष्णाक्षारलवणैरम्लैः कटुभिरेव च ॥१॥ पित्तं विदग्धं स्वगुणैर्विदहत्याशु शोणितम् । ततः प्रवर्तते रक्तमूर्ध्वमधो द्विधाऽपि वा ॥२॥ ऊर्ध्वं नासाक्षिकर्णास्यैर्मेहनाद्गुदैरधः । कुपितं रोमकूपैश्च समस्तैस्तत्र वर्तते ॥३॥
transliteration: Gharmavyāyāmaśokādhvavyavāyairatisevitaiḥ | Tīkṣṇoṣṇākṣāralavaṇairamlaiḥ kaṭubhireva ca ||1|| Pittaṃ vidagdhaṃ svaguṇairvidahatyāśu śoṇitam | Tataḥ pravartate raktamūrdhvamadho dvidhā'pi vā ||2|| Ūrdhvaṃ nāsākṣikarṇāsyairmehanādgudairadhaḥ | Kupitaṃ romakūpaiśca samastaistatra vartate ||3||
commentary: Due to over exposure to sun, excercise, grief, walking and sexual intercourse, excessive intake of fast, warm, alkali, salty, sour and pungent foods, Pitta gets vitiated and in turn vitiates the blood immediately with its own qualities. Then there will be bleeding upwards, downwards or from both ways. Upward bleeding takes place through nostrils, eyes, ears and mouth; downward bleeding through penis/vagina and anus. When there is extreme aggravation, bleeding takes place through hair-roots all over the body. The commentator explains that Raktapitta is called so because both blood and pitta are involved.

sanskrit_text: पूर्वरूपं रक्तपित्तस्य । हृदये दाहः । मूत्रपुरीषे च पीतता । नेत्रे च रक्तता ॥४॥
transliteration: Pūrvarūpaṃ raktapittasya | Hṛdaye dāhaḥ | Mūtrapurīṣe ca pītatā | Netre ca raktatā ||4||
commentary: The premonitory symptoms of Raktapitta are: burning sensation in the heart, yellowishness in urine and faeces, and redness in the eyes. The commentator explains that these are the early signs of impending haemorrhagic disease.

sanskrit_text: रक्तपित्तं त्रिविधम् । वातात् पित्तात् कफात् । तत्र वातात् श्यावं फेनिलम् । पित्तात्पीतं हरितम् । कफात्पिच्छिलं शुक्लम् ॥५-६॥
transliteration: Raktapittaṃ trividham | Vātāt pittāt kaphāt | Tatra vātācchyāvaṃ phenilam | Pittātpītaṃ haritam | Kaphātpicchilaṃ śuklam ||5-6||
commentary: Raktapitta is of three types: due to Vāta, Pitta and Kapha. Vāta type is blackish and froathy. Pitta type is yellowish-green. Kapha type is sticky and whitish. The commentator explains that when pure Pitta causes Raktapitta without association of other Dosas, it is labelled as Pitta type.

sanskrit_text: ऊर्ध्वगं कफसंसृष्टमधोगं पवनानुगम् । द्विमार्गं कफवाताभ्यामुभाभ्यामनुवर्तते ॥७॥
transliteration: Ūrdhvagaṃ kaphasaṃsṛṣṭamadhogaṃ pavanānugam | Dvimārgaṃ kaphavātābhyāmubhābhyāmanuvartate ||7||
commentary: The Raktapitta when comes upwards (through vomiting etc.) is associated with Kapha, while there is Vāta association when it is manifested downwards (bleeding per rectum etc.). If it occurs in both directions, Kapha and Vāta both are associated. The commentator explains that this helps in planning the treatment direction.

sanskrit_text: एकमार्गं बलवतो नातिवेगं नवोत्थितम् । रक्तपित्तं सुखे काले साध्यं स्यान्निरुपद्रवम् ॥८॥ एकदोषानुगं साध्यं द्विदोषं याप्यमुच्यते । त्रिदोषमग्निसादेन क्षीणमांसबलं नवम् ॥९॥ अरोचकयुक्तं च याप्यं वा प्रत्याख्येयम् ॥१०॥
transliteration: Ekamārgaṃ balavato nātivegaṃ navotthitam | Raktapittaṃ sukhe kāle sādhyaṃ syānnirupadravam ||8|| Ekadoṣānugaṃ sādhyaṃ dvidoṣaṃ yāpyamucyate | Tridoṣamagnisādena kṣīṇamāṃsabalaṃ navam ||9|| Arocakayuktaṃ ca yāpyaṃ vā pratyākhyeyam ||10||
commentary: The Raktapitta which is manifested through one direction, afflicting an energetic individual, not so fast, with a short duration, occurring in convenient season and which has no complications is curable. Single Dosa involvement is curable. Dual Dosa affliction is prolongable. Tridosa involvement with lack of appetite, emaciated body, old age and inability to accept food is incurable. The commentator explains that one direction here is to be interpreted as upward direction only, as the downward is considered Yāpya.

sanskrit_text: दौर्बल्यं श्वासः कासो ज्वरश्छर्दिर्मदः पाण्डुता । दाहो मूर्च्छाविपाकौ हृदयातुल्या रुक् । तृष्णाऽतिसारः शिरस्तपनम् । पूतिवक्त्रता भक्तद्वेषाविपाकौ विकृतिरपि भवेद्रक्तपित्तोपसर्गाः ॥११॥
transliteration: Daurbalyaṃ śvāsaḥ kāso jvaraśchardirmadaḥ pāṇḍutā | Dāho mūrcchāvipākau hṛdayātulyāruk | Tṛṣṇā'tisāraḥ śirastapanam | Pūtivaktratā bhaktadvēṣāvipākau vikṛtira pi bhavedraktapittopasargāḥ ||11||
commentary: Weakness, dyspnoea, cough, fever, vomiting, feeling of intoxication, pale appearance, burning sensation, syncope, uneven digestion, irregular pain in the heart, thirst, diarrhoea, warmth in the head, spitting putrified liquids, disliking food, indigestion and improper colour are the complications of Raktapitta. The commentator explains that these complications make the disease difficult to manage.

sanskrit_text: मांसप्रक्षालनाभं कुथितमिव च यत्कर्दमाभं वा, मेदःपूयास्त्रकल्पं यकृदिव यदि वा पक्वजम्बूफलाभम् । यत्कृष्णं यच्च नीलं भृशमतिकुणपं यत्र चोक्ता विकारा- स्तद्वर्ज्यं रक्तपित्तं सुरपतिधनुषा यच्च तुल्यं विभाति ॥१२॥ येन चोपहतो रक्तं रक्तपितेन मानवः । पश्येद् दृश्यं विवच्चापि तच्चासाध्यमसंशयम् ॥१३॥ लोहितं छर्दयेद्यस्तु बहुशो लोहितेक्षणः । लोहितोद्गारदर्शी च प्रियते रक्तपैतिकः ॥१४॥
transliteration: Māṃsaprakṣālanābhaṃ kuthitamiva ca yatkardamābhaṃ vā, medaḥpūyāstrakalpaṃ yakṛdiva yadi vā pakvajambūphalābham | Yatkṛṣṇaṃ yacca nīlaṃ bhṛśamatikupaṇaṃ yatra coktā vikārā- stadvarjyaṃ raktapittaṃ surapatidhanuṣā yacca tulyaṃ vibhāti ||12|| Yena copahato raktaṃ raktapitena mānavaḥ | Paśyed dṛśyaṃ vivaccāpi taccāsādhyamasaṃśayam ||13|| Lohitaṃ chardayed yastu bahuśo lohitekṣaṇaḥ | Lohitodgāradarśī ca priyate raktapaitikaḥ ||14||
commentary: If the Raktapitta looks like meat-washed water, has putrified smell, looks like turbid water, mixed with fat and pus, in the colour of the liver or ripened Jambūphala, black in colour, blue, with dead smell, with complications and in the colour of a rainbow, such case should be avoided for treatment. If the patient sees everything blood-red in colour including the sky, it is undoubtedly incurable. If a patient vomits profuse blood, his eyes become red, has blood eructations and looks everything blood-red in colour, he will die. The commentator explains that these are the signs of incurability.

sanskrit_text: वेगरोधात् क्षयाच्चैव साहसाद्विषमाशनात् । त्रिदोषो जायते यक्ष्मा गदो हेतुचतुष्टयात् ॥१॥
transliteration: Vegarodhāt kṣayāccaiva sāhasādviṣamāśanāt | Tridoṣo jāyate yakṣmā gado hetucatuṣṭayāt ||1||
commentary: Suppression of natural urges, emaciation, over doing daring deeds and irregular eating habits are the four aetiological factors causing the disease of consumption in which Tridosas are involved. The commentator explains that the natural urges in this context are fart, urine and faeces, not all the urges mentioned elsewhere. This disease is called by various names like Śoṣa, Kṣaya and Rājayakṣma.

sanskrit_text: रसवाहिस्रोतोरोधात्कफप्रधानात् । अतिव्यवायाच्छुक्रक्षयात् । धातवः क्षीयन्ते ॥२॥
transliteration: Rasavāhisrotorodhātkaphapradhānāt | Ativyavāyācchukrakṣayāt | Dhātavaḥ kṣīyante ||2||
commentary: When the Rasa (chyle) channels are blocked by Dosas with Kapha in predominance, and also due to over indulgence in sexual act, when the semen is depleted in the body, the other Dhātus are diminished and ultimately an individual gets emaciated. The commentator explains that consumption occurs not only due to drying-up of the tissues but also due to blockage of the channels carrying the Rasa.

sanskrit_text: श्वासाङ्गमर्दः कफसंस्रवस्तालुशोषः । छर्दिरग्निसादो मदः पीनसः कासो निद्रा ॥३॥ शोषे भविष्यति भवन्ति । स चापि जन्तुः शुक्लेक्षणो भवति । मांसस्त्रीरिरंसुः । स्वप्नेषु काकशुकशल्लकिनीलकण्ठगृध्रकपिकृकलासकैः सह वाह्यते । नदीर्विजलाश्च पश्येत् । शुष्कान् तरुवनधूमदग्धान् ॥४॥
transliteration: Śvāsāṅgamardaḥ kaphasaṃsravastāluśoṣaḥ | Chardir agnisādo madaḥ pīnasaḥ kāso nidrā ||3|| Śoṣe bhaviṣyati bhavanti | Sa cāpi jantuḥ śuklekṣaṇo bhavati | Māṃsastrīriransuḥ | Svapneṣu kākaśukaśallakinīlakaṇṭhagṛdhrakapikṛkalāsakaiḥ saha vāhyate | Nadīrvijalāśca paśyet | Śuṣkān taruvanadhūmadagdhān ||4||
commentary: Dyspnoea, myalgia, dribbling phlegm, dryness in the palate, vomiting, loss of appetite, intoxication, corryza, cough, excessive sleep are premonitory symptoms of consumption. The individual has whiteness in the eyes and he desires more for eating meat and having the company of women. He dreams as if riding on crow, parrot, porcupine, peacock, vulture, monkey and lizard, and dreams of dry rivers and dry trees afflicted by wind, smoke and fire. The commentator explains that these dreams are considered as premonitory symptoms of consumption.

sanskrit_text: अंसपार्श्वरुक् दाहो ज्वरश्च शरीरस्य । कासः श्वासः स्वरभेदः पार्श्वशूलम् । भक्तद्वेषो ज्वरः श्वासः कासः शोणितदर्शनम् । स्वरभेदश्च षड्रूपाणि ॥५-७॥
transliteration: Aṃsapārśvaruk dāho jvaraśca śarīrasya | Kāsaḥ śvāsaḥ svarabhedaḥ pārśvaśūlam | Bhaktadveṣo jvaraḥ śvāsaḥ kāsaḥ śoṇitadarśanam | Svarabhedaśca ṣaḍrūpāṇi ||5-7||
commentary: Pain in the scapular region and flanks, burning sensation, fever that affects the complete body, cough, dyspnoea, hoarseness of voice, pain in the flanks, hatred toward food, fever, dyspnoea, cough, bleeding and hoarseness of voice are the eleven and six features of consumption. The commentator explains that the three symptoms in probability can be any three of these.

sanskrit_text: एकादशभिरेतैर्वा षड्भिर्वा पि समन्वितम् । कासातीसारपार्श्वार्तिस्वरभेदारुचिज्वरैः ॥८॥ त्रिभिर्वा पीडितं लिङ्गैः कासीश्वासासृगामयैः । जह्याच्छोषाभितं जन्तुमिच्छन् सुविमलं यशः ॥९॥ सर्वैरेतैस्त्रिभिर्वापि लिङ्गैर्मासबलक्षये । युक्तो वर्ज्यश्चिकित्स्यस्तु सर्वरूपोऽन्यथा भवेत् ॥१०॥ महाशनं क्षीयमाणमतिसारनिपीडितम् । शूनमुत्क्लेदनं चैव यक्ष्माणं परिवर्जयेत् ॥११॥ श्वासकासारुचिज्वरैश्च स युक्तो वर्ज्यः ॥१२॥
transliteration: Ekādaśabhiretairvā ṣaḍbhirvā pi samanvitam | Kāsātisārapārśvārtisvarabhedārucijvaraiḥ ||8|| Tribhirvā pīḍitaṃ liṅgaiḥ kāsīśvāsāsṛgāmayaiḥ | Jahyācchoṣābhitaṃ jantumicchan suvimalaṃ yaśaḥ ||9|| Sarvairetai tribhirvāpi liṅgairmāsabalakṣaye | Yukto varjyaścikitsyastu sarvarūpo'nyathā bhavet ||10|| Mahāśanaṃ kṣīyamāṇamatisāranipīḍitam | Śūnamutkledanaṃ caiva yakṣmāṇaṃ parivarjayet ||11|| Śvāsakāsārucijvaraiśca sa yukto varjyaḥ ||12||
commentary: The consumption patient with eleven, six or three of the features, when associated with cough, diarrhoea, pain in flanks, hoarseness, distaste and fever, or with cough, dyspnoea and bleeding, should be avoided if he is emaciated. Excessive eating by a emaciating person is a bad omen. Swelling of the testes is also considered as a complication. The commentator explains that the transformation from eleven to six features can always take place.

sanskrit_text: अज्वरो बलवान् स्थिरधातुः । श्रद्दधानोऽल्पक्षयः । साध्यो यक्ष्मा ॥१३॥
transliteration: Ajvaro balavān sthiradhātuḥ | Śraddadhāno'lpakṣayaḥ | Sādhyo yakṣmā ||13||
commentary: The consumption patient who has no continuous fever, has natural strength, can withstand the therapy, is very much in his senses, has good appetite and is not emaciated should be taken for treatment. The commentator explains that even if the individual is young, he should be told about the disease before treatment.

sanskrit_text: द्विविधः शोषः । अतिव्यवायशोकवृद्धव्यायामाध्वगमनजः । उरःक्षतजश्च ॥१४॥
transliteration: Dvidhaḥ śoṣaḥ | Ativyavāyaśokavṛddhavyāyāmādhvagamanajaḥ | Uraḥkṣatajaśca ||14||
commentary: There are two types of Śoṣa: one caused by over indulgence in sexual act, grief, senility, strenuous exercise and extensive travel by foot; and the other by trauma in the chest. The commentator explains that this is to rule out the opinion that Rājayakṣma is caused by only a few reasons.

sanskrit_text: अतिव्यवायात्क्षीणशुक्रस्य पाण्डुता । पूर्वधातुक्षयश्च ॥१५॥
transliteration: Ativyavāyātkṣīṇaśukrasya pāṇḍutā | Pūrvadhātukṣayaśca ||15||
commentary: The individual emaciated by over indulgence in sexual act is complicated by the symptoms of spending out of semen. He has pale body and his predecessor tissues (to semen: bone marrow, bone, fat, muscle, blood and chyle) are depleted. The commentator explains that the signs of depleted semen are pain in the penis and testes, inability in performing coitus, and delayed ejaculation.

topic_heading: Consumption due to Grief, Senility and Trauma
sanskrit_text: शोकः स्मृतिबुद्धिक्षयो मनसः । वृद्धत्वं जरया । व्यायामाध्वगमनजो विशेषैः । उरःक्षतजो रक्तश्लेष्मप्रवृत्त्या च ॥१६-१८॥
transliteration: Śokaḥ smṛtibuddhikṣayo manasaḥ | Vṛddhatvaṃ jarayā | Vyāyāmādhvagamanajo viśeṣaiḥ | Uraḥkṣatajo raktakaphapravṛttyā ca ||16-18||
commentary: Consumption caused by grief has over thinking and shrunken body. Senile consumption is due to old age. Consumption caused by strenuous exercise has severe symptoms. Consumption caused by chest trauma has bleeding and phlegm discharge. The commentator explains that the signs of consumption caused by trauma are similar to those mentioned by Caraka.

sanskrit_text: व्यायामशोषी भूयिष्ठमेभिरेव समन्वितः । लिङ्गैरःक्षतकृतेः संयुक्तश्च क्षतं विना ॥१९॥
transliteration: Vyāyāmaśoṣī bhūyiṣṭhamebhireva samanvitaḥ | Liṅgairaḥkṣatakṛteḥ saṃyuktaśca kṣataṃ vinā ||19||
commentary: The individual suffering from consumption caused by strenuous exercise suffers from the same symptomatology in severe manner along with those of Urahkṣata (trauma to the chest) without any trauma in the chest. The commentator explains that as walking has similarity with physical exercise, the symptoms are more severe.

topic_heading: Incurability of Consumption due to Wound
sanskrit_text: रक्तक्षयाद् वेदनाभिस्तथैवाहारयन्त्रणात् । व्रणितस्य भवेच्छोषः स चासाध्यतमो मतः ॥२०॥
transliteration: Raktakṣayād vedanābhistathaivāhārayantraṇāt | Vraṇitasya bhavecchoṣaḥ sa cāsādhyatamo mataḥ ||20||
commentary: Due to blood-loss, pains and restricted food, the wounded individual develops consumption which is highly incurable. The commentator explains that this condition is considered highly incurable due to the combination of factors.

sanskrit_text: धनुषः शिलानिघातात् पशूनां निघातात् । शकटव्यसनात् । अभिघातात् पातात् । महानदीतरणात् । अधीयानस्य । युद्धात् । एभिः कर्मभिः क्रूरैः क्षतजः शोषः । भिन्नस्वरो रक्तश्लेष्माणं वमेत् । क्षीयते च ॥२१-२८॥
transliteration: Dhanuṣaḥ śilānighātāt paśūnāṃ nighātāt | Śakaṭavyasanāt | Abhighātāt pātāt | Mahānadītaraṇāt | Adhīyānasya | Yuddhāt | Ebhiḥ karmabhiḥ krūraiḥ kṣatajaḥ śoṣaḥ | Bhinnasvaro raktakaphāṇaṃ vamet | Kṣīyate ca ||21-28||
commentary: The individual (with traumatic chest) gets emaciated due to trauma from bow, stone, beasts, chariot accidents, injury, fall, crossing rivers, studying, war and other cruel acts. He has hoarse voice, vomits blood and phlegm, and gets emaciated due to trauma and loss of semen and Ojas. The commentator explains that these are the causes of Kṣatakṣīna.

sanskrit_text: अव्यक्तं लक्षणं तस्य पूर्वरूपमिति स्मृतम् ॥२९॥
transliteration: Avyaktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tasya pūrvarūpamiti smṛtam ||29||
commentary: The symptoms, if they are incompletely manifested, it is considered as Pūrvarūpa (prodromata) of this (Urahkṣata) disease. The commentator explains that the prodromata are incomplete signs.

sanskrit_text: उरोरुक् शोणितच्छर्दिः कासो वैशेषिकः क्षते । क्षीणे सरक्तमूत्रत्वं पार्श्वपृष्ठकटीग्रहः ॥३०॥
transliteration: Uroruk śoṇitacchardīḥ kāso vaiśeṣikaḥ kṣate | Kṣīṇe saraktamūtratvaṃ pārśvapṛṣṭhakaṭīgrahaḥ ||30||
commentary: Pain in the chest, blood-vomiting and specific type of cough are the features of traumatic chest. In consumption, haematuria and gripping sensation in flanks, back and pelvic-region are present. The commentator explains that specific cough is that in which phlegm of putrified nature, black or yellow in colour and mixed with blood is expectorated.

sanskrit_text: अल्पलिङ्गस्य दीप्ताग्नेः साध्यो बलवतो नवः । परिसंवत्सरो याप्यः सर्वलिङ्गं तु वर्जयेत् ॥३१॥
transliteration: Alpaliṅgasya dīptāgneḥ sādhyo balavato navaḥ | Parisaṃvatsaro yāpyaḥ sarvaliṅgaṃ tu varjayet ||31||
commentary: This disease (Kṣatakṣīna) occurring with mild symptomatology to an individual who has active digestive fire and who is energetic and with a lesser duration is curable. The disease having crossed one year of duration is prolongable and that with complete symptomatology is to be discarded. The commentator explains that these are the prognostic criteria.

sanskrit_text: धूमाभिघाताद्विदग्धाद्रसात् । व्यायामाद्रूक्षाशनात् । विषमाशनात् । वेगरोधाच्छुक्रोद्गारक्षवथूनाम् । प्राणोऽनुसृत्योदानं कुपितो विवृतमुखान्निःसरति । स कास इत्युच्यते ॥१-२॥
transliteration: Dhūmābhighātād vidagdhādrasāt | Vyāyāmādrūkṣāśanāt | Viṣamāśanāt | Vegarodhācchukrodgārakṣavathūnām | Prāṇo'nusṛtyodānaṃ kupito vivṛtamukhānnissarati | Sa kāsa ityucyate ||1-2||
commentary: Due to invasion of smoke, vitiated Rasa (chyle), strenuous exercise, consuming dry foods, reversal movement of food, suppression of natural urges and also due to suppression of sneeze, the Prāṇavāyu gets mixed up with Udānavāyu, gets vitiated and comes out at a stretch from the mouth along with impurities making a noise that is similar to the sound made by the broken bronze vessel. This is called Kāsa (cough). The commentator explains that Kāsa means sudden movement.

sanskrit_text: पञ्च कासाः स्मृता वातपित्तश्लेष्मक्षतक्षयैः । क्षयायोपेक्षिताः सर्वे बलिनश्चोत्तरोत्तरम् ॥३॥
transliteration: Pañca kāsāḥ smṛtā vātapittaśleṣmakṣatakṣayaiḥ | Kṣayāyopekṣitāḥ sarve balinaścottarottaram ||3||
commentary: Five types of Kāsa are told: due to Vāta, Pitta, Śleṣma, Kṣata (trauma) and Kṣaya (consumption). All these, when neglected, lead to emaciation. These are powerful one after another. The commentator explains that Jarākāsa (cough due to old age) is included in the doshic affliction.

sanskrit_text: पूर्वरूपं भवेत्तेषां शूकपूर्णगलास्यता । कण्डूश्च भोज्यानामवरोधश्च जायते ॥४॥
transliteration: Pūrvarūpaṃ bhavetteṣāṃ śūkapūrṇagalāsyatā | Kaṇḍūśca bhojyānāmavarodhaśca jāyate ||4||
commentary: The premonitory symptoms are: feeling of full of thorns in the throat and mouth, itching sensation and obstruction of foods in the throat. The commentator explains that obstruction of foods is either due to distaste or inability in swallowing.

sanskrit_text: हृत्शङ्खमूर्धोदरपार्श्वशूली क्षामाननः क्षीणबलस्वरौजाः । प्रसक्तवेगस्तु समीरणेन भिन्नस्वरः कासति शुष्कमेव ॥५॥
transliteration: Hṛtśaṅkhamūrdhodarapārśvaśūlī kṣāmānanaḥ kṣīṇavalasvaraujāḥ | Prasaktavegastu samīraṇena bhinnasvaraḥ kāsati śuṣkameva ||5||
commentary: The individual suffering from Vāta type of cough has pain in the heart, temples, head, abdomen and flanks, he has weary face, weakened energy, voice and vital force, he has continuous bouts of cough with hoarse voice and his cough is always dry. The commentator explains that dry cough means having no phlegm or saliva.

sanskrit_text: उरोविदाहज्वरवक्रशोषैरभ्यर्दितः कटुमुखस्तृषातः । छर्दिति पीतं कटुकं च कासी पीतत्वगादिः पित्तकृतः ॥६॥
transliteration: Urovidāhajvaravakraśoṣairabhyarditaḥ kaṭumukhastṛṣātaḥ | Charditi pītaṃ kaṭukaṃ ca kāsī pītatvagādiḥ pittakṛtaḥ ||6||
commentary: Burning sensation in the chest, fever, dryness, bitter taste in the mouth, thirst, vomiting of yellowish and pungent contents, coughing, paleness and burning sensation all over the body are the features of Pitta type of cough. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Pitta type of cough.

sanskrit_text: आस्योपदेहं कफवृत्तिको हृदयं मन्यते भरितम् । शिरोरुग्गौरवारुच्यौ कासते कफं घनम् ॥७॥
transliteration: Āsyopadehaṃ kaphavṛttiko hṛdayaṃ manyate bharitam | Śirorug gauravarucyau kāsate kaphaṃ ghanam ||7||
commentary: In Kapha type of cough, the individual is depressed due to coating in the mouth. He has pain in the head, feels filling of the body with Kapha, distaste, heaviness in the body, itching sensation and repeated expectoration of thick phlegm. The commentator explains that these are the features of Kapha type of cough.

sanskrit_text: अतिव्यवायाद्भाराध्वयुद्धाश्वगजनिग्रहात् । शुष्कस्य कासस्तु क्षतजः । शुष्ककासस्ततः पश्चाद्रक्तं ष्ठीवति । कण्ठशूलस्तीव्रः । सूचीभिरिव भिद्यमानहृदयः । स्पर्शासहः । पार्श्वभेदश्च । सन्धिशब्दो ज्वरः श्वासस्तृष्णा स्वरभेदः । कपोत इव कूजति ॥८-११॥
transliteration: Ativyavāyādbhārādhvayuddhāśvagajanigrahāt | Śuṣkasya kāsastu kṣatajaḥ | Śuṣkakāsastataḥ paścādraktaṃ ṣṭhīvati | Kaṇṭhaśūlastīvraḥ | Sūcībhiriva bhidyamānahṛdayaḥ | Sparśāsahaḥ | Pārśvabhedaśca | Sandhiśabdo jvaraḥ śvāsastṛṣṇā svarabhedaḥ | Kapota iva kūjati ||8-11||
commentary: By over-indulgence in sexual act, lifting weights, walking to distant places, fighting and controlling horses and elephants, the dry individual's chest gets the injury. Vāyu that increases due to above deeds causes cough. He, first, has dry cough followed by expectoration of blood. There is severe pain in the throat and he feels as if chest is pierced with sharp needles and cannot withstand even touch as there is also breaking pain in the chest. He also suffers from breaking sounds in the joints, fever, dyspnoea, thirst and shrill voice. He makes sounds like that of a pigeon while coughing. The commentator explains that expectoration of blood is caused by the breaking of heart.

sanskrit_text: विषमासात्म्यभोज्यातिव्यवायाद्वेगनिग्रहात् । घृणिनां शोचतां नृणां व्यापन्नेऽग्नौ त्रयो मलाः । कुपिताः क्षयजं कासं कुर्युः क्षयप्रदम् ॥१२॥ सगात्रशूलं ज्वरदाहमोहान् प्राणक्षयं च कासी । शुष्यन् विनिष्ठीवति दुर्बलस्तु प्रक्षीणमांसो रुधिरं सपूयम् । तं सर्वलिङ्गभूयिष्ठं चिकित्सकाः क्षयजं वदन्ति ॥१३॥
transliteration: Viṣamāsātmyabhojyā tivyavāyādveganigrahāt | Ghṛṇināṃ śocatāṃ nṛṇāṃ vyāpanne'gnau trayo malāḥ | Kupitāḥ kṣayajaṃ kāsaṃ kuryuḥ kṣayapradam ||12|| Sagātraśūlaṃ jvaradāhamohān prāṇakṣayaṃ ca kāsī | Śuṣyan viniṣṭhīvati durbalastu prakṣīṇamāṃso rudhiraṃ sapūyam | Taṃ sarvaliṅgabhūyiṣṭhaṃ cikitsakāḥ kṣayajaṃ vadanti ||13||
commentary: The three Dosas are aggravated due to deterioration of digestive fire by irregular and incompatible foods, over indulgence in sex, suppression of natural urges, and also to those who suffer from hatred and grief. These Dosas cause Kṣayaja Kāsa which results in emaciation of body. The individual has cough, pain all over the body, fever, burning sensation, delusion and depletion of vitality. He loses the musculature of the body, gets dried up and has expectoration of blood with pus. If the individual has all the above symptomatology, the physicians declare the situation as unmanageable. The commentator explains that cough in consumption is due to Kapha while this is due to Tridoṣa.

sanskrit_text: इत्येष क्षयजः कासः क्षीणानां देहनाशनः । साध्यो बलवतां वा स्याद्याप्यस्त्वेवं क्षतोत्थितः ॥१४॥ नवो कदाचित्साध्येतापि पादगुणान्वितः । स्थविराणां जराकासः सर्वो याप्यः प्रकीर्तितः । त्रीन् पूर्वान् साधयेत्साध्यान् यथायाप्यास्तु यापयेत् ॥१५॥
transliteration: Ityeṣa kṣayajaḥ kāsaḥ kṣīṇānāṃ dehanāśanaḥ | Sādhyo balavatāṃ vā syādyāpyastvevaṃ kṣatotthitaḥ ||14|| Navo kadācitsādhyetāpi pādaguṇānvitaḥ | Sthavirāṇāṃ jarākāsaḥ sarvo yāpyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ | Trīn pūrvān sādhayetsādhyān yathāyāpyāstu yāpayet ||15||
commentary: This Kṣayajakāsa is the destroyer of the body of weak individuals. It is curable if occurred in energetic ones or it may prolong in them. The same is the case with the cough caused by traumatic chest. These two may rarely become manageable by best tetrad of treatment. The cough occurring in aged ones always prolongs. The first three types of cough are curable and they are to be treated. The prolongable ones are to be managed with suitable foods and drugs. The commentator explains that the best tetrad of treatment is best of physician, drug, nurse and the patient.

topic_heading: Common Aetiology of Hiccough and Dyspnoea
sanskrit_text: विदाहिगुरुविष्टभिरूक्षाभिष्यन्दिभोजनैः । शीतपानाशनस्थानरजोधूमातपानिलैः ॥१॥ व्यायामकर्मभाराध्ववेगायासापतर्पणैः । हिक्का श्वासश्च कासश्च नृणां समुपजायते ॥२॥
transliteration: Vidāhiguruviṣṭabhirūkṣābhiṣyandibhojanaiḥ | Śītapānāśanasthānarajodhūmātapānilaiḥ ||1|| Vyāyāmakarmabhārādhvavegāyāsāpatarpaṇaiḥ | Hikkā śvāsaśca kāsaśca nṛṇāṃ samupajāyate ||2||
commentary: By consuming foods that cause burning sensation, heavy, those cause constipation, dry and moist, and consuming cold drinks and foods and living in cold places, exposure to dust, smoke, sun and wind, indulgence in strenuous physical exercise, lifting weights, walking more distances, suppression of natural urges and by following depletive procedures, the human beings get Hikkā (hiccup), Śvāsa (dyspnoea) and Kāsa (cough). The commentator explains that due to commonality in aetiology, hiccup and dyspnoea are being explained after cough.

sanskrit_text: वायुः पुनः पुनर्मुखान्निःसरति शब्देन । स हिक्केति कथ्यते ॥३॥
transliteration: Vāyuḥ punaḥ punarmukhānnissarati śabdena | Sa hikketi kathyate ||3||
commentary: Vāyu comes out repeatedly from the mouth with sound as if expelling out the liver, spleen and intestines. That Vāyu depletes the life due to the sound, hence named as Hikkā (hiccup). The commentator explains that Hikkā is so named as it makes the sound 'Hik' in every bout.

sanskrit_text: वायुः कफेनानुगतः पञ्च हिक्काः करोति हि । अन्नजा यमला क्षुद्रा गम्भीरा च महत्यपि ॥४॥
transliteration: Vāyuḥ kaphenānugataḥ pañca hikkāḥ karoti hi | Annajā yamalā kṣudrā gambhīrā ca mahatyapi ||4||
commentary: Vāyu which follows Kapha, causes five varieties of hiccup: Annajā (caused while eating/swallowing food), Yamalā (dual bout of hiccup), Kṣudrā (minor type), Gambhīrā (hiccup with deep sound) and Mahatī (big one). The commentator explains that Yamalā type is named Vyāpetā in Caraka.

sanskrit_text: पूर्वरूपं हिक्कायाः । कण्ठहृद्गौरवम् । कषायास्यता । आध्मानं च ॥५॥
transliteration: Pūrvarūpaṃ hikkāyāḥ | Kaṇṭhahṛdgauravam | Kaṣāyāsyatā | Ādh mānaṃ ca ||5||
commentary: The premonitary symptoms of hiccup are: heaviness in the throat and chest, astringent taste in the mouth and abdominal distension. The commentator explains that the astringent taste is due to Vata, but there will be no sweetness of Kapha which is the special effect of this disease.

sanskrit_text: अन्नजा भुक्तमात्रस्य भवति । अजीर्णात् ॥६॥
transliteration: Annajā bhuktamātrasya bhavati | Ajīrṇāt ||6||
commentary: Annajā Hikkā occurs immediately after eating or due to indigestion. The commentator explains that this type of hiccup is caused by food-related factors.

sanskrit_text: यमला द्वौ द्वौ वेगौ । सा व्यपेतापि ॥७॥
transliteration: Yamalā dvau dvau vegau | Sā vyapetāpi ||7||
commentary: Yamalā Hikkā has two consecutive bouts. It is also called Vyapetā. The commentator explains that this is the dual type of hiccup.

sanskrit_text: क्षुद्रा जत्रुस्थानात् । मन्दवेगा ॥८॥
transliteration: Kṣudrā jatrusthānāt | Mandavegā ||8||
commentary: Kṣudrā Hikkā originates from the root of the neck and has mild bouts. The commentator explains that Gayadāsa says Jatru is the root of neck, which includes the heart, spleen and throat.

sanskrit_text: नाभिप्रवृत्ता या हिक्का घोरा गम्भीरनादिनी । अनेकोपद्रववती गम्भीरा नाम सा स्मृता ॥९॥
transliteration: Nābhipravṛttā yā hikkā ghorā gambhīranādinī | Anekopadravavatī gambhīrā nāma sā smṛtā ||9||
commentary: The severe hiccup which originates from the navel with deep sound and associated with many complications is known as Gambhīrā. The commentator explains that the deep sound is due to its origination from the navel, and many complications include thirst, fever etc.

sanskrit_text: मर्माण्युत्पीडयन्तीव सततं या प्रवर्तते । महाहिक्केति सा ज्ञेया सवेगात्रहरकम्पनी ॥१०॥
transliteration: Marmāṇyutpīḍayantīva satataṃ yā pravartate | Mahāhikketi sā jñeyā savegātraharakampanī ||10||
commentary: The hiccup which manifests continuously shaking the whole body and as if squeezing the Marmas (the vital parts) is called Mahatī Hikkā. The commentator explains that the main Marmas are Basti (bladder), Hrdaya (heart) and Śiras (head).

sanskrit_text: आयम्यते हिक्कतो यस्य देहो, दृष्टिश्चोर्ध्वं नाम्यते यस्य नित्यम् । क्षीणोऽन्नद्विट् क्षीति यश्चातिमात्रं, तौ द्वौ चान्त्यौ वर्जयेद्धिक्कमानौ ॥११॥ अति सञ्चितदोषस्य भक्तच्छेदकृशस्य च । व्याधिभिः क्षीणदेहस्य वृद्धस्यातिव्यवायिनः ॥१२॥ आसां या सा समुत्पन्ना हिक्का हन्त्याशु जीवितम् । यमिका च प्रलापार्तिमोहतृष्णासमन्विता ॥१३॥ अक्षीणश्चाव्यथीनश्च स्थिरधात्विन्द्रियश्च यः । तस्य साधयितुं शक्या यमिका हन्त्यतोऽन्यथा ॥१४॥
transliteration: Āyamyate hikkato yasya deho, dṛṣṭiścordhvaṃ nāmyate yasya nityam | Kṣīṇo'n nadviṭ kṣīti yaścātimātraṃ, tau dvau cāntyau varjayeddhikkamānau ||11|| Ati sañcitadoṣasya bhaktacchedakṛśasya ca | Vyādhibhiḥ kṣīṇadehasya vṛddhasyātivyavāyinaḥ ||12|| Āsāṃ yā sā samutpannā hikkā hantyāśu jīvitam | Yamikā ca pralāpārtimohatṛṣṇāsamanvitā ||13|| Akṣīṇaścāvyathīnaśca sthiradhātvindriyaśca yaḥ | Tasya sādhayituṃ śakyā yamikā hantyato'nyathā ||14||
commentary: One who feels as if one's body is expanding during the bout of hiccup and one's eyes keep looking upwards continuously, who is shrunken and the one who is emaciated, does not like food and keeps sneezing heavily - these two individuals are to be considered as terminal and are to be avoided from treating. Hiccup occurring to those who have enormous dosa-accumulation, emaciated due to lack of food, depleted due to diseases, old and those who indulge in more sexual act, kills them immediately. The Yamikā (dual hiccup) also kills the individuals soon, if it is associated with delirium, delusion and thirst. In case the individual having the dual hiccup is not emaciated, not depressed and has stable tissues and organs, then only can he be treated, otherwise it kills him. The commentator explains that Gambhīrā and Mahatī types are by nature incurable.

sanskrit_text: महानूर्ध्वश्छिन्नस्तमकः क्षुद्र इति पञ्च श्वासाः ॥१५॥
transliteration: Mahānūrdhvaśchinnastamakaḥ kṣudra iti pañca śvāsāḥ ||15||
commentary: Śvāsa (dyspnoea) is of five types: Mahān (great), Ūrdhva (upward), Chinna (interrupted), Tamaka (darkening) and Kṣudra (mild). The commentator explains that Kṣudra is of Vāta predominance, Tamaka of Kapha predominance, Chinna is caused by both Kapha and Vāta, and Mahān and Ūrdhva are caused by Vāta aggravation.

sanskrit_text: पूर्वरूपं तस्य हृत्पीडा शूलमाध्मानमेव च । आनाहो वक्त्रवैरस्यं शङ्खनिस्तोद एव च ॥१६॥ यदा स्रोतांसि संरुध्य मारुतः कफपूर्वकः । विष्यग्ग्रजति संरुद्धस्तदा श्वासान् करोति सः ॥१७॥
transliteration: Pūrvarūpaṃ tasya hṛtpīḍā śūlamādh mānameva ca | Ānāho vakravairasyaṃ śaṅkhanistoda eva ca ||16|| Yadā srotāṃsi saṃrudhya mārutaḥ kaphapūrvakaḥ | Viṣyaggrajati saṃruddhastadā śvāsān karoti saḥ ||17||
commentary: Pain in the heart, abdominal colic, flatulence, distension, distaste in the mouth and pinning sensation in the temples are the premonitory symptoms of dyspnoea. When Vāta follows the Kapha and blocks the channels completely, then it causes Śvāsa (dyspnoea). The commentator explains that the channels involved are Prāṇavahasrotas and Udāṇavahasrotas.

sanskrit_text: उद्धूयमानवातो यः शब्दवद् दुःखितो नरः । उच्चैः श्वसिति संरुद्धो मत्तवृषभ इवानिशम् ॥१८॥ प्रनष्टज्ञानविज्ञानस्तथा विभ्रान्तलोचनः । विवृतास्याननो बद्धमूत्रवर्चा विशीर्णवाक् ॥१९॥ प्रताम्यति चासौ दूराच्छ्रूयते श्वासः । स न जीवति चिरम् ॥२०॥
transliteration: Uddhūyamānavāto yaḥ śabdavad duḥkhito naraḥ | Uccaiḥ śvasiti saṃruddho mattavṛṣabha ivāniśam ||18|| Pranaṣṭajñānavijñānastathā vibhrāntalocanaḥ | Vivṛtāsyānano baddhamūtravarcā viśīrṇavāk ||19|| Pratāmyati cāsau dūrācchrūyate śvāsaḥ | Sa na jīvati ciram ||20||
commentary: The individual with Mahā Śvāsa breathes with great difficulty sounding like that of a bull which breathes on getting angry. He loses his senses, has terrified looks with wide opened eyes and mouth, suffers from constipation and retention of urine; speaks in feeble voice. He is depressed and his breathing can be heard from a distance. He will not live long after getting afflicted by this disease. The commentator explains that this is the most severe type of dyspnoea.

sanskrit_text: उच्छ्वासी दीर्घं निःश्वासं न लभते । कफरुद्धस्रोताः । वातप्रकोपात् । ऊर्ध्वदृष्टिः । भ्रान्तलोचनः । मुहुर्मुहुः प्रताम्यति । नानावेदनाभिः पीड्यते । मुखं पाण्डुवर्णम् । उच्छ्वासी प्राणं न लभते । स मुहुर्मुहुः पतति । स ऊर्ध्वश्वासो हन्ति ॥२१-२३॥
transliteration: Ucchvāsī dīrghaṃ niḥśvāsaṃ na labhate | Kapharuddhasrotāḥ | Vātaprakopāt | Ūrdhvadṛṣṭiḥ | Bhrāntalocanaḥ | Muhurmuhuḥ pratāmyati | Nānāvedanābhiḥ pīḍyate | Mukhaṃ pāṇḍuvarṇam | Ucchvāsī prāṇaṃ na labhate | Sa muhurmuhuḥ patati | Sa ūrdhvaśvāso hanti ||21-23||
commentary: The individual who breathes out for long time, but cannot take back breathe, whose channels are blocked by Kapha, who suffers from aggravated Vāta, looks upwards with eyes of terrified and fickle nature, who swoons repeatedly and suffers from various pains, whose face becomes pale and has uneasiness, such a patient breathes out but his breathing-in is obstructed. He keeps falling down with swooning. Such Ūrdhva Śvāsa kills him. The commentator explains that the upward breathing or breathing out heavily is the symptom of all types of dyspnoea.

sanskrit_text: यस्तु श्वसिति विच्छिन्नं सर्वप्राणेन पीडितः । न वा श्वसिति दुःखार्तो मर्मच्छेदरुगर्दितः ॥२४॥ आनाहस्वेदमूर्च्छितो दह्यमानेन वस्तिना । विप्लुताक्षः परिक्षीणः श्वसन् रक्तैकलोचनः ॥२५॥ विचेताः परिशुष्कास्यो विवर्णः प्रलपन्नरः । छिन्नश्वासेन विच्छिन्नः स शीघ्रं विजहात्यसून् ॥२६॥
transliteration: Yastu śvasiti vicchinnaṃ sarvaprāṇena pīḍitaḥ | Na vā śvasiti duḥkhārto marmacchedarugarditaḥ ||24|| Ānāhasvedamūrcchito dahyamānena vastinā | Viplutākṣaḥ parikṣīṇaḥ śvasan raik alocanaḥ ||25|| Vicetāḥ pariśuṣkāsyo vivarṇaḥ pralapannaraḥ | Chinnasvāsena vicchinnaḥ sa śīghraṃ vijahātyasūn ||26||
commentary: The individual suffering from Chinna Śvāsa breathes with interruption with great difficulty inspite of using all his strength. He may not also breathe due to cutting pain in the vital points of the body. He suffers from bloating of abdomen, sweat, swooning, burning sensation in the bladder. His eyes are wet with tears, he is emaciated thoroughly, his eyes are red in colour, he loses his senses, his mouth is dry, he is discoloured and suffers from delirium. He is totally broken due to this disease and will die soon. The commentator explains that the pain in the vital points is pain in the heart, and burning sensation in the bladder indicates the involvement of Pitta along with Vāta.

sanskrit_text: प्रतिलोमं यदा वायुः स्रोतांसि प्रतिपद्यते । ग्रीवां शिरश्च संगृह्य श्लेष्माणं समुदीर्य च ॥२७॥ करोति पीनसं तेन रुद्धौ घुर्धुरकं तथा । अतीव तीव्रवेगं च श्वासं प्राणप्रपीडकम् ॥२८॥ प्रताम्यति स वेगेन तृष्यति सन्निरुध्यते । प्रमुह्यति कासमानश्च स गच्छति मुहुर्मुहुः ॥२९॥ श्लेष्मणि मुच्यमाने तु भूयो भवति दुःखितः । तस्यैव च विमोक्षान्ते मुहूर्तं लभते सुखम् ॥३०॥ तथाऽस्योद्ध्वंसते कण्ठः कृच्छ्राच्छक्नोति भाषितुम् । न चापि लभते निद्रां शयानः श्वासपीडितः ॥३१॥ पार्श्वं तस्यावगूह्णाति शयानस्य समीरणः । आसीनो लभते सौख्यमुष्णं चैवाभिनन्दति ॥३२॥ उच्छ्वसिताक्षो ललाटेन स्विद्यता भूय आर्तिमान् । विशुष्कास्यो मुहुः श्वासो मुहुश्चैवावधम्यते ॥३३॥ मेघाम्बुशीतप्राग्वातैः श्लेष्मलैश्च विवर्धते । स याप्यस्तमकः श्वासः साध्यो वा स्यान्नवोत्थितः ॥३४॥
transliteration: Pratilomaṃ yadā vāyuḥ srotāṃsi pratipadyate | Grīvāṃ śiraśca saṃgṛhya śleṣmāṇaṃ samudīrya ca ||27|| Karoti pīnasaṃ tena ruddhau ghurdhurakaṃ tathā | Atīva tīvravegaṃ ca śvāsaṃ prāṇaprapīḍakam ||28|| Pratāmyati sa vega tṛṣyati sannirudhyate | Pramuhyati kāsamānaśca sa gacchati muhurmuhuḥ ||29|| Śleṣmaṇi mucyamāne tu bhūyo bhavati duḥkhitaḥ | Tasyaiva ca vimokṣānte muhūrtaṃ labhate sukham ||30|| Tathā'syoddhvaṃsate kaṇṭhaḥ kṛcchrācchaknoti bhāṣitum | Na cāpi labhate nidrāṃ śayānaḥ śvāsapīḍitaḥ ||31|| Pārśvaṃ tasyāvagūhṇāti śayānasya samīraṇaḥ | Āsīno labhate saukhyamuṣṇaṃ caivābhinandati ||32|| Ucchvasitākṣo lalāṭena svi dvatā bhūya ārtimān | Viśuṣkāsyo muhuḥ śvāso muhuścaivāvadhamyate ||33|| Meghāmbuśītaprāgvātaiḥ śleṣmalaiśca vivardhate | Sa yāpyastamakaḥ śvāsaḥ sādhyo vā syānnavotthitaḥ ||34||
commentary: When the Vāyu moves in reverse direction in the respiratory channels, it grips the neck and head while increasing Kapha and causes Pinasa (coryza). Due to hinderance of phlegm, it makes 'ghur-ghur' sounds and causes Tamaka Śvāsa troubling the vital parts with severe bouts. The individual afflicted feels as if driven into darkness. Due to severity of the bouts, he gets swooned, feels thirst and cannot perform any activity. He gets deluded during the bouts of cough and while phlegm releases, he feels great pain. After it comes out he feels relieved for some time. He has irritated throat and speaks with great difficulty. On lying, he gets the bout of dyspnoea and cannot sleep. By lying on the sides, the Vāyu gets aggravated. He feels relieved on sitting and likes warm foods, drinks and places. His eyes are bulged out, has sweating on the forehead and feels shaking of the body. His mouth is dried and gets dyspnoea repeatedly. This disease is increased by clouds, rains, cold and eastward winds and by foods that produce Kapha. This can only be prolonged, but can be cured if afflicting newly. The commentator explains that Kapha is considered as the blocking factor of channels.

sanskrit_text: ज्वरमूर्च्छासमन्वितं प्रतमकम् । उदावर्तधूमाजीर्णाभिष्यन्दवेगरोधैश्च । तमसि वर्धते । शीतैः प्रशाम्यति । अतितमःप्रवेशो संतमकम् ॥३५-३६॥
transliteration: Jvaramūrcchāsamanvitaṃ pratamakam | Udāvartadhūmājīrṇābhiṣyandavegarodhaiśca | Tamasi vardhate | Śītaiḥ praśāmyati | Atitamaḥpraveśo santamakam ||35-36||
commentary: If the individual (having Tamaka Śvāsa) is also suffering from fever and syncope, that condition is to be known as Pratamaka. This arises due to Udāvarta, dust, indigestion, wetness of the body and suppression of natural urges. When this disease increases highly during darkness or aggravation of Tamas and pacifies by cold applications, and if the individual feels that he is entering endless darkness, it is to be known as Santamaka. The commentator explains that Pratamaka is the subclassification of Tamaka Śvāsa.

sanskrit_text: रूक्षाल्पशीतवाताशनैः । क्षुद्रः श्वासः । उदीरयति चैनम् । स साध्यः । अव्यक्तलक्षणाश्च सर्वे साध्याः । महोर्ध्वच्छिन्नास्तु न सिध्यन्ति । तमकोऽपि क्षीणे न सिध्यति ॥३७-४०॥
transliteration: Rūkṣālpaśītavātāśanaiḥ | Kṣudraḥ śvāsaḥ | Udīrayati cainam | Sa sādhyaḥ | Avyaktalakṣaṇāśca sarve sādhyāḥ | Mahordhvachinnāstu na sidhyanti | Tamako'pi kṣīṇe na sidhyati ||37-40||
commentary: Kṣudra Śvāsa is caused by dry, less, cold foods and wind. It is curable. All dyspnoeas with unclear symptoms are curable. Mahān, Ūrdhva and Chinna are incurable. Tamaka is also incurable when it occurs to a weak individual. The commentator explains that Kṣudra is the disease which is caused by feeble aetiology and manifests with mild symptomatology.

sanskrit_text: कामं प्राणहरा रोगा बहवो न तु ते तथा । यथा श्वासश्च हिक्का च हरतः प्राणमाशु च ॥४१॥
transliteration: Kāmaṃ prāṇaharā rogā bahavo na tu te tathā | Yathā śvāsaśca hikkā ca harataḥ prāṇamāśu ca ||41||
commentary: There are many killer diseases but they do not take away life as fast as Hikkā (hiccup) and Śvāsa (dyspnoea) do. The commentator explains that the definite bad prognosis of Hikkā and Śvāsa by not taking up the treatment and also by improper management is explained in this stanza.

sanskrit_text: अतिव्यवायादति जल्पनात् । हास्यात् भोजनादतिशीतोष्णात् । वातादयः प्रकुप्यन्ति । स्रोतांसि संरुध्य कण्ठे । स्वरनाड्यां प्रतिहताः । स्वरभेदं कुर्वन्ति । स पञ्चधा । वातात् पित्तात् कफात् सन्निपातात् क्षयाच्च ॥१-४॥
transliteration: Ativyavāyādati jalpanāt | Hāsyāt bhojanāda tiśītoṣṇāt | Vātādayaḥ prakupyanti | Srotāṃsi saṃrudhya kaṇṭhe | Svaranāḍyāṃ pratihataḥ | Svarabhedaṃ kurvanti | Sa pañcadhā | Vātāt pittāt kaphāt sannipātāt kṣayācca ||1-4||
commentary: Due to excessive sexual act, excessive talking, laughing, eating very hot and cold foods, Vāta etc. Dosas get aggravated, block the channels in the throat, get obstructed in the voice-nerves and cause Svarabheda (disturbed voice). It is of five types: due to Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, Sannipāta and Kṣaya. The commentator explains that Svarabheda is the disturbance of voice due to vitiation of Dosas in the throat.

sanskrit_text: वातात्कण्ठशुष्कता रूक्षता कषायास्यता । पित्तात्पीतता कण्ठदाहः । कफात्स्निग्धता गौरवम् । सन्निपातात्सर्वलिङ्गम् । क्षयात्कण्ठशोषः ॥१-४॥
transliteration: Vātātkaṇṭhaśuṣkatā rūkṣatā kaṣāyāsyatā | Pittātpītatā kaṇṭhadāhaḥ | Kaphātsnigdhatā gauravam | Sannipātātsarvāliṅgam | Kṣayātkaṇṭhaśoṣaḥ ||1-4||
commentary: In Vāta type: dryness of throat, roughness, astringent taste. In Pitta type: yellowishness, burning sensation in throat. In Kapha type: oiliness, heaviness. In Sannipāta type: all the above symptoms. In Kṣaya type: dryness of throat. The commentator explains that the presence of all the symptomatology given for the three Dosas individually is seen in Sannipāta type, which is also incurable.

sanskrit_text: क्षीणस्य वृद्धस्य दुर्बलस्य चिरोत्पन्नस्य सहजस्य स्थूलस्य च । सन्निपातजं चासाध्यम् ॥५॥
transliteration: Kṣīṇasya vṛddhasya durbalasya cirotpannasya sahajasya sthūlasya ca | Sannipātajaṃ cāsādhyam ||5||
commentary: Svarabheda occurring to the emaciated, old and feeble, that of long duration and congenital, and also occurring to the obese persons and that where Dosa triad is involved, is incurable. The commentator explains that the Svarabheda occurring to the obese person due to obstruction of channels by fat is incurable, while it is curable which is caused by vitiated Medas (fat) in ordinary person.

sanskrit_text: अरोचका वातादिभिः शोकभयक्रोधलोभैः । मनसो द्वेष्यैः शब्दस्पर्शरसगन्धैश्च । पञ्चविधा अरोचका । वातात् पित्तात् कफात् सन्निपातादागन्तोश्च ॥१-२॥
transliteration: Arocakā vātādibhiḥ śokabhayakrodhalobhaiḥ | Manaso dveṣyaiḥ śabdasparśarasagandhaiśca | Pañcavidhā arocakā | Vātāt pittāt kaphāt sannipātādāgantośca ||1-2||
commentary: Arocaka (anorexia) is caused by Vāta etc. and also by grief, fear, greed, anger and foods, scenes and smells that cause depression to the Manas (mind). It is of five types: one each due to Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, one due to Sannipāta, and one due to external stimuli. The commentator explains that though grief etc. aggravate Vāta etc., it is separately enumerated to facilitate the treatment plan which is anti-causative factor.

topic_heading: Vāta and Pitta Types of Anorexia
sanskrit_text: वाताज्जिह्वास्तम्भः कषायास्यता । पित्तात्कटुकास्यता सदाहं लवणकटुकादीनां प्रतिभासः ॥२॥
transliteration: Vātājjihvāstambhaḥ kaṣāyāsyatā | Pittātkaṭukāsyatā sadāhaṃ lavaṇakaṭukādīnāṃ pratibhāsaḥ ||2||
commentary: In Vāta type of Arocaka, the teeth get sensitive and the mouth has astringent taste. In Pitta type, there is bitter and sour taste in the mouth with warmth, differed taste perception on eating and there is bad odour. The commentator explains that Katu here is to be taken as bitter.

sanskrit_text: कफाल्लवणस्वादुत्वम् । उपदेहगौरवशैत्यम् । भोज्यस्यावरोधः । आगन्तोः स्वभावास्यत्वम् । त्रिदोषात्सर्वरसप्रतिभासः ॥३॥
transliteration: Kaphāllavaṇasvādu tvam | Upadehagauravaśaityam | Bhojyasyāvarodhaḥ | Āgantoḥ svabhāvāsyatvam | Tridoṣātsarvarasapratibhāsaḥ ||3||
commentary: In Kapha type of Arocaka, salty and sweet tastes are perceived in the mouth with sticky, heavy and cold feeling, and there is hinderance in eating due to coating of Kapha. In Agantu type, there is no change in the natural taste in the mouth but there is distaste. In Tridosa type, there is perception of many tastes. The commentator explains that salty taste in the mouth is due to over burning of Kapha, and many tastes are astringent etc. due to the involvement of all the three Dosas.

sanskrit_text: वाते हृद्रुक् । पित्ते तृट्दाहः । कफे प्रसेकः । सन्निपाते सर्वम् । आगन्तौ मनसो विकारः ॥४॥
transliteration: Vāte hṛdruk | Pittetṛḍdāhaḥ | Kaphe prasekaḥ | Sannipāte sarvam | Āgantau manaso vikāraḥ ||4||
commentary: In Vāta type, there is pain in the heart. In Pitta type, thirst and burning sensation. In Kapha type, dribbling of phlegm. In Tridosa type, multiple symptoms. In Agantu type, instability of mind, syncope, immobility etc. The commentator explains that these are the specific features of each type of Arocaka.

sanskrit_text: छर्दिः पञ्चविधा । वातात् पित्तात् कफात् सन्निपाताद्बिभत्सादेश्च । दोषा भुक्तमामाशयात् समुत्क्षिप्य मुखेन निःसरन्ति । अतिद्रवस्निग्धविरुद्धातियोगात् । अत्यम्ललवणात् । अकालेऽतिमात्रम् । विषमाशनात् । शोकभयात् । अजीर्णात् क्रिमिभ्यः । गर्भिणीनाम् । अतिवेगात् । बिभत्सादर्शनात् ॥१-४॥
transliteration: Chardiḥ pañcavidhā | Vātāt pittāt kaphāt sannipātād bibhatsādeśca | Doṣā bhuktamāmāśayāt samutkṣipya mukhena nissaranti | Atidravasnigdhaviruddhātiyogāt | Atyamlalavaṇāt | Akāle'timātram | Viṣamāśanāt | Śokabhayāt | Ajīrṇāt krimibhyaḥ | Garbhiṇīnām | Ativegāt | Bibhatsādarśanāt ||1-4||
commentary: Chardi is of five types: caused by Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, Sannipāta and by looking at hatred things etc. It is caused by consuming more liquids, more oily foods, unpleasant foods, salty foods; due to eating untimely in higher doses and in incompatible foods; due to over exertion, fear, anxiety, indigestion, worm-infestation, in pregnant women, due to eating very speedily and also due to things that cause hatred. The commentator explains that Chardi is being explained after Arocaka as Arocaka is seen in Chardi.

sanskrit_text: हृल्लासोद्गारप्रतिघातो लालाप्रसेको लवणः । भक्तपानद्वेषश्च ॥५॥
transliteration: Hṛllāsodgārapratighāto lālāpraseko lavaṇaḥ | Bhaktapānadveṣaśca ||5||
commentary: Nausea, hinderance of belching, dribbling of thin and salty saliva, disliking foods and drinks are the prodromata of Chardi. The commentator explains that Lavaṇatva (the salty taste) in the saliva is the special effect of this disease.

sanskrit_text: हृन्नाभिपार्श्वरुग्शुष्कास्यः । कासः स्वरभेदः । शिरोरुक् । विविधा वेदनाः । सशब्दमल्पमल्पं कषायं फेनिलं छर्दति ॥६॥
transliteration: Hṛnnābhipārśvarugśuṣkāsyaḥ | Kāsaḥ svarabhedaḥ | Śiroruk | Vividhā vedanāḥ | Saśabdamalpamalpaṃ kaṣāyaṃ phenilaṃ chardati ||6||
commentary: In Vāta type of Chardi, there is pain in the heart and flanks, dryness of mouth, pain in the head and navel, cough, hoarseness of voice and pinning sensation in the body. The belchings are noisy and the vomit comes with difficulty and in small quantity with high speed containing froathy, broken material, black, thin and astringent in taste. The commentator explains that astringency in taste is due to Vata predominance.

sanskrit_text: मूर्च्छातृड्दाहतमःप्रवेशभ्रमाः । पीतं हरितं चोष्णं कटुकं छर्दति ॥७॥
transliteration: Mūrcchātṛḍdāhatamaḥpraveśabhramāḥ | Pītaṃ haritaṃ coṣṇaṃ kaṭukaṃ chardati ||7||
commentary: In Pitta type of Chardi, the individual suffers from syncope, thirst, dryness of the mouth, burning sensation of the head, palate and eyes, feeling of darkness and giddiness and vomits yellowish, very warm, green, bitter and blackish red material with burning sensation. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Pitta type of vomiting.

sanskrit_text: तन्द्रास्वादुप्रसेकतृप्तिनिद्रारुचिगौरवाणि । स्निग्धं घनं सितं मधुरं छर्दति । सरोमहर्षो मन्दवेदनश्च ॥८॥
transliteration: Tandrāsvāduprasekatṛptinidrārucigauravāṇi | Snigdhaṃ ghanaṃ sitaṃ madhuraṃ chardati | Saromaharṣo mandavedanaśca ||8||
commentary: In Kapha type of Chardi, the individual feels dizziness, sweetness in the mouth, dribbling of phlegm, satisfaction (as if fully eaten), sleepiness, distaste and heaviness and he vomits oily, thick and sweet tasted white material due to Kapha. There is also skintillation and less amount of pain during vomiting. The commentator explains that Santosha is satisfaction of having fully eaten.

sanskrit_text: कुक्षिशूलाजीर्णारुचिदाहतृट्छ्वासमोहाः । लवणाम्लं नीलं घनमुष्णं सरक्तं छर्दति ॥९॥
transliteration: Kukṣiśūlājīrṇārucidāhatṛṭchvāsamohāḥ | Lavaṇāmlaṃ nīlaṃ ghanamuṣṇaṃ saraktaṃ chardati ||9||
commentary: Pain in the abdomen, indigestion, distaste, burning sensation, thirst, dyspnoea and delusion are seen severely in Tridosa type of Chardi. The vomit is salty and sour in taste, blue, dense, warm and mixed with blood. The commentator explains that the above symptoms and vomiting are severe and seen continuously in this type.

sanskrit_text: वायुः प्रकुप्य मलमूत्रस्वेदस्रोतांसि रुन्धन् । ऊर्ध्वं गत्वा दोषान् संगृह्य छर्दयति । विड्मूत्रगन्धवर्णं च । तृष्णाश्वासहिक्काभिः पीडितं मुञ्चति । स मरणाय ॥१०-११॥
transliteration: Vāyuḥ prakupya malamūtrasvedasrotāṃsi rundhan | Ūrdhvaṃ gatvā doṣān saṃgṛhya chardayati | Viḍmūtragandhavarṇaṃ ca | Tṛṣṇāśvāsahikkābhiḥ pīḍitaṃ muñcati | Sa maraṇāya ||10-11||
commentary: When Vāyu gets aggravated, it obstructs the channels of faecal matter, sweat and water and turns upwards in the alimentary canal, brings the aggravated Dosa and causes vomiting that smells and looks like faeces and urine. The patient suffers from thirst, dyspnoea and hiccup and the vomiting is full of vitiated matter and very fast. Such a patient dies very soon. The commentator explains that this type of vomiting is incurable.

sanskrit_text: बिभत्सादर्शनगर्भाजीर्णविरुद्धासात्म्यक्रिमिभ्यश्च । आगन्तुः पञ्चमी । स दोषानुगतः ॥१२॥
transliteration: Bibhatsādarśanagarbhājīrṇaviruddhāsātmyakrimibhyaśca | Āgantuḥ pañcamī | Sa doṣānugataḥ ||12||
commentary: Chardi (vomiting) that occurs by seeing awful things, due to pregnancy, due to Ama (undigested stuff), incompatible foods or non-homologous foods and due to worm infestation, is called Agantuja which is the fifth type of Chardi and is to be labelled as per the predominance of Dosas (for treatment purpose). The commentator explains that for the convenience of management, they should be labelled as per the dosa-predominance.

sanskrit_text: क्रिमिभ्यो हृल्लासशूलम् । क्रिमिहृद्रोगलिङ्गम् ॥१३॥
transliteration: Krimibhyo hṛllāsaśūlam | Krimihṛdro galiṅgam ||13||
commentary: In Chardi caused by Krimi (worm-infestation), there is severe pain and nausea. The symptomatology is similar to that of heart-disease caused by Krimi (Krimija Hrdroga). The commentator explains that this type of vomiting is caused by worms.

sanskrit_text: क्षीणस्यातिप्रवृत्ता सोपद्रवा । रक्तपूयचन्द्रकोपगता च । असाध्या । निरुपद्रवा साध्या ॥१४॥
transliteration: Kṣīṇasyātipravṛttā sopadravā | Raktapūyacandrakopagatā ca | Asādhyā | Nirupadravā sādhyā ||14||
commentary: Chardi occurring excessively to an emaciated individual, if it is associated with complications and if the vomit contains blood, pus and looks lustrous, it is to be considered as incurable. The uncomplicated and curable is only to be treated. The commentator explains that the lustre in the vomit is due to the expulsion of fat etc. tissues.

sanskrit_text: कासश्वासज्वरहिक्कातृट्संमोहाः । च्छर्द्युपद्रवाः ॥१५॥
transliteration: Kāsaśvāsajvarahikkātṛṭsaṃmohāḥ | Chard yupadravāḥ ||15||
commentary: Cough, dyspnoea, fever, hiccup, thirst, instability of mind, feeling of getting into darkness are to be known as complications of Chardi. The commentator explains that these complications make the disease severe.

sanskrit_text: वातः पित्तेन सह ऊर्ध्वं गत्वा तालु संश्रित्य तृष्णां जनयति । उदकवाहिस्रोतोदोषैः । तृष्णा सप्तविधा । वातात् पित्तात् कफात् क्षतात् क्षयात् आमात् भक्तोत्था च ॥१-२॥
transliteration: Vātaḥ pittena saha ūrdhvaṃ gatvā tālu saṃśritya tṛṣṇāṃ janayati | Udakavāhisrotodoṣaiḥ | Tṛṣṇā saptavidhā | Vātāt pittāt kaphāt kṣatāt kṣayāt āmāt bhaktotthā ca ||1-2||
commentary: Vāta aggravates due to fear, strain and emaciation and gets mingled with Pitta, also aggravated by consuming more of Pitta-provocative foods. These two go up the body and reach the palate and cause thirst. Thirst is also caused by vitiation of Udakavāha srotas (channels that carry watery element) by aggravated Dosas. Thirst is of seven types: due to Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, injury, emaciation, Ama and caused during eating. The commentator explains that Pitta is accumulated and aggravated in its own place due to consumption of pungent and sour foods and indulgence in anger.

sanskrit_text: वातात्क्षामास्यता । शङ्खशिरस्तोदः । स्रोतोरोधः । विरसास्यता । शीतपानैर्वर्धते ॥३॥
transliteration: Vātātkṣāmāsyatā | Śaṅkhaśirastodaḥ | Srotorodhaḥ | Virasāsyatā | Śītapānairvardhate ||3||
commentary: In Vāta type of Trṣṇā, face becomes weak, there is pinning sensation in the temples and head, obstruction of channels, opposite taste in the mouth and the thirst increases by cold drinks and water. The commentator explains that lack of sleep, giddiness and dryness in the throat and palate are also seen in Vata type.

sanskrit_text: पित्तान्मूर्च्छाऽरुचिः प्रलापः । दाहो रक्ताक्षता । तीव्रतृष्णा । शीतप्रार्थनम् । कट्वास्यता । देहे ज्वालाविसरणम् ॥४॥
transliteration: Pittānmūrcchā'ruciḥ pralāpaḥ | Dāho raktākṣatā | Tīvratṛṣṇā | Śītaprārthanam | Kaṭvāsyatā | Dehe jvālāvisaraṇam ||4||
commentary: Syncope, having no desire to eat food, delirium, burning sensation, redness in the eyes, severe thirst, longing for cold things, bitter taste in the mouth and feeling of flames all over the body are seen in Pitta type of Trṣṇā. The commentator explains that the common symptoms of Pitta aggravation, i.e. yellowish colour of the faeces, urine, eyes etc. are to be included.

sanskrit_text: कफान्निद्रागौरवम् । मुखमाधुर्यम् । दौर्बल्यम् ॥५॥
transliteration: Kaphānidrāgauravam | Mukhamādhuryam | Daurbalyam ||5||
commentary: Kapha type of thirst is caused when aggravated Kapha covers the Agni and the heat of water-carrying channels is obstructed. The individual has more sleep, heaviness in the body, sweetness in the face and becomes very weak. The commentator explains that Susruta mentions this type to differentiate the treatment plan, and Harita says that Kapha-type thirst is caused only due to association of Pitta.

topic_heading: Thirst due to Injury and Emaciation
sanskrit_text: क्षतात् क्षीणरक्तस्य । क्षयाद्रसक्षयजा । तृष्णा न शाम्यति । दिनरात्रं पिबतोऽपि ॥६॥
transliteration: Kṣatāt kṣīṇaraktasya | Kṣayādrasakṣayajā | Tṛṣṇā na śāmyati | Din arātraṃ pibato'pi ||6||
commentary: The fourth variety of thirst occurs to the injured due to pain and loss of blood. The thirst caused due to emaciation of Rasa dhatu is called Kṣayajā. The individual afflicted by this cannot get satisfied even on drinking water during day and night. The commentator explains that the repeated drinking of water is the cardinal symptom here.

topic_heading: Thirst due to Ama and Food
sanskrit_text: आमात् सर्वलिङ्गम् । हृल्लासप्रसेकगौरवम् । भक्तोत्था स्निग्धाम्ललवणगुरुभ्यः ॥७-८॥
transliteration: Āmāt sarvaliṅgam | Hṛllāsaprasekagauravam | Bhaktotthā snigdhāmlalavaṇagurubhyaḥ ||7-8||
commentary: In Ama type of thirst, the symptomatology of the aggravation of Tridosa is seen, along with pain in the heart, excessive salivation and inactivity of the body. Thirst caused by certain foods (Bhaktotthā) occurs immediately after eating oily, sour, salty and heavy foods. The commentator explains that Drḍhabala mentions five types of thirst, and Kapha-variety comes under Amaja.

sanskrit_text: उपसर्गात् क्षीणस्वरः । अधृतिः । शुष्कवक्त्रतालुकण्ठः । दुश्चिकित्स्यः । ज्वरसंमोहराजयक्ष्मकासश्वासादिभ्यः ॥९॥
transliteration: Upasargāt kṣīṇasvaraḥ | Adhṛtiḥ | Śuṣkavaktratālukaṇṭhaḥ | Duścikitsyaḥ | Jvarasaṃmoharājayakṣmakāsaśvāsādibhyaḥ ||9||
commentary: In thirst caused as a complication (Upasarga) of some other disease, the individual has feeble voice, instability of the body, tiredness and dryness in the mouth, throat and palate. This type weakens the individual and is very difficult to cure. It occurs to those who are afflicted by fever, delusion, consumption, cough, dyspnoea etc. The commentator explains that Upasarga is Upadrava (complication), and this type is difficult to cure because the individual is already emaciated due to the main disease.

sanskrit_text: चिरोत्पन्ना क्षीणस्य छर्दियुक्ता च । घोरोपद्रवा च हन्ति ॥१०॥
transliteration: Cirotpannā kṣīṇasya chardiyuktā ca | Ghoropadravā ca hanti ||10||
commentary: All types of thirst, when continued for longer periods, thirst occurring to those emaciated due to any disease, having vomiting while suffering from thirst, and that with severe complications will kill the patient. The commentator explains that severe complications are those like dryness of the mouth etc. in more intensity.

sanskrit_text: क्षीणस्य बहुदोषस्य विरुद्धाशनस्य वेगरोधिनः । अभिघातिनो मनस्विनो वा । दोषा बहिरिन्द्रियाणि मनोवहानि स्रोतांसि च संश्रित्य । तमोगुणाभिभूतं चेतः । मोहं जनयन्ति । स षड्विधः । वातात् पित्तात् कफात् शोणितान्मद्याद्विषाच्च ॥१-५॥
transliteration: Kṣīṇasya bahudoṣasya viruddhāśanasya vegarodhinaḥ | Abhighātino manasvino vā | Doṣā bahirindriyāṇi manovahāni srotāṃsi ca saṃśritya | Tamoguṇābhibhūtaṃ cetaḥ | Mohaṃ janayanti | Sa ṣaḍvidhaḥ | Vātāt pittāt kaphāt śoṇitānmadyādv iṣācca ||1-5||
commentary: The one who is emaciated or has accumulation of aggravated Dosa, consumes incompatible foods, suppresses natural urges, indulges in injuries or is weak-minded; when such individual's external organs and internal channels of psyche are occupied by disturbed Dosas, he gets syncope. Mūrcchā is of six types: one due to each of the three Dosas, one due to Śoṇita (blood), one due to Madya (alcohol) and one due to Viṣa (poison). In all these six types, Pitta stands dominating. The commentator explains that Tamoguna which is causative for unreal knowledge suddenly increases and the Sañjñāvaha nāḍīs are occupied by that Tamas.

sanskrit_text: हृद्रुक् जृम्भा ग्लानिरिन्द्रियाग्रहणम् ॥६॥
transliteration: Hṛdruk jṛmbhā glānirindriyāgrahaṇam ||6||
commentary: Pain in the heart, yawning, fatigue and weak perception of senses are the Pūrvarūpa (prodromata) of Mūrcchā (syncope). It is labelled as per the Dosa-predominance. The commentator explains that the labelling is to be done when it is completely manifested and not at the stage of Pūrvarūpa.

sanskrit_text: वातान्नीलकृष्णारुणं नभः पश्यति । तमःप्रवेशः । क्षिप्रं प्रतिबुध्यते । कम्पः । अङ्गरुक् । हृद्रुक् । कार्श्यम् । श्यावरक्ताङ्गता ॥७-८॥
transliteration: Vātānnīlakṛṣṇāruṇaṃ nabhaḥ paśyati | Tamaḥpraveśaḥ | Kṣipraṃ pratibudhyate | Kampaḥ | Aṅgaruk | Hṛdruk | Kārśyam | Śyāvaraktāṅgatā ||7-8||
