commentary: The individual suffering from Vāta type of Mūrcchā sees the sky in bluish, black or red colour followed by entering into darkness. He comes to normalcy immediately. He has shivering, pain in the body, severe pain in the heart, emaciation and blackish red colour in the body. The commentator explains that Nīla is glowing black, Kṛṣṇa is dry black, and Aruna is blood red colour.

sanskrit_text: पित्ताद्रक्तहरितपीतानि पश्यति । तमःप्रवेशः । स्वेदेन प्रतिबुध्यते । तृट्दाहौ । रक्तपीताक्षत्वम् । आविलत्वम् । सद्यः पतति सद्यः प्रतिबुध्यते । अतिसारः । पीताङ्गता ॥९-१०॥
transliteration: Pittādraktaharitapītāni paśyati | Tamaḥpraveśaḥ | Svedena pratibudhyate | Tṛṭdāhau | Raktapītākṣatvam | Āvilatvam | Sadyaḥ patati sadyaḥ pratibudhyate | Atisāraḥ | Pītāṅgatā ||9-10||
commentary: In Pitta type of syncope, the individual sees the sky in blood red, green or yellow followed by entering into darkness and gets to his senses with profuse sweating. He has thirst, burning sensation and eyes are reddish-yellow in colour and turbid. He falls suddenly and comes to senses immediately. He has diarrhoea and his body turns to yellowish in colour. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Pitta type of syncope.

sanskrit_text: कफान्मेघतमोनभः पश्यति । चिरात्प्रतिबुध्यते । चर्मावनद्धमिव गात्रम् । प्रसेकहृल्लासौ ॥११-१२॥
transliteration: Kaphānmeghatamonabhaḥ paśyati | Cirātpratibudhyate | Carmāvanaddhamiva gātram | Prasekahṛllāsau ||11-12||
commentary: The patient of Kapha type of Mūrcchā sees the sky as if fully clouded or covered with darkness and clouds and enters into darkness. He gets to his senses very late. He feels as if his body is covered with heavy things like wet leather. He has dribbling of saliva from the mouth and nausea. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Kapha type of syncope.

sanskrit_text: सन्निपातात्सर्वलिङ्गम् । अपस्मारवत्सद्यः पतति । विभ्रमरहितं च ॥१३॥
transliteration: Sannipātātsarvāliṅgam | Apasmāravatsadyaḥ patati | Vibhramarahitaṃ ca ||13||
commentary: Due to aggravation of three of the Dosas, the individual has the symptomatology of all the three types of Mūrcchā and faints immediately without awful acts of the body. The commentator explains that 'Like in Apasmāra' means the individual falls all of a sudden and gets late to his senses.

sanskrit_text: रक्तगन्धेन मूर्च्छा भवति । रक्तदर्शनेनापि ॥१४॥
transliteration: Raktagandhena mūrcchā bhavati | Raktadarśanenāpi ||14||
commentary: By the smell of blood, the human beings get fainted. Fainting also occurs on mere seeing blood. The commentator explains that Pṛthvī (earth) and Apa (water) are predominantly of Tamas, and the smell of blood has these two components.

topic_heading: Mūrcchā due to Visa and Madya
sanskrit_text: विषमद्ययोस्तीक्ष्णगुणाधिक्यान्मोहः । रक्तजे स्तम्भः । मद्यजे विलापः । विषजे कम्पनिद्रातृष्णातमःप्रवेशाः ॥१५-१८॥
transliteration: Viṣamadyayostīkṣṇaguṇādhikyānmohaḥ | Raktaje stambhaḥ | Madyaje vilāpaḥ | Viṣaje kampanidrātṛṣṇātamaḥpraveśāḥ ||15-18||
commentary: Due to the excessive fastness of the qualities existing in Viṣa and Madya, Moha occurs by consuming them with respective symptomatology. In Raktajamūrcchā, the patient has rigid body and looks. In Madyajamūrcchā, the individual lies making cries that look like weeping with destroyed and disturbed mind. In Visajamūrcchā, there are shivering, sleep, thirst, feeling of darkness and syncope. The commentator explains that the qualities of Viṣa are light, dry, quick, vivid, active, fast, opening, fine, warm and unclear taste.

sanskrit_text: मूर्च्छा पित्ततमःप्राया । भ्रमो रजःपित्तानिलप्रायः । तन्द्रा तमोवातकफप्राया । निद्रा श्लेष्मतमःप्राया ॥१९॥
transliteration: Mūrcchā pittatamaḥprāyā | Bhramo rajaḥpittānilaprāyaḥ | Tandrā tamovātakaphaprāyā | Nidrā śleṣmatamaḥprāyā ||19||
commentary: Mūrcchā (syncope) is caused due to more of Pitta and Tamas. Bhrama (giddiness) is due to Rajas, Pitta and Anila (Vata). Tandrā (dizziness) is caused by Tamas, Vata and Kapha. Nidrā (sleep) is the result of Śleṣma and Tamas. The commentator explains that the body rotates like a wheel and the individual keeps falling down in Bhrama.

sanskrit_text: अरतिर्गात्रगौरवम् । जृम्भा ग्लानिः । तन्द्रा ॥२०॥
transliteration: Aratirgātragauravam | Jṛmbhā glāniḥ | Tandrā ||20||
commentary: Non inclination towards objects, heaviness in the body, yawning, tiredness and sleepy posture are to be considered as Tandrā (dizziness). The commentator explains that Nidrā is the detachment of mind with the organs, while delusion is to Indriyas and not mind in Tandrā.

sanskrit_text: मूर्च्छा मदश्च वेगान्ते शाम्यति । न तु संन्यासः ॥२१॥
transliteration: Mūrcchā madaśca vegānte śāmyati | Na tu saṃnyāsaḥ ||21||
commentary: The intoxication and syncope get pacified when the bout of the Dosa is completed. But Saṃnyāsa (coma) does not pacify without treatment. The commentator explains that when the manifestation of aggravated Dosa is complete, the diseases are naturally receded while it needs medication in comatic condition.

sanskrit_text: दोषा मर्माण्याश्रित्य । वाक्चेष्टामनसां नाशः । काष्ठभूतः । आशु चिकित्सितो न चेत् म्रियते ॥२२-२३॥
transliteration: Doṣā marmāṇyāśritya | Vākceṣṭāmanasāṃ nāśaḥ | Kāṣṭhabhūtaḥ | Āśu cikitsito na cet mriyate ||22-23||
commentary: The powerful impurities make place in the vital parts of the body of the weak individual and cause Saṃnyāsa, who, on getting affected by this disease loses the speech and activity of body and mind and looks like a log like a dead person. And if he is not attended with quick-acting treatment, dies soon. The commentator explains that quick-acting treatment measures are like pricking with needles, eye-applications, stronger nasal application, rubbing with grains and pulses etc.

sanskrit_text: मद्ये विषगुणाः सन्ति । अतिमिथ्योपयोगान्मदः ॥१॥
transliteration: Madye viṣaguṇāḥ santi | Atimithyopayogānmadaḥ ||1||
commentary: The qualities of Viṣa (poison) are existing in Madya (alcohol) also. Severe intoxication occurs by misuse of alcohol. The commentator explains that proper use of alcohol is to be taken in a pleasant atmosphere with peaceful mind sitting amidst beautiful damsels.

topic_heading: Good and Bad Effects of Madya
sanskrit_text: अन्नं प्राणभृतां श्रेष्ठम् । अयोगाद्विषमिव । विषमपि योगात्सुधा ॥२-३॥
transliteration: Annaṃ prāṇabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭham | Ayogādviṣamiva | Viṣamapi yogātsudhā ||2-3||
commentary: As such Madya is considered as a food stuff. This gives rise to diseases when used improperly and it is like a nectar when used in a proper manner. The Anna (food stuff) enlivens the human beings; but when consumed indiscriminately, it takes away the life. Viṣa (poison) is a killer, but when administered in a proper method, it acts as a rejuvenator of the body. The commentator explains that the improper usage of food is in terms of quantity etc.

sanskrit_text: हृष्टचित्तः सहायवान् । हितभोजी । मात्राकालविधानतः । मद्यं सुधासमम् । स्निग्धैरन्नैर्मांसैश्च । आयुर्बलवर्णसुखस्मृतिहर्षोत्साहकरम् ॥४-६॥
transliteration: Hṛṣṭacittaḥ sahāyavān | Hitabhojī | Mātrakālavidhānataḥ | Madyaṃ sudhāsamam | Snigdhairannairmāṃsaiśca | Āyurbalavarṇasukhasmṛtiharṣotsāhakaram ||4-6||
commentary: The Madya acts as a nectar to those who consume it with a pleasant mood along with compatible foods in a specific method, in a suitable dosage and in suitable time. Madya, if taken along with unctuous substances and foods and meat prepared with unctuous substances in a proper manner, enhances longevity, strength, replenishment of the body, good looks, satisfaction of the mind, inclination and valour. The commentator explains that compatible foods are those having antagonistic qualities to Madya.

sanskrit_text: बुद्धिस्मृतिप्रसादः । हर्षः । पानभोजननिद्रामैथुनेच्छा । पाठगीतप्रसङ्गः । वाचः प्रसरः । प्रथममदे ॥७॥
transliteration: Buddhismṛtiprasādaḥ | Harṣaḥ | Pānabhojananidrāmaithunecchā | Pāṭhagītaprasaṅgaḥ | Vācaḥ prasaraḥ | Prathamamade ||7||
commentary: Pleasantness of intellect and memory, happiness, increase in desire for drinking, eating, sleeping and sexual intercourse, development of capacity in reading and singing and rise in voice are seen in Prathamamada (primary intoxication) which keeps the individual joyful. The commentator explains that Buddhi is experience and Smṛti is continuance of experience.

sanskrit_text: अस्पष्टबुद्धिवाक्यः । विपरीताचारः । क्रोधन उन्मत्त इव । तन्द्रालस्ययुक्तः ॥८॥
transliteration: Aspaṣṭabuddhivākyaḥ | Viparītācāraḥ | Krodhana unmatta iva | Tandrālas yayuktaḥ ||8||
commentary: The individual afflicted with secondary intoxication has unclear intellect and speech. He has reverse activity, furious nature and behaves like an insane person. He is affected by repeated lassitude and sleep. The commentator explains that this is the medium stage of intoxication.

sanskrit_text: अगम्यगामी । गुरुजनानादरः । अभक्ष्यभक्षकः । गूढाभिधः । नष्टसंज्ञः । अस्वतन्त्रः ॥९॥
transliteration: Agamyagāmī | Gurujanānādaraḥ | Abhakṣyabhakṣakaḥ | Gūḍhābhidhaḥ | Naṣṭasaṃjñaḥ | Asvatantraḥ ||9||
commentary: In the third stage of intoxication, the individual is totally in the grip of intoxication due to which he goes in the ways that one should not go, does not regard the teachers, eats uneatables and speaks out the secrets of his heart. He lacks discriminatory capability and is totally dominated by intoxication. The commentator explains that Agamyan means not fit for going like copulation with teachers' wife.

sanskrit_text: मूर्च्छा । काष्ठवत् स्तब्धः । संज्ञानाशः । मृतकल्पः । नरः क इच्छेत् ॥१०-११॥
transliteration: Mūrcchā | Kāṣṭhavat stabdhaḥ | Saṃjñānāśaḥ | Mṛtakalpaḥ | Naraḥ ka icchet ||10-11||
commentary: On attaining fourth stage of intoxication, the individual faints and becomes motionless like a broken log of wood. He loses the sensation of what to and what not to and becomes worse than a corpse. The commentator explains that the individual in this stage is not capable of discriminating what to do and what not to, and this stage is terrible and troubling.

sanskrit_text: अन्नेन विना सहायेन विना । नित्यं मद्यपानं दुःखदम् । देहभेदकरम् ॥१२॥
transliteration: Annena vinā sahāyena vinā | Nityaṃ madyapānaṃ duḥkhadam | Dehabhedakaram ||12||
commentary: If alcohol is taken on empty stomach without any company regularly, it gives rise to very difficult diseases and it also destroys the body. The commentator explains that this is against the regulation of taking alcohol along with oily foods etc.

sanskrit_text: क्रोधितस्य भीतस्य तृषितस्य शोचतः । क्षुधितस्य व्यायामभाराध्ववेगरोधिनः । जलातिभोजनात् । अजीर्णिनः । क्षीणस्यातपपीडितस्य । पानं विकारकरम् ॥१३-१५॥
transliteration: Krodhitasya bhītasya tṛṣitasya śocataḥ | Kṣudhitasya vyāyāmabhārādhvavegarodhinaḥ | Jalātibhojanāt | Ajīrṇinaḥ | Kṣīṇasyātapapīḍitasya | Pānaṃ vikārakaram ||13-15||
commentary: Alcohol, if consumed by those who are angry, terrified, thirsty, agonised, hungry, emaciated due to strenuous exercise, carrying weights and walking distances, weakened due to suppression of natural urges, with a bloated stomach due to over drinking of water and over eating, eaten on incomplete digestion of previous food, emaciated and hit by heat, causes various diseases. The commentator explains that even if alcohol is taken with regulated food etc., it causes various diseases when consumed in the above conditions.

sanskrit_text: वाताद्धिक्काश्वासशिरःकम्पः । पार्श्वरुगनिद्राप्रलापाः । पित्तात्तृड्दाहज्वरस्वेदप्रलापातिसारभ्रमहरिताङ्गता । कफाच्छर्द्यरुचिहृल्लासतन्द्रालस्यगौरवशीताङ्गता । सर्वलिङ्गं त्रिदोषजम् ॥१६-१८॥
transliteration: Vātāddhikkāśvāsaśiraḥ kampaḥ | Pārśvaruganidrāpralāpāḥ | Pittāttṛḍdāhajvarasvedapralāpāt isārabhramaharitāṅgatā | Kaphācchardyarucihṛllāsatandrālas yagauravaśītāṅgatā | Sarvaliṅgaṃ tridoṣajam ||16-18||
commentary: Excessive intoxication in which Vāta predominance exists: hiccup, dyspnoea, trembling of the head, pain in the flanks, sleeplessness and irrelevant talk. In Pitta predominant: thirst, burning sensation, fever, sweating, delusion, diarrhoea, severe giddiness and greenish colour all over the body. In Kapha predominant: vomiting, distaste, nausea, drowsiness, lassitude, heaviness and cold touch on all over the body. If all the above symptomatology is seen, it should be understood as Tridosaja. The commentator explains that all intoxications have the involvement of all three Dosas, and predominance leads to labelling.

sanskrit_text: अतिप्रसेको गात्रगौरवम् । मुखारुचिः । मूत्रपुरीषनिरोधः । तन्द्रा । अरुचिः । तृट्शिरोरुक् । सन्धिभेदः ॥१९॥
transliteration: Atipraseko gātragauravam | Mukhāruciḥ | Mūtrapurīṣanirodhaḥ | Tandrā | Aruciḥ | Tṛṭśiroruk | Sandhibhedaḥ ||19||
commentary: Excessive dribbling of saliva, heaviness in the body, distaste in the mouth, non-movement of the urine and stool, drowsiness, anorexia, thirst, headache and breaking pain in the joints are the features of Paramada. The commentator explains that these are the signs of ultimate intoxication.

sanskrit_text: पानाजीर्णे आध्मानं छर्दिर्दाहः । पानविभ्रमे हृद्गात्रतोदः । प्रसेकः । कण्ठधूमः । मूर्च्छा । छर्दिः । ज्वरः । शिरोरुक् । दाहः । मद्यान्नद्वेषः ॥२०॥
transliteration: Pānājīrṇe ādh mānaṃ chardirdāhaḥ | Pānavibhrame hṛdgāt ratodaḥ | Prasekaḥ | Kaṇṭhadhūmaḥ | Mūrcchā | Chardiḥ | Jvaraḥ | Śiroruk | Dāhaḥ | Madyānnadveṣaḥ ||20||
commentary: Bloating of the abdomen, vomiting and burning sensation are the symptoms when alcohol does not get digested. Pānavibhrama is characterised by pinning sensation in the heart and the body, dribbling of saliva, fumes in the throat, syncope, vomiting, fever, headache, burning sensation and hatred towards alcohol and food. The commentator explains that Kanthadhūma is the feeling as if fumes come out of the throat.

sanskrit_text: अधरोष्ठश्लथता । अतिशीताङ्गता । अन्तर्दाहः । मुखस्नेहः । कृष्णनीलजिह्वौष्ठदन्तता । रक्तपीतनेत्रता । हिक्काज्वरच्छर्दिकम्पपार्श्वरुक्कासभ्रमाः ॥२१-२२॥
transliteration: Adharoṣṭhaślathatā | Atiśītāṅgatā | Antardāhaḥ | Mukhasnehaḥ | Kṛṣṇanīlajihv auṣṭhadantatā | Raktapītanetratā | Hikkājvaracchardikampapārśvarukkāsabhramāḥ ||21-22||
commentary: Flaccidity of the upper lip, very cold in touch (externally) and severe burning sensation (from within the body), oily mouth, black or bluish colour in the tongue, lips and teeth, yellowish or blood red colour in the eyes are the features of over intoxicated individual, who should not be taken for treatment. Hiccup, fever, vomiting, shivering, pain in the flanks, cough and giddiness are the complications which occur to the one who is afflicted by over drinking of alcohol. The commentator explains that these complications make the intoxication difficult for care but not incurable as the features of incurability are given separately.

sanskrit_text: पानोष्मा त्वग्गतः । पित्तरक्तयोः संसर्गात् । दाहं करोति । पित्तप्रत्यनीकं कार्यम् ॥१॥
transliteration: Pānoṣmā tvaggataḥ | Pittaraktayoḥ saṃsargāt | Dāhaṃ karoti | Pittapratyanīkaṃ kāryam ||1||
commentary: The heat caused by alcohol reaches the skin, gets mixed up with the Pitta and Rakta (blood) and causes severe burning sensation. Anti-Pitta regimen has to be followed in the management of such conditions. The commentator explains that Dāha (burning sensation) also occurs in Madātyaya (over intoxication).

sanskrit_text: रक्तं प्रकुप्य सर्वगात्रं दहति । दह्यमान इव तृष्णा । ताम्रवर्णता । ताम्राक्षता । लोहगन्धित्वं वक्त्रस्य । अग्निमध्य इव ॥२॥
transliteration: Raktaṃ prakupya sarvagātraṃ dahati | Dahyamāna iva tṛṣṇā | Tāmravarṇatā | Tāmrākṣatā | Lohagandhitvaṃ vaktrasya | Agnimadhya iva ||2||
commentary: The aggravated blood spreads all over the body and causes burning. The individual feels as if he is being burnt, thirsty, his body becomes coppery in colour and eyes become coppery-red. His body and mouth smell like iron and he feels as if he is amidst fire. The commentator explains that this is the burning sensation caused by blood vitiation.

sanskrit_text: पित्तजे पित्तज्वरलिङ्गम् । तच्चिकित्सा च पित्तज्वरवत् ॥३॥
transliteration: Pittaje pittajvaraliṅgam | Taccikitsā ca pittajvaravat ||3||
commentary: In Dāha caused by Pitta, the symptomatology is similar to Pitta Jvara (fever caused by Pitta) and the treatment to be followed is also like that of Pitta Jvara. The commentator explains that the vitiation of Amāsaya is not in Pittaja Dāha which is the difference between these two.

sanskrit_text: तृष्णाया निरोधात् । उदकक्षयात् । उष्मा वर्धते । अन्तर्बहिर्दाहः । मूढता । कण्ठताल्वोष्ठशोषः । जिह्वानिर्गमः ॥४॥
transliteration: Tṛṣṇāyā nirodhāt | Udakakṣayāt | Uṣmā vardhate | Antarbahir dāhaḥ | Mūḍhatā | Kaṇṭhatālvoṣṭhaśoṣaḥ | Jihvānirgamaḥ ||4||
commentary: By suppressing the thirst, the watery part of the body diminishes and warmth (Pitta) increases which causes burning sensation internally and externally. The individual becomes dull, his throat, palate and lips dry up and his tongue extends out from the mouth. The commentator explains that this is the burning sensation caused by suppressing thirst.

sanskrit_text: रक्तेन कोष्ठपूर्णत्वात् । सुदारुणो दाहः ॥५॥
transliteration: Raktena koṣṭhapūrṇatvāt | Sudāruṇo dāhaḥ ||5||
commentary: There is another variety of Dāha caused by filling of the alimentary canal with blood which is unbearable. The commentator explains that filling of the alimentary canal with blood is caused by deep injuries in the Koṣṭhāṅgas (organs of the alimentary canal).

sanskrit_text: धातुक्षयात् मूर्च्छातृट् । क्षीणस्वरः । क्रियाहीनः । प्राणान्तकरः ॥६॥
transliteration: Dhātukṣayāt mūrcchātṛṭ | Kṣīṇasvaraḥ | Kriyāhīnaḥ | Prāṇāntakaraḥ ||6||
commentary: In the burning sensation caused by depletion of bodily tissues, the individual suffers from syncope and thirst. He has weak voice, inability in performing bodily activity and dies due to severity of the problem. The commentator explains that Kriyāhīna means immobile, and if he is not given any treatment, he breathes his last soon.

topic_heading: Dāha due to Injury and Marma Injury
sanskrit_text: अभिघातात् । अभोजनात् । बहुविधं विलापम् । अन्तर्दाहः । तृट्मूर्च्छाप्रलापः । मर्माभिघातजो दाहः सप्तमः । सर्वे दाहा शीताङ्गाः प्रत्याख्येयाः ॥७॥
transliteration: Abhighātāt | Abhojanāt | Bahuvidhaṃ vilāpam | Antardāhaḥ | Tṛṭmūrcchāpralāpaḥ | Marmābhighātajo dāhaḥ saptamaḥ | Sarve dāhā śītāṅgāḥ pratyākhyeyāḥ ||7||
commentary: In the burning sensation caused by injury, the individual does not eat food and keeps weeping in many ways. Therefore he has more of internal burning sensation and suffers from thirst, syncope and delirium. The seventh variety of burning sensation is incurable which is caused by injury to the vital parts of the body. All types of Dāhas, if associated with cold touch on the body, should be avoided from treating. The commentator explains that Marmas (vital parts) are head, heart, bladder etc.

sanskrit_text: दोषा मनोवहानि स्रोतांसि संश्रित्य । मनसः संमोहं कुर्वन्ति । स उन्मादः ॥१॥
transliteration: Doṣā manovahāni srotāṃsi saṃśritya | Manasaḥ saṃmohaṃ kurvanti | Sa unmādaḥ ||1||
commentary: The aggravated Dosas, on approaching upwards to the Manas (mind) cause mental disturbance, hence this disease is called Unmāda (insanity). The commentator explains that Madayanti means they intoxicate or cause mental disturbance, and Unmārgagamana is going in different or unusual direction.

sanskrit_text: त्रय एकैकशो दोषैः । चतुर्थः सन्निपातेन । पञ्चमः शोकादिभिः । षष्ठो विषजः । अप्रवृद्धास्तरुणा मदाः ॥२-३॥
transliteration: Traya ekaikaśo doṣaiḥ | Caturthaḥ sannipātena | Pañcamaḥ śokādibhiḥ | Ṣaṣṭho viṣajaḥ | Apravṛddhāstaruṇā madāḥ ||2-3||
commentary: Three due to each of the three aggravated Dosas; one due to combination of all the three Dosas; one due to mental agony etc.; and sixth variety also occurs due to poisoning. If this disease is not very aggressive and early in duration, it is named as Mada (intoxication). The commentator explains that mental agony is grief etc., and Mada is also caused by Dosa-vitiation.

sanskrit_text: विरुद्धाशनात् । दुष्टान्नात् । अशुचिभोजनात् । देवगुरुब्राह्मणनिन्दा । भयहर्षाभिघातैः । अस्वस्थाचारैः ॥४॥
transliteration: Viruddhāśanāt | Duṣṭānnāt | Aśucibhojanāt | Devagurubrāhmaṇanindā | Bhayaharṣābhighātaiḥ | Asth ācāraiḥ ||4||
commentary: Eating incompatible, spoilt and unclean foods; blasphemy of Gods, teachers and Brahmins; mental shock caused by terror and over pleasure; and irregular/improper bodily activities are the causative factors of Unmāda. The commentator explains that Duṣṭa means added with Gara (food poisoning) etc.

sanskrit_text: दोषा हृदयं बुद्धिस्थानमाश्रित्य । मनोवहानि स्रोतांसि दूषयन्ति । संज्ञां विनाशयन्ति ॥५॥
transliteration: Doṣā hṛdayaṃ buddhisthānamāśritya | Manovahāni srotāṃsi dūṣayanti | Saṃjñāṃ vināśayanti ||5||
commentary: Due to the above causative factors, the weak minded individual's Dosas vitiate and get lodged in the heart which is the seat of intellect. Having vitiated the Manovahasrotas (mind-channels), they immediately stupefy his consciousness. The commentator explains that Alpasattva is the one who has lesser Sattva guna, the most required mental characteristic.

sanskrit_text: विभ्रान्तदृष्टिः । चलमनाः । भ्रान्तलोचनः । भीरुः । प्रलापी । हृदयशून्यः ॥६॥
transliteration: Vibhrāntadṛṣṭiḥ | Calamanāḥ | Bhrāntalocanaḥ | Bhīruḥ | Pralāpī | Hṛdayaśūnyaḥ ||6||
commentary: Disturbed perception, instability of mind, fickle looks, fear, irrelevant talk, hollowness in the heart are the common symptomatology of insanity. The commentator explains that Jejjata considers the above as common prodromata, while Cakrapāṇi holds that this is common symptomatology.

sanskrit_text: वातात् । रूक्षाल्पशीतभोजनात् । विरेकात् । धातुक्षयात् । उपवासात् । अति चिन्तया हृदि क्षुब्धे । बुद्धिस्मृतिनाशः । असंबद्धहास्यस्मितनृत्यगीतभाषणचेष्टितरोदनानि । परुषत्वं कार्श्यम् । रक्ताङ्गता । पाकान्ते वेगः ॥७-८॥
transliteration: Vātāt | Rūkṣālpaśītabhojanāt | Virekāt | Dhātukṣayāt | Upavāsāt | Ati cintayā hṛdi kṣubdhe | Buddhis smṛtināśaḥ | Asambaddhahāsyasmitanṛtyagītabhāṣaṇaceṣṭitarodanāni | Paruṣatvaṃ kārśyam | Raktāṅgatā | Pākānte vegaḥ ||7-8||
commentary: Vāta, which is increased due to dry, less and cold foods, purificatory measures like purgation and emesis, depletion of bodily tissues and fasting, vitiates the heart that is already disturbed with over thinking etc. and destroys intellect and memory. The individual has irrelevant laughter, smile, dancing, singing, speech, bodily postures and weeping. He also has coarseness, emaciation and reddish colour of the body and the bout of insanity is more energetic on digestion of food. The commentator explains that the use of Vireka (laxation) includes Vamana (emesis) as well.

sanskrit_text: पित्तात् । अजीर्णभोजनात् । कट्वम्लविदाह्यतिउष्णात् । हृदयमाश्रित्य । अतिकोपः । रुदितम् । नग्नता । भीषणता । पलायनम् । उष्मा । धूमायनम् । छायाप्रार्थना । शीतभोज्यपानेच्छा । हरिद्राङ्गता ॥९-१०॥
transliteration: Pittāt | Ajīrṇabhojanāt | Kaṭvamlavidāhyat iuṣṇāt | Hṛdayamāśritya | Atikopaḥ | Ruditam | Nagnatā | Bhīṣaṇatā | Palāyanam | Uṣmā | Dhūmāyanam | Chāyāprārthanā | Śītabhojyapānecchā | Haridrāṅgatā ||9-10||
commentary: Pitta, which is accumulated due to Aajīrṇabhojana (eating without digestion of the previous food), pungent, sour, over burnt and very warm foods, moves fast, gets lodged in the heart of the weak individual and causes severe insanity. Intolerance, making hue and cry, being naked, frightening, running away, warmth and feeling of fumes coming out of the body, desire to be in shadow, to eat cold foods and to drink cool drinks and yellowish lusture on the body are the signs and symptoms of Pitta type of insanity. The commentator explains that Purvavat means in the same manner as the pathogenesis took place in Vata type of insanity.

sanskrit_text: कफात् । संपूरणैः । उष्णेन सह । हृदयमाश्रित्य । बुद्धिस्मृतिनाशः । चित्तमोहः । मन्दभाषणचेष्टः । अजीर्णः । स्त्रीसङ्गप्रार्थना । अमित्रप्रार्थना । अतिनिद्रा । छर्दिः । प्रसेकः । शुक्लनखादिः । भुक्ते वेगः ॥११-१२॥
transliteration: Kaphāt | Saṃpūraṇaiḥ | Uṣṇena saha | Hṛdayamāśritya | Buddhi smṛtināśaḥ | Cittamohaḥ | Mandabhāṣaṇaceṣṭaḥ | Ajīrṇaḥ | Strīsaṅgaprārthanā | Amitrapra rthanā | Atinidrā | Chardiḥ | Prasekaḥ | Śuklanakhādiḥ | Bhukte vegaḥ ||11-12||
commentary: Kapha gets aggravated due to replenishing foods in the inactive individual and along with Uṣṇa (Pitta), it vitiates the heart and destroys the intellect and memory and produces the disease of insanity stupefying the Citta (innermind). The individual has mild speech and physical activity, indigestion, desirous of the company of women and unfriendly people, over sleep, vomiting, dribbling of saliva, whitish colour of the nails etc. and the bout of insanity is stronger on eating food. The commentator explains that Saṃpūraṇaiḥ means due to replenishing foods, and Uṣṇa indicates that even in Unmāda caused by Kapha, Pitta is also associated.

sanskrit_text: सन्निपातात् । सर्वदोषहेतुभिः । सर्वलिङ्गम् । विरुद्धभैषज्यविधिः । तादृगसाध्यम् ॥१३॥
transliteration: Sannipātāt | Sarvadoṣahetubhiḥ | Sarvaliṅgam | Viruddhabhaiṣajyavidhiḥ | Tādṛgasādhyam ||13||
commentary: Unmāda caused by Sannipāta (all three of the Dosas) is very severe in which the aetiological factors of all the Dosas participate in the causation of the disease and it has all the symptomatology of Dosa-triad. This has negative treatment and hence is surely avoidable from treating. The commentator explains that Sarvaiḥ Samastaiḥ means all the three Dosas aggravated due to all the aetiological factors of each of them, and Viruddhabhaisajyavidhi means that single Dosa treatment would not suffice here.

sanskrit_text: चौरराजशत्रुभयात् । धनबन्धुनाशात् । प्रियावियोगात् । मनसः क्षोभात् । अनेकं प्रलपति । गायति हसति रोदिति । संमूढः ॥१४॥
transliteration: Caurarājaśatrubhayāt | Dhanabandhunāśāt | Priyāviyogāt | Manasaḥ kṣobhāt | Anekaṃ pralapati | Gāyati hasati roditi | Saṃmūḍhaḥ ||14||
commentary: The mind will be upset (and Unmāda occurs) when the individual is terrified by thieves, kingsmen, enemies and the like or when there is a loss of money and relatives or on deprival of the loved ones and ultimately mental blow occurs. Then he speaks innumerable things including secrets, sings, laughs and weeps. He is stupefied due to improper perception. The commentator explains that Priyāviraṃsaḥ means not being able to get the company of loved one.

sanskrit_text: विषात् । रक्ताक्षता । हतौजः । हतबलः । हतेन्द्रियः । दीनः । कृष्णमुखः । विभ्रान्तसंज्ञः ॥१५॥
transliteration: Viṣāt | Raktākṣatā | Hataujaḥ | Hatabalaḥ | Hatendriyaḥ | Dīnaḥ | Kṛṣṇamukhaḥ | Vibhrāntasaṃjñaḥ ||15||
commentary: In the Unmāda caused by poison, the individual has reddish eyes, decreased energy, senses and lusture, he is depressed with a black face and improper perception. The commentator explains that these are the signs of poison-induced insanity.

sanskrit_text: अधोमुखः ऊर्ध्वमुखो वा । क्षीणमांसबलः । अनिद्रः । म्रियते ॥१६॥
transliteration: Adhomukhaḥ ūrdhvamukho vā | Kṣīṇamāṃsabalaḥ | Anidraḥ | Mriyate ||16||
commentary: The individual suffering from Unmāda who always keeps his face downwards or upwards and who has depleted musculature and strength and who has no sleep will die. The commentator explains that these are the signs of incurability.

sanskrit_text: अमर्त्यवाक्शौर्यचेष्टाज्ञानविज्ञानबलादियुक्तः । अनियतवेगः । भूतोन्मादः ॥१७॥
transliteration: Amartyavākśauryaceṣṭājñānavijñānabalādiyuktaḥ | Aniyatavegaḥ | Bhūtonmādaḥ ||17||
commentary: If a patient of Unmāda possesses super human power in speech, valour, activity, knowledge and its implications, strength etc. and if his bout of the disease is irregular, such individual should be known as suffering from Bhūtonmāda (insanity caused by supernatural powers). The commentator explains that Jñāna is knowledge and Vijñāna is its practical implications.

sanskrit_text: देवग्रहः सौम्यः । देवशत्रुग्रहः क्रूरः । गन्धर्वग्रहः स्मितकीर्तननृत्यगीतप्रियः । यक्षग्रहः ताम्राक्षः । पितृग्रहः पितृभक्तः । नागग्रहः सर्पवत्सर्पति । राक्षसग्रहो मांसरुधिरप्रियः । पिशाचग्रहः स्रस्तपाणिः ॥१८-२५॥
transliteration: Devagrahaḥ saumyaḥ | Devaśatrugrahaḥ krūraḥ | Gandharvagrahaḥ smitakīrtananṛtyagītapriyaḥ | Yakṣagrahaḥ tāmrākṣaḥ | Pitṛgrahaḥ pitṛbhaktaḥ | Nāgagrahaḥ sarpavatsarpati | Rākṣasagraho māṃsarudhirapriyaḥ | Piśācagrahaḥ srastapāṇiḥ ||18-25||
commentary: Deva Graha: contented, tidy, divine garlands, no sleep, truth, bright, stable looks, gives boons. Devaśatru Graha: profuse sweating, abuses brahmins, teachers and gods, red eyes, fear, irregular looks, not satisfied, crooked. Gandharva Graha: pleasant, roams in gardens, well-mannered, sings, wears garlands, liked by all, dances, smiling. Yakṣa Graha: coppery eyes, red thin attire, majestic, walks fast, speaks less, patient, bright. Pitṛ Graha: offers food to forefathers, peaceful, reverse clothes, likes meat, sesame, jaggery, kheer. Nāga Graha: crawls like snake, licks lips, furious, likes jaggery, honey, milk, kheer. Rākṣasa Graha: fond of meat, blood, alcohol, shameless, furious, valourous, roams in darkness, hates cleanliness. Piśāca Graha: hands up, emaciated, harsh, blabbering, stinking, untidy, gluttony, roams in woods, weeping. The commentator explains that these are the signs of different Graha afflictions.

sanskrit_text: शूनाक्षः स्थूलाक्षो वा । शीघ्रगामी । फेनलालास्वादी । निद्रालुः । पतनशीलः । कम्पते । त्रयोदशवर्षाणि चेत् । असाध्यः ॥२६-२८॥
transliteration: Śūnākṣaḥ sthūlākṣo vā | Śīghragāmī | Phenalālāsvādī | Nidrāluḥ | Patanaśīlaḥ | Kampate | Trayodaśavarṣāṇi cet | Asādhyaḥ ||26-28||
commentary: The one who has swollen eyes, walks fast, licks the froath that comes from his mouth, sleeps continuously, falls from high altitudes, shivers and also who has 13 years of history of insanity is incurable. The commentator explains that the Grahas afflict for three purposes: to trouble, to play with, or to get honoured. The Godly Grahas afflict during the full-moon day, demons during dawn and dusk, Gandharvas on the eighth day, Yakṣas on the first day, Pitṛs on the descending-moon, Nāgas on the fifth day, Rākṣasas during night time and Piśācas on the fourteenth day.

sanskrit_text: आदर्शादौ प्रतिबिम्बवत् । शीतोष्णवत् । सूर्यकान्ते अग्निवत् । शरीरे आत्मवत् । अदृश्याः । पीडयन्ति ॥२९-३०॥
transliteration: Ādarśādau pratibimbavat | Śītoṣṇavat | Sūryakānte agnivat | Śarīre ātmavat | Adṛśyāḥ | Pīḍayanti ||29-30||
commentary: As the reflection to the mirror etc., cold and warmth to the living beings, fire to the sun-stone and as the body to the soul, the Grahas are invisible to the human beings. After afflicting the body being invisible, they create unbearable pain. The commentator explains that the word etc. in 'mirror etc.' includes water, oil etc. which reflect the objects.

sanskrit_text: ग्रहाः प्रभावतः सिद्धाः । तपोदानयज्ञसत्यव्रतादिभिः । अष्टसिद्धियुक्ताः । न मनुष्यैः सह संसर्गम् । न हिंसन्ति । एतेषां सेवका हिंसन्ति ॥३१-३२॥
transliteration: Grahāḥ prabhāvataḥ siddhāḥ | Tapodānayajñasatyavratādibhiḥ | Aṣṭasiddhiyuktāḥ | Na manuṣyaiḥ saha saṃsargam | Na hiṃsanti | Eteṣāṃ sevakā hiṃsanti ||31-32||
commentary: The Grahas possess superior qualities as per their capacity by means of severe penance, donations, rituals, righteous behaviour, regulated living as speaking truth and also the eight attainments called Aṣṭasiddhis. Hence they would not mingle with human beings nor they attack or afflict them. The subordinates of these Grahas who are innumerable in number and who are furious, have the habit of consuming blood, essence of meat and flesh and who keep roaming in the night time, only afflict the human beings. The commentator explains that this verse explains the relationship between supernatural powers and human beings.

sanskrit_text: दोषा हृदयमार्गान् गत्वा । स्मृतिं नाशयन्ति । तमःप्रवेशः । वेपथुः । स्मृतिभ्रंशः । चतुर्विधः ॥१॥
transliteration: Doṣā hṛdayamārgān gatvā | Smṛtiṃ nāśayanti | Tamaḥpraveśaḥ | Vepathuḥ | Smṛtibhraṃśaḥ | Caturvidhaḥ ||1||
commentary: Dosas aggravated by continuous thinking, grief etc. get lodged in the channels of the heart, destroy the memory and cause Apasmāra (epilepsy). Feeling of entering into darkness, convulsions/fits and loss of memory are present in this disease which is called Apasmāra and this is of four types. The commentator explains that Smṛti is a part of knowledge which may also be acquired by experience.

sanskrit_text: हृत्कम्पः । हृच्छून्यता । स्वेदः । भ्रान्तदृष्टिः । मूर्च्छा । प्रज्ञानाशः । अनिद्रा ॥२॥
transliteration: Hṛtkampaḥ | Hṛcchūnyatā | Svedaḥ | Bhrāntadṛṣṭiḥ | Mūrcchā | Prajñānāśaḥ | Anidrā ||2||
commentary: Trembling sensation in the heart (palpitation) and feeling of hollowness in the heart, perspiration, hollow looks, syncope, loss of sensation, loss of sleep are the premonitory symptoms of this disease. The commentator explains that Mūrcchā is delusion of the mind while Prajñānāśaḥ is that of senses.

sanskrit_text: वातात्कम्पते । दन्तान् खादति । फेनं वमति । तीव्रश्वासः । रूक्षारुणकृष्णं पश्यति ॥३॥
transliteration: Vātātkampate | Dantān khādati | Phenaṃ vamati | Tīvraśvāsaḥ | Rūkṣāruṇakṛṣṇaṃ paśyati ||3||
commentary: In Apasmāra caused by Vāta, the individual shivers, bites his teeth, vomits froath, suffers from severe dyspnoea and he sees everything to be harsh, red and black in colour. The commentator explains that Susruta says that the patient feels as if black objects are following him.

sanskrit_text: पित्तात्पीतफेनः । पीतगात्रवक्त्रनेत्रः । पीतरक्तं पश्यति । अग्निसंवृतम् । तृट्दाहौ ॥४॥
transliteration: Pittātpītaphenaḥ | Pītagātravaktranetraḥ | Pītaraktaṃ paśyati | Agnisaṃvṛtam | Tṛṭdāhau ||4||
commentary: The patient suffering from Pitta type of Apasmāra has yellowish froath coming from his mouth; his body, face and eyes are also yellowish in colour. He sees his surroundings and people in yellow and red in colour and as if occupied by fire while he suffers from thirst and heat. The commentator explains that Susruta says yellow objects are seen in Pitta type.

sanskrit_text: कफाच्छुक्लफेनः । शुक्लगात्रवक्त्रनेत्रः । शीताङ्गः । रोमहर्षः । गौरवम् । शुक्लं पश्यति । चिरात्प्रतिबुध्यते ॥५॥
transliteration: Kaphācchuklaphenaḥ | Śuklagātravaktranetraḥ | Śītāṅgaḥ | Romaharṣaḥ | Gauravam | Śuklaṃ paśyati | Cirātpratibudhyate ||5||
commentary: The patient of Kapha (Śleṣma) Apasmāra has whitish froath, body colour, face and eyes. He has cold touch on the body with horripilation and heaviness. He sees everything including living beings white in colour and he takes longer time to come out of the bout (of epilepsy) compared to those of Vata and Pitta type. The commentator explains that Susruta says white objects are seen in Kapha type.

sanskrit_text: सर्वलिङ्गं सन्निपातजम् । असाध्यम् । क्षीणस्य चिरोत्पन्नं चासाध्यम् । मुहुः कम्पते । क्षीणः । भ्रूविभ्रमः । विभ्रान्तदृष्टिः ॥६-७॥
transliteration: Sarvaliṅgaṃ sannipātajam | Asādhyam | Kṣīṇasya cirotpannaṃ cāsādhyam | Muhuḥ kampate | Kṣīṇaḥ | Bhrū vibhramaḥ | Vibhrāntadṛṣṭiḥ ||6-7||
commentary: If all the above symptomatology is seen in one patient, it should be understood that he is suffering from Sannipāta (Dosa-triad) type of Apasmāra, which is incurable. It is also incurable to an individual who is emaciated and also when it is chronic. Such Apasmāra is fatal in which the patient repeatedly trembles, is emaciated, has irregular movements of the eye-brows and improper looks (eyes). The commentator explains that these are the signs of incurability.

sanskrit_text: वातात्द्वादशाहात् । पित्तात्पञ्चदशाहात् । कफान्मासात् । विकारादनियमः ॥८-९॥
transliteration: Vātātdvādaśāhāt | Pittātpañcadaśāhāt | Kaphānmāsāt | Vikārādaniyamaḥ ||8-9||
commentary: The aggravated Dosas - Vāta, Pitta and Kapha cause the bout of Apasmāra once in a twelve-day interval, once in fifteen days and once in a month respectively with slight variation. The commentator explains that though the seeds are sown in the rainy season, some of them sprout in the Sarat Ṛtu, so also the manifestation of the disease.

sanskrit_text: रूक्षशीताल्पलघुभोजनैः । अतिव्यवायात् । अतिजागरणात् । अतिद्रवस्वेदनात् । अध्वजलक्रीडात् । व्यायामात् । धातुक्षयात् । चिन्ताशोकात् । व्याधिक्षयात् । वेगरोधात् । आमोत्पत्तेः । अभिघातात् । उपवासात् । मर्माभिघातात् । पतनात् । वातः प्रकुप्यति । स शून्यानि स्रोतांसि गत्वा । नानाविधान् विकारान् करोति ॥१-४॥
transliteration: Rūkṣaśītālp laghubhojanaiḥ | Ativyavāyāt | Atijāgaraṇāt | Atidravasvedanāt | Adhvajalakrīḍāt | Vyāyāmāt | Dhātukṣayāt | Cintāśokāt | Vyādhikṣayāt | Vegarodhāt | Āmotpatter | Abhighātāt | Upavāsāt | Marmābhighātāt | Patanāt | Vātaḥ prakupyati | Sa śūnyāni srotāṃsi gatvā | Nānāvidhān vikārān karoti ||1-4||
commentary: Due to dry-cold-low quantity and light foods, excessive coitus, excessive awakening, excessive out flow of Dosas and blood as a result of improper purificatory techniques, overdoing jumping from high altitudes, swimming, walking, physical exercise etc. activities, depletion of tissues, over thinking, grief, emaciation due to chronic diseases, suppression of natural urges, formation of Āma, getting injured, skipping food, getting trauma on the vital parts and by falling from fast moving vehicles like elephant, camel and horse, the Vāta becomes powerful and enters into the empty channels in the body and causes innumerable diseases. The commentator explains that Vāta is the most powerful of all the Dosas, and the severity of Vāta diseases makes them difficult to manage.

sanskrit_text: अव्यक्तलिङ्गानि पूर्वरूपम् । आपायलाघवम् ॥५॥
transliteration: Avyaktaliṅgāni pūrvarūpam | Āpāyalāghavam ||5||
commentary: The Pūrvarūpa (prodromata) of Vātavyādhi are those which are existing in the incomplete manifestation of the disease. When the complete manifestation takes place, there is also instability of symptomatology and lightness in the affected part of the body. The commentator explains that Apāya means the absence of the symptomatology like rigidity, contraction, trembling etc. due to instability of Vata.

sanskrit_text: आकुञ्चनप्रकोचनौ । अस्थिभेदः । सन्धिविश्लेषः । रोमहर्षः । असंबद्धप्रलापः । ग्रहः । पङ्गुत्वम् । जानुस्तम्भः । कुब्जता । शोफः । अनिद्रा । गर्भस्रावः । शुक्रस्रावः । रजःस्रावः । स्पन्दनम् । सुप्तता । ग्रहः । शिरसो ग्रहः । नासाग्रहः । ग्रीवाग्रहः । भेदः । तोदः । रुक् । पातः । श्रमः । इत्यादि ॥६-९॥
transliteration: Ākuñcanaprakochanau | Asthibhedaḥ | Sandhiviśleṣaḥ | Romaharṣaḥ | Asambaddhapralāpaḥ | Grahaḥ | Paṅgutvam | Jānustambhaḥ | Kubjatā | Śophaḥ | Anidrā | Garbhasrāvaḥ | Śukrasrāvaḥ | Rajaḥsrāvaḥ | Spandanam | Suptatā | Grahaḥ | Śiraso grahaḥ | Nāsāgrahaḥ | Grīvāgrahaḥ | Bhedaḥ | Todaḥ | Ruk | Pātaḥ | Śramaḥ | Ityādi ||6-9||
commentary: Contraction and rigidity in the joints, brittleness of bones and dislocation of joints, horripilation, irrelevant speech, gripping sensation in the hands, back and head, lameness, rigidity in the legs, dwarfism, swelling of the body, sleeplessness, instability or loss of pregnancy, semen and menstrual flow, pulsation or tickling sensation, numbness of the body, gripping and displacement of head, nose and neck, breaking sensation, pinning sensation, pain, falling down, fatigue and such other signs and symptoms are caused by aggravated Vāta. As per the causative factor and the location, the disease-manifestation takes place. The commentator explains that swelling is mainly manifested on hands, face etc., and sleeplessness indicates less sleep.

sanskrit_text: कोष्ठे मूत्रपुरीषविबन्धः । वृद्धिः । हृद्रोगः । गुल्मः । अर्शांसि । पार्श्वरुक् । सर्वगते सर्वाङ्गकम्पनम् । आघातः । सन्धिशब्दः । सर्वाङ्गवेदना ॥१०-११॥
transliteration: Koṣṭhe mūtrapurīṣavibandhaḥ | Vṛddhiḥ | Hṛdrogaḥ | Gulmaḥ | Arśāṃsi | Pārśvaruk | Sarvagate sarvāṅgakampanam | Āghātaḥ | Sandhiśabdaḥ | Sarvāṅgavedanā ||10-11||
commentary: When (the aggravated) Vāta lodges in the Koṣṭha (alimentary canal), there will be retention of urine and faeces, Vṛddhi (hernia), heart-disease, tumor in the abdomen, piles and pain in the flanks. When Vāta occupies the whole body on aggravation, it causes shaking of limbs, beating pain and the joints crack with full of pain. The commentator explains that the word Koṣṭha includes all the parts of the alimentary canal along with Āmāsaya.

sanskrit_text: गुदे मूत्रपुरीषवातविबन्धः । शूलमाध्मानम् । अश्मरी । शर्करा । जङ्घोरुत्रिकपृष्ठरुक् । आमाशये पार्श्वहृत्कुक्षिरुक् । तृट् । उद्गारः । कुक्षितोदः । कासः । मुखकण्ठशोषः । श्वासः ॥१२-१३॥
transliteration: Gude mūtrapurīṣavātavibandhaḥ | Śūlamādh mānam | Aśmarī | Śarkarā | Jaṅghorutrikapṛṣṭharuk | Āmāśaye pārśvahṛtkukṣiruk | Tṛṭ | Udgāraḥ | Kukṣitodaḥ | Kāsaḥ | Mukhakaṇṭhaśoṣaḥ | Śvāsaḥ ||12-13||
commentary: When vitiated Vāta settles in the anus, it causes retention of faeces, urine and fart, causes pain, flatulance, calculi, Śarkarā (sandy formation in the urine) and pain and wasting in the calf muscle, thighs, sacrum, legs and back. When Vāta occupies the stomach, there will be pain in the flanks, abdomen, heart and navel; thirst, belchings, pinning sensation in the abdomen, cough, dryness in the mouth and throat and dyspnoea. The commentator explains that Guda includes the upper part of the anus i.e., intestines etc.

topic_heading: Vāta in Intestines and Sensory Organs
sanskrit_text: पक्वाशये कुजनम् । शूलमाध्मानम् । मूत्रपुरीषविबन्धः । कटीरुक् । इन्द्रियेषु तद्विनाशः ॥१४॥
transliteration: Pakvāśaye kujanam | Śūlamādh mānam | Mūtrapurīṣavibandhaḥ | Kaṭīruk | Indriyeṣu tadvināśaḥ ||14||
commentary: When the vitiated Vāta gets seated in the Pakvāśaya (intestines), it causes sounds in the abdomen, pain and flatulance, difficulty in micturition, defaecation, bloating of the abdomen and pain in the sacrum. When it lodges in the sensory organs, it destroys the particular organ. The commentator explains that this stanza is from Susruta Samhitā and compiles the complete picture.

sanskrit_text: त्वक्स्थे रौक्ष्यम् । स्फुटनम् । सुप्तता । कार्श्यम् । कृष्णता । तोदः । अतन्यता । रागः । सन्धिरुक् ॥१५॥
transliteration: Tvaksthe raukṣyam | Sphuṭanam | Suptatā | Kārśyam | Kṛṣṇatā | Todaḥ | Atanyatā | Rāgaḥ | Sandhiruk ||15||
commentary: Vāta when aggravated and seated in the skin, causes dryness and fissuring in the skin and the skin becomes numb, emaciated, black, has sense of pins and needles, it stretches and gets reddened. There will also be pain in the joints. The commentator explains that 'Atanyate' means stretches due to lack of elasticity.

sanskrit_text: असृक्स्थे तीव्ररुक् । दाहः । वैवर्ण्यम् । कार्श्यम् । अरुचिः । अरुंसि । भुक्ते स्तम्भः ॥१६॥
transliteration: Asṛksthe tīvraruk | Dāhaḥ | Vaivarṇyam | Kārśyam | Aruciḥ | Aruṃsi | Bhukte stambhaḥ ||16||
commentary: When Vāta gets lodged in the Asṛk (blood), there will be severe pain and burning sensation, discolouration, emaciation, distaste and there arise innumerable small boils on the body and rigidity of the body on eating. The commentator explains that 'Arumsi' means wounds, and rigidity on eating occurs due to increase of blood by eating.

topic_heading: Vāta in Mamsa, Medas, Majja and Asthi
sanskrit_text: मांसस्थे गात्रगौरवम् । तीव्रतोदः । दण्डाहत इव । मुष्टिघात इव । रुक् । ग्लानिः । मेदःस्थे गात्रगौरवम् । तीव्रतोदः । दण्डाहत इव । मुष्टिघात इव । रुक् । ग्लानिः । मज्जस्थे सन्धिशब्दः । सन्धिरुक् । मांसबलक्षयः । अनिद्रा । सततरुक् ॥१७-१८॥
transliteration: Māṃsasthe gātragauravam | Tīvratodaḥ | Daṇḍāhata iva | Muṣṭighāta iva | Ruk | Glāniḥ | Medaḥsthe gātragauravam | Tīvratodaḥ | Daṇḍāhata iva | Muṣṭighāta iva | Ruk | Glāniḥ | Majjasthe sandhiśabdaḥ | Sandhiruk | Māṃsabalakṣayaḥ | Anidrā | Satataruk ||17-18||
commentary: Heaviness in the limbs, severe pricking sensation as if beaten with rods and fists, pain and excessive fatigue are the symptoms when vitiated Vāta is seated in Māṃsa (muscle) and Meda (fat). Breaking and creaking sounds in the bone-joints, pain in the joints, emaciation of musculature and strength, sleeplessness and continuous pain are seen when Vāta reaches Majjā (Marrow) and Asthi (bone). The commentator explains that due to proximity in the tissues, the symptomatology is similar when Vāta occupies either of these two.

topic_heading: Vāta in Śukra, Sira and Snayu
sanskrit_text: शुक्रस्थे शुक्रधारणम् । गर्भस्य च्यवनम् । सिरास्थे तोदः । तनुता । स्थूलता । स्नायुस्थे बाह्यायामः । अन्तरायामः । खल्ली । कुब्जता । एकाङ्गरोगः ॥१९-२०॥
transliteration: Śukrasthe śukradhāraṇam | Garbhasya cyavanam | Sirāsthe todaḥ | Tanutā | Sthūlatā | Snāyusthe bāhyāyāmaḥ | Antarāyāmaḥ | Khallī | Kubjatā | Ekāṅgarogaḥ ||19-20||
commentary: Semen in the men and the resultant foetus in the women are held and slipped without much difference of time and there is also deterioration in these two when the aggravated Vāta is seated in the semen. Aggravated Vāta seated in the Sira (vein) causes pain, thinning and bulging in the veins. Vāta seated in the Snāyu (ligaments) causes Bāhyāyama (opisthotonos), Antarāyama (emprosthotonos), Khallī (muscular spasm of head and feet), Kubjatva (dwarfism) and diseases affecting all the body or one particular part. The commentator explains that Akuncana means constriction and Pūraṇa filling up, by which the veins become bulged.

sanskrit_text: सन्धिषु सन्धिविश्लेषः । शब्दः । रुक् ॥२१॥
transliteration: Sandhiṣu sandhiviśleṣaḥ | Śabdaḥ | Ruk ||21||
commentary: Vāta seated in the joints destroys them and causes pain and sounds. The commentator explains that either it may create dislocation of the joints or rigidity in the joints.

sanskrit_text: प्राणे पित्तावृते छर्दिदाहौ । कफावृते ग्लानितन्द्रारुचयः । उदाने पित्तावृते दाहमूर्च्छाभ्रमग्लानयः । कफावृते स्वेदविबन्धः । रोमहर्षः । मन्दाग्निता । शीताङ्गता । समाने पित्तावृते स्वेददाहोष्ममूर्च्छाः । कफावृते मूत्रपुरीषविबन्धः । रोमहर्षः । अपाने पित्तावृते दाहोष्ममूत्ररक्तम् । कफावृते गुरुत्वम् । शीताङ्गता । व्याने पित्तावृते दाहाक्षेपग्लानयः । कफावृते स्तम्भः । दण्डकः । रुक् । शोफः ॥२२-२६॥
transliteration: Prāṇe pittāvṛte chardidāhau | Kaphāvṛte glānitandrārucayaḥ | Udāne pittāvṛte dāhamūrcchābhramaglānayaḥ | Kaphāvṛte svedavibandhaḥ | Romaharṣaḥ | Mandāgnitā | Śītāṅgatā | Samāne pittāvṛte svedadāhoṣmamūrcchāḥ | Kaphāvṛte mūtrapurīṣavibandhaḥ | Romaharṣaḥ | Apāne pittāvṛte dāhoṣmamūtrarak tam | Kaphāvṛte gurutvam | Śītāṅgatā | Vyāne pittāvṛte dāhākṣepaglānayaḥ | Kaphāvṛte stambhaḥ | Daṇḍakaḥ | Ruk | Śophaḥ ||22-26||
commentary: When Pitta covers Prāṇavāyu, there is vomiting and burning sensation. Kapha covering causes lack of energy, depression, drowsiness and distaste. When Pitta covers Udānavāta: burning sensation, syncope, giddiness and tiredness. Kapha covering: hinderance in sweating, horripilation, mild appetite and cold touch. When Samānavāyu is covered by Pitta: sweating, burning sensation, heat and syncope. Kapha covering: constipation of faeces and urine and horripilation. When Pitta covers Apānavāyu: burning sensation, heat and blood in the urine. Kapha covering: heaviness in the lower part of the body and cold touch. When Pitta covers Vyānavāyu: burning sensation, convulsions and tiredness. Kapha covering: rigidity, Daṇḍaka (plenosthotonos), pain and swelling. The commentator explains that Daṇḍaka is becoming straight like a stick.

sanskrit_text: सर्वा धमनीः प्रपद्य वातः क्षिपति । सोऽक्षेपकः । हृदयं शिरश्च गत्वा । धनुर्वन्नमयति । कम्पयति । मूर्च्छयति । दुःखश्वासः । विस्तारिताक्षः । मीलिताक्षः वा । कपोत इव कूजति । संज्ञानाशः । अपतन्त्रकः । हृदि ग्रहः । अपतानकः ॥२७-३१॥
transliteration: Sarvā dhamanīḥ prapadya vātaḥ kṣipati | So'kṣepakaḥ | Hṛdayaṃ śiraśca gatvā | Dhanurvannamayati | Kampayati | Mūrcchayati | Duḥkhaśvāsaḥ | Vistāritākṣaḥ | Mīlitākṣaḥ vā | Kapota iva kūjati | Saṃjñānāśaḥ | Apatantrakaḥ | Hṛdi grahaḥ | Apatānakaḥ ||27-31||
commentary: When the aggravated Vāta takes over all the arteries, it shakes the body immediately and repeatedly causing convulsions. This is called Aksepaka. Vāyu, on getting aggravated, moves out of its place and reaches heart and head causing severe pain and bends the body like a bow, shaking and making it swoon. The individual breathes with difficulty with straight looks or closed eyes. He makes sounds like a pigeon and loses his senses. This condition is called Apatantraka. When Vāyu grips the heart, the individual has rigid looks, loses his senses and makes sounds in the throat. When it loosens the grip, he becomes free and when it grips again, he would go into syncope again. This severe disease is called Apatānaka. The commentator explains that the different forms of convulsions are being explained.

sanskrit_text: कफान्वितो दण्डवत्पातयति । दण्डपातनकः । धनुर्वत्स्तम्भः । धनुस्तम्भः ॥३२-३३॥
transliteration: Kaphānvito daṇḍavatpātayati | Daṇḍapātanakaḥ | Dhanurvatstambhaḥ | Dhanustambhaḥ ||32-33||
commentary: If Vāta settles in the arteries suddenly along with Kapha, it makes the body rigid like a stick or a log which is called Daṇḍapātanaka (plenosthotonos). When the body of the individual bends like a bow, such condition is called Dhanustambha (tetanus). The commentator explains that by saying Kaphanvita, it implies that it can also cause disease by being along with Pitta.

sanskrit_text: स्नायुप्रतानेषु वायुः । अभ्यन्तरायामः । बहिरायामः । अभ्यन्तरायामे हनुस्तम्भः । पार्श्वरुक् । कफवमनम् । बहिरायामे कण्ठकटीजंघाभङ्गः । असाध्यः ॥३४-३६॥
transliteration: Snāyupratāneṣu vāyuḥ | Abhyantarāyāmaḥ | Bahirāyāmaḥ | Abhyantarāyāme hanustambhaḥ | Pārśvaruk | Kaphavamanam | Bahirāyāme kaṇṭhakaṭījaṅghābhaṅgaḥ | Asādhyaḥ ||34-36||
commentary: When Vāyu takes shelter in the ligaments, it causes Abhyantarāyama (bending forward) and Bahirāyāma (bending backward). In Abhyantarāyama, there is lockjaw, severe pain in the flanks and vomiting of phlegm. In Bahirāyāma, the throat, low-back and thighs get fractured and is incurable according to the learned. The commentator explains that Vaksa is the chest, and Snāyu (ligament) here includes veins and muscles.

sanskrit_text: वातः कफान्वितः पित्तान्वितो वा । अभिघातजश्च । अपतानको गर्भपातशोणितातिस्रावाभिघाताभ्यामसाध्यः ॥३७-३८॥
transliteration: Vātaḥ kaphānvitaḥ pittānvito vā | Abhighātajaśca | Apatānako garbhapātaśoṇitāt isrāvābhighātābhyāmasādhyaḥ ||37-38||
commentary: Vāyu, along with Kapha and/or Pitta or Vāyu alone can cause Aksepaka (convulsions). The fourth variety of this disease is caused by Vāyu aggravated due to Abhighāta (injury). Apatānaka (tetanus) caused due to abortion, loss of blood and due to injury, will not be cured. The commentator explains that the convulsions caused by Garbhapāta and Śoṇitātisrava are to be categorised as of Vāta alone.

sanskrit_text: अर्धकायं वायुर्गृह्णाति । सिरास्नायुशोषणात् । पक्षाघातः । एकाङ्गरोगश्च । सर्वशरीरे च ॥३९-४१॥
transliteration: Ardhakāyaṃ vāyurgṛhṇāti | Sirāsnāyuśoṣaṇāt | Pakṣāghātaḥ | Ekāṅgarogaśca | Sarvaśarīre ca ||39-41||
commentary: Vāyu grips half part of the body and dries up the veins and ligaments of that half and destroys either left or right side, loosening the firmness of the joints. That particular half of the body becomes troublesome and inactive with loss of sense. Some call it Ekāṅgaroga while others style it as Pakṣāghāta (haemiplegia). The same pathogenesis takes place when Vāta occupies the complete body (which should be called as Sarvāṅgāghāta). The commentator explains that Ardha means half of the body, Paksa means the side including shoulder, armpit, flank etc.

sanskrit_text: पित्तान्विते दाहोष्ममूर्च्छाः । कफान्विते शीतशोफगौरवम् । केवलं वातेन दुःसाध्यम् । अन्येन साध्यम् । क्षयहेतुकमसाध्यम् ॥४२-४३॥
transliteration: Pittānvite dāhoṣmamūrcchāḥ | Kaphānvite śītaśophagauravam | Kevalaṃ vātena duḥsādhyam | Anyena sādhyam | Kṣayahetukamasādhyam ||42-43||
commentary: If there is association of Pitta with Vāta in causing this disease, burning sensation, warmth and syncope are seen, while cold touch, swelling and heaviness exist when there is Kapha association. The Pakṣāghāta caused by Vāta alone is most difficult for cure; it is curable if associated with others (Kapha or Pitta) while it is incurable if caused due to emaciation/consumption. The commentator explains that 'Kevala' means alone, 'Anyena' means with others - Kapha or Pitta, and 'Kṣayahetuka' means caused by Vata alone that is aggravated due to emaciation of tissues.

sanskrit_text: अतिजल्पनात् । कठिनाशनात् । अतिहास्यात् । जृम्भणात् । भारात् । विषमशयनात् । वायुः शिरोनासिकानेत्रोष्ठचिबुकगण्डान् गृह्णाति । अर्धमुखविकारः । ग्रीवाभङ्गः । शिरःकम्पः । वाग्रोधः । नेत्रविकारः । ग्रीवाचिबुकदन्तरुक् । रोमहर्षः । कम्पः । नेत्राविलत्वम् । उद्गारः । त्वक्सुप्तता । तोदः । ग्रीवास्तम्भः । हनुस्तम्भः । अर्दितम् ॥४४-४६॥
transliteration: Atijalpanāt | Kaṭhināśanāt | Atihāsyāt | Jṛmbhaṇāt | Bhārāt | Viṣamaśayanāt | Vāyuḥ śironāsikānetroṣṭhacibukagaṇḍān gṛhṇāti | Ardhamukhavikāraḥ | Grīvābhaṅgaḥ | Śiraḥ kampaḥ | Vāgrodhaḥ | Netravikāraḥ | Grīvācibukadantaruk | Romaharṣaḥ | Kampaḥ | Netrāvilatvam | Udgāraḥ | Tvaksuptatā | Todaḥ | Grīvāstambhaḥ | Hanustambhaḥ | Arditaṃ ||44-46||
commentary: Vāyu on entering the conjoining places of head, nose, eyes, lips, chin, forehead and eyes of those who overdo speaking loudly, eating hard foods, laughing, yawning, carrying weights and lying in irregular form, troubles the face and thereby causes Ardita (Bell's palsy). In this condition, half of the face becomes irregular, the neck bends, the head trembles and there will be hinderance of speech, deformity in the eyes etc., pain of neck, chin and teeth of the affected side. Horrippilation, trembling, turbidity of the eyes, belching, numbness and pinning sensation in the skin, cervical rigidity (immobility) and lockjaw. This disease is called Ardita. The commentator explains that 'Ardayati' means troubles.

sanskrit_text: क्षीणस्य । अक्षिनिमीलनासामर्थ्यम् । अव्यक्तभाषित्वम् । चिरोत्पन्नं त्रिवर्षम् । असाध्यम् ॥४७॥
transliteration: Kṣīṇasya | Akṣinimīlanāsāmarth yam | Avyaktabhāṣitvam | Cirotpannaṃ trivarṣam | Asādhyam ||47||
commentary: If the patient of Ardita is emaciated, not able to close the eye-lid of the affected part, utters words with difficulty and if the disease is deep rooted and crossed a duration of three years after onset, he can not be relieved of his ailment. The commentator explains that Animīṣākṣa means not able to close the eye, and Prasaktabhāṣiṇa means having hindered speech.

sanskrit_text: वेगान्ते स्वास्थ्यम् ॥४८॥
transliteration: Vegānte svāsthyam ||48||
commentary: On completion of bout, there will be relief of the symptoms in convulsions etc. The commentator explains that Svasthya means decrease in the pain as the pleasure that is felt by an individual on taking off the weight he has been carrying.

sanskrit_text: जिह्वानिर्लेखनात् । रूक्षाशनात् । अभिघातात् । वायुर्हनुमूलं गत्वा । हनुं श्रंसयति । मुखमुन्नामयति । यद्वा नामयति । हनुग्रहः । भोजनवाक्यासामर्थ्यम् ॥४९-५०॥
transliteration: Jihvānirlekhanāt | Rūkṣāśanāt | Abhighātāt | Vāyurhanumūlaṃ gatvā | Hanuṃ śraṃsayati | Mukhamunnāmayati | Yadvā nāmayati | Hanugrahaḥ | Bhojanavākyāsāmarth yam ||49-50||
commentary: Due to cleaning the tongue, eating dry foods and due to injury, the Vāta which exists in the root of jaw gets aggravated and pushes it down and makes the mouth wide open or closes completely. This is called Hanugraha (lock jaw) because of which there is difficulty in eating and speaking. The commentator explains that either opened mouth or closed mouth are caused due to fickleness of Vāyu.

sanskrit_text: दिवास्वप्नात् । विषमासनात् । ऊर्ध्वदृष्टेः । विकृतास्यात् । वायुः कफान्वितः । मन्यास्तम्भम् ॥५१॥
transliteration: Divāsvapnāt | Viṣamāsanāt | Ūrdhvadṛṣṭeḥ | Vikṛtāsyāt | Vāyuḥ kaphānvitaḥ | Manyāstambham ||51||
commentary: Due to day-sleep, sitting in uneven places and looking upwards with mouth wide-open, the same Vāyu covered by Śleṣma causes Manyāstambha (wry neck). The commentator explains that this is the symptom of torticollis.

sanskrit_text: वायुः स्वरवाहिनीं सिरां गत्वा । जिह्वां स्तम्भयति । अन्नपानवाक्यासामर्थ्यम् ॥५२॥
transliteration: Vāyuḥ svaravāhinīṃ sirāṃ gatvā | Jihvāṃ stambhayati | Annapānavākyāsāmarth yam ||52||
commentary: Vāta that exists in the speech conducting vein (nerves), hinders the movements of the tongue (on aggravation) due to which there will be inability in eating, drinking and speech. The commentator explains that this is glossal palsy.

sanskrit_text: वायुः शिरःसिराः प्रपद्य । शुष्काः सरुजः कृष्णाः करोति । सिराग्रहः असाध्यः ॥५३॥
transliteration: Vāyuḥ śiraḥsirāḥ prapadya | Śuṣkāḥ sarujaḥ kṛṣṇāḥ karoti | Sirāgrahaḥ Asādhyaḥ ||53||
commentary: Vāyu gets lodged in the blood and makes the veins of the neck dry, painful and black. This condition is called Sirāgraha which is incurable. The commentator explains that 'Mūrdhadharā' means those in the neck, and some read 'Sirāgraha' as 'Sirograha' in view of the acting of the head.

sanskrit_text: वाताद्गृध्रसिः । स्तम्भरुक्तोदाः । कटीप्रभृत्यधोगच्छन्ति । स्पन्दनम् । कफान्विते तन्द्रागौरवारुचयः ॥५४-५६॥
transliteration: Vātādgṛdhrasiḥ | Stambharuktodāḥ | Kaṭīprabhṛtyadhogacchanti | Spandanam | Kaphānvite tandrāgauravārucayaḥ ||54-56||
commentary: In Gṛdhrasī caused by Vāta there will be rigidity, pain and pinning sensation which affect, first, the buttocks and then descend to low-back, knees, calves and legs, gradually. There will be repeated pulsation in these limbs. When this is caused by Vāta-Kapha, there will also be drowsiness, heaviness and anorexia (along with the above symptomatology). The commentator explains that in Vata type of Gṛdhrasī, there will be pinning sensation, deformity, pulsation in the knee, loin and thigh-joints along with rigidity.

sanskrit_text: विश्वाची स्कन्धादङ्गुलीगतस्नायुः । हस्तकर्मणामसामर्थ्यम् ॥५७॥
transliteration: Viśvācī skandhādaṅgulīgatasnāyuḥ | Hastakarmaṇāmasāmarth yam ||57||
commentary: The tendons which extend from the back of the shoulder to the upper part of the fingers of the hand are affected and the activity of the hands is diminished. This condition is called Viśvācī. The commentator explains that Gayadāsa says Khallī is also called Viśvācī and Gṛdhrasī.

sanskrit_text: जानुसन्धौ वातशोणितात् । क्रोष्टुकशीर्षम् । सशोफं सरुजम् ॥५८॥
transliteration: Jānusandhau vātaśoṇitāt | Kroṣṭukaśīrṣam | Saśophaṃ sarujam ||58||
commentary: The inflammation caused by Vāta and Śoṇita (blood) in the knee joint which is very painful is known as Kroṣṭukaśīrṣa. The knee joint becomes big (swollen) and looks like the head of a jackal. The commentator explains that Gayadāsa says this is caused by Vatarakta but given separately for treatment differs.

sanskrit_text: वायुः सक्थिस्नायून् क्षिपति । खञ्जः । सक्थ्नोः विनाशात् पङ्गुः । कलायखञ्जः सन्धिमुक्तः ॥५९-६०॥
transliteration: Vāyuḥ sakthisnāyūn kṣipati | Khañjaḥ | Sakthnoḥ vināśāt paṅguḥ | Kalāyakhañjaḥ sandhimuktaḥ ||59-60||
commentary: When Vāta that exists in the loin disturbs the tendons of the thigh, then Khañja occurs to the individual and makes him limp. Due to destruction of both the thighs, Paṅgu (paraplegia) occurs. When the individual trembles on starting to walk and limps while walking, he is considered to be suffering from Kalāyakhañja in which the joints will be loosened (ruined). The commentator explains that Sakthi is the upper part of the calf muscle, and Kṣipet means disturbs to some extent.

sanskrit_text: विषमपादप्रसारणात् । गुल्फसन्धौ वातः । वातकण्टकः ॥६१॥
transliteration: Viṣamapādaprasāraṇāt | Gulphasandhau vātaḥ | Vātakaṇṭakaḥ ||61||
commentary: When the legs are kept in an irregular poise or due to strain, Vāta gets aggravated in the ankle joints causing pain there. This condition is called Vātakaṇṭaka. The commentator explains that this disease is called Khudukavata elsewhere.

sanskrit_text: अतिपादचारात् । वातः पित्तरक्ताभ्याम् । पाददाहः ॥६२॥
transliteration: Atipādacārāt | Vātaḥ pittaraktābhyām | Pādadāhaḥ ||62||
commentary: Vāta along with Pitta and Rakta causes burning sensation in the (soles of the) feet due to over-walking which is called Pādadāha (burning feet). The commentator explains that this condition is different from Vatarakta because of absence of discolouration etc.

sanskrit_text: पादयो रोमहर्षः सुप्तता । पादहर्षः कफवातात् ॥६३॥
transliteration: Pādayo romaharṣaḥ suptatā | Pādaharṣaḥ kaphavātāt ||63||
commentary: Whoever has horripilation in the feet and also numbness, such condition is to be known as Pādaharṣa which is caused by Kapha and Vāta. The commentator explains that Harsa means the horripilation due to inner cold, and this feeling is comparable to Jhaṭiti.

sanskrit_text: अंसबन्धनं वायुः शोषयति । अंसशोषः ॥६४॥
transliteration: Aṃsabandhanaṃ vāyuḥ śoṣayati | Aṃsaśoṣaḥ ||64||
commentary: The Vāta existing in the scapular region dries up the binding of scapular joint (on aggravation). The commentator explains that this is caused by Vāta alone, and Amsabandhana means the factor that binds the scapula.

sanskrit_text: अंसदेशसिरासङ्कोचात् । अवबाहुकः ॥६५॥
transliteration: Aṃsadeśasirāsaṅkocāt | Avabāhukaḥ ||65||
commentary: By constricting the veins in the scapular region, (aggravated Vāta) causes Avabāhuka. The commentator explains that this is caused by Vāta-Kapha, and some say that Aṃsaśoṣa is a part of Avabāhuka.

sanskrit_text: वायुः कफेन स्वरवाहिनीः सिराः प्रपद्य । मूकम् मिन्मिनम् गद्गदम् करोति ॥६५॥
transliteration: Vāyuḥ kaphena svaravāhinīḥ sirāḥ prapadya | Mūkam minminam gadgadam karoti ||65||
commentary: The Vāta, along with Kapha occupies/covers the speech-conducting arteries (nerves) and causes Mūka (aphonia), Minmina (rhinophonia) and Gadgada (disarthria) which are the speech hindering phenomena. The commentator explains that Mūka means not able to speak at all, Minmina means nasal voice, and Gadgada is speaking without uttering the consonants.

sanskrit_text: पायुमेढ्रवेदना । ऊर्ध्वगा प्रतितूनी ॥६६-६७॥
transliteration: Pāyumeḍhravedanā | Ūrdhvagā pratitūnī ||66-67||
commentary: The pain originating in the colon and urinary bladder and radiates downwards as if piercing the anus and genitals, famous by name Tūnī. The pain originating in the anus and genitalia and radiates upwards to the intestines is called Pratitūnī. The commentator explains that the piercing nature of the pain exists in both.

sanskrit_text: आध्मानम् । प्रत्याध्मानम् आमाशयात् ॥६८-६९॥
transliteration: Ādh mānam | Pratyādh mānam āmāśayāt ||68-69||
commentary: Due to obstruction, Vāta inflates the abdomen and causes sounds and severe pain which is called Ādhmana and is very acute. Pratyādhmana is caused due to Vāta covered by Kapha, which originates in the Āmāśaya (stomach) leaving the flanks and heart. The commentator explains that Atopa is fickle movement in the abdomen, and Udara is Pakvāśaya.

sanskrit_text: नाभ्यधः श्वयथुः । अश्मसदृशः । अष्ठीला । तिर्यक् प्रत्यष्ठीला ॥७०-७२॥
transliteration: Nābhyadhaḥ śvayathuḥ | Aśmasadṛśaḥ | Aṣṭhīlā | Tiryak pratyaṣṭhīlā ||70-72||
commentary: The tumour that originates below the navel, which is mobile or static, looks like Aṣṭhīlā (a stony mass) which spreads up in the edges and wide in shape. This is to be known as Vātaṣṭhīlā which hinders urine and faeces. If this originates in a transverse position in the stomach, it is to be called as Pratyasthīlā which also hinders the fart, faeces and urine. The commentator explains that Aṣṭhīlā is a round stone, and there is also hinderance of fart in Pratyasthīlā.

sanskrit_text: अनुगुणे वाते मूत्रप्रवृत्तिः । प्रतिलोमे मूत्राघातः ॥७३॥
transliteration: Anuguṇe vāte mūtrapravṛttiḥ | Pratilome mūtrāghātaḥ ||73||
commentary: If Vāta is in its positive movement in the Basti (bladder), the process of urination takes place properly. When it becomes reverse (upward), there will be various disorders (of urinary tract). The commentator explains that this verse indicates the possibility of urinary obstruction even without Aṣṭhīlā.

sanskrit_text: सर्वाङ्गशिरःकम्पः । वेपथुः । खल्ली पादजङ्घोरुस्कन्धेषु ॥७४॥
transliteration: Sarvāṅgaśiraḥ kampaḥ | Vepathuḥ | Khallī pādajaṅghoruskandheṣu ||74||
commentary: The trembling of the whole body or the head is called Vepathu. Cramps in the feet, calves, thighs and shoulders is called Khallī. The commentator explains that shaking of the whole body or part of it is to be known as Vepathu.

sanskrit_text: अधोवातनिरोधात् । ऊर्ध्वगमनम् । ऊर्ध्ववातः ॥७५॥
transliteration: Adhovātanirodhāt | Ūrdhvagamanam | Ūrdhvavātaḥ ||75||
commentary: Vāyu, when hindered in the lower part either by Śleṣma or Vāta (of local origin), causes excessive belchings which is called Ūrdhvavāta. The commentator explains that this is over-belching.

sanskrit_text: देशतो नामतश्च लिङ्गतः । पित्तादिसंयोगतः । ज्ञेयाः ॥७६॥
transliteration: Deśato nāmataśca liṅgataḥ | Pittādisaṃyogataḥ | Jñeyāḥ ||76||
commentary: One should know the other Vāta disorders basing on the place of origination and nomenclature of the symptomatology. One should also estimate the association of Pitta etc. (Pitta, Kapha, Āma etc.). The commentator explains that basing on the place of origination - as in the case of Kuksisūla (pain in the abdomen); and name of the symptom - as in the case of Sūla (pain as if a nail is sent in).

sanskrit_text: हनुस्तम्भः अर्दितः पक्षाघातः अपतानकः । कृच्छ्रसाध्याः । चिरात्साध्याः । न वा सिध्यन्ति । बलिनो निरुपद्रवाः ॥७७॥
transliteration: Hanustambhaḥ arditaḥ pakṣāghātaḥ apatānakaḥ | Kṛcchrasādhyāḥ | Cirātsādhyāḥ | Na vā sidhyanti | Balino nirupadravāḥ ||77||
commentary: Hanustambha (lock-jaw), Ardita (facial paralysis), Pakṣāghāta (haemiplegia) and Apatānaka types of Vāta disorders are curable with great effort and after longer duration of treatment. They may not be cured also. The patient should be energetic and should not have any complications for positive result in the treatment. The commentator explains that as such Vātavyādhi is incurable, physicians do not give any guarantee, as it is cured only by divine power.

sanskrit_text: पक्षाघातादयः क्षीणस्य विसर्पदाहरुक्सङ्गमूर्च्छारुच्यग्निमार्दवैः । शोफसुप्तताभग्नकम्पातिरुग्भिः । न जीवति ॥७८-७९॥
transliteration: Pakṣāghātādayaḥ kṣīṇasya visarpadāharuk saṅgamūrcchārucyagnimārdavaiḥ | Śophasuptatābha gnakampātirugbhiḥ | Na jīvati ||78-79||
commentary: Vāta disorders i.e. Pakṣāghāta (haemiplegia etc.) will kill the individual if he is emaciated and or afflicted by Visarpa (erysipalus), Dāha (burning sensation), Ruk (pain), Saṅga (constipation), Mūrcchā (syncope), Aruci (anorexia) and Agnimārdava (low digestive fire). Apart from this, if the patient of Vāta has oedema, numbness of the skin, broken limbs, trembling and severe pain, he will not survive. The commentator explains that these are the complications leading to death.

sanskrit_text: अव्याहतगतिः स्थानस्थः प्रकृतिस्थः । शतायुर्वीतरोगः ॥८०॥
transliteration: Avyāhatagatiḥ sthānasthaḥ prakṛtisthaḥ | Śatāyurvītarogaḥ ||80||
commentary: In whose body, Vāta movement is not obstructed, it is in its place and in its original nature, such a person lives over hundred years without any disease. The commentator explains that 'Avyāhatagati' means uninterupted pathway; 'Sthānastha' means in its original place; and 'Prakṛtistha' means neither with low intensity nor high intensity.

sanskrit_text: लवणाम्लकटूष्णक्षारस्निग्धविदाहिभोजनात् । अजीर्णात् । आममांसशुष्कमांसात् । तिलपिष्टात् । मूलकात् । कुलत्थात् । माषात् । कलायात् । शाकात् । मांसात् । इक्षुरसात् । दध्नः । सुराशुक्तारनालादिभ्यः । विरुद्धाशनात् । अतिभोजनात् । क्रोधात् । दिवास्वप्नात् । रात्रिजागरणात् । सुकुमाराणाम् । विषमाचाराणाम् । स्थूलानाम् । सुखशीलिनाम् ॥१-३॥
transliteration: Lavaṇāmlakaṭūṣṇakṣārasnigdhavidāhibhojanāt | Ajīrṇāt | Āmamāṃsaśuṣkamāṃsāt | Tilapiṣṭāt | Mūlakāt | Kulatthāt | Māṣāt | Kalāyāt | Śākāt | Māṃsāt | Ikṣurasāt | Dadhnaḥ | Surāśuktāranālādibhyaḥ | Viruddhāśanāt | Atibhojanāt | Krodhāt | Divāsvapnāt | Rātrijāgaraṇāt | Sukumārāṇām | Viṣamācārāṇām | Sthūlānām | Sukhaśīlinām ||1-3||
commentary: Due to consumption of salt, sour and pungent tasted foods, alkalis, oily and very hot foods and eating without complete digestion of previous food, consuming wet and very dry meat of amphibians, sesame paste, radish, horse-gram, black-gram, peas, greens, meat, preparations of sugarcane juice, curds, sour liquids like over fermented alcoholic preparations, buttermilk etc., incompatible foods; over eating; getting angry, day-sleep and waking during nights and generally to the delicate ones and to those who have irregular dietetic and behavioural habits and also in the obese and those who lead pleasurable life, Vatarakta gets aggravated. The commentator explains that the delicate ones get Rakta aggravated due to less activity and eating more salt, and Vāta provokes by consuming pungent and bitter foods and waking during nights.

sanskrit_text: हस्त्यश्वोष्ट्रारोहणात् । विदाहिभोजनात् । रक्तं प्रकुप्यति । पादयोः सञ्चितम् । वातेन सह । वातरक्तम् ॥४॥
transliteration: Hastyaśvoṣṭrārohaṇāt | Vidāhibhojanāt | Raktaṃ prakupyati | Pādayoḥ sañcitam | Vātena saha | Vātaraktam ||4||
commentary: Riding the elephant, horse and camel and consuming over burnt foods causes over burning (vitiation) of complete blood in the body and such vitiated blood gets accumulated in the legs. When that blood is colluded with the aggravated Vāta, such condition due to domination of Vāta, is called Vātarakta. The commentator explains that riding on elephant etc. causes aggravation of Vāta and it also facilitates the liquid (blood) to get accumulated in the lower extremities.

sanskrit_text: अतिस्वेदोऽस्वेदः । श्यावता । स्पर्शाग्रहः । क्षतेऽतिरुक् । सन्धिशैथिल्यम् । सादः । ग्लानिः । कोठाः । तोदः । स्पन्दनम् । भेदः । गौरवम् । सुप्तता । कण्डूः । जानुजङ्घोरुकटीश्रोण्यंसबाहुपादसन्धिषु । सन्धिरुक् । अनियतवृद्धिक्षयः । वैवर्ण्यम् । मण्डलानि ॥५-७॥
transliteration: Atisvedo'svedaḥ | Śyāvatā | Sparśāgrahaḥ | Kṣate'tiruk | Sandhiśaithilyam | Sādaḥ | Glāniḥ | Koṭhāḥ | Todaḥ | Spandanam | Bhedaḥ | Gauravam | Suptatā | Kaṇḍūḥ | Jānujaṅghorukaṭīśroṇyaṃsabāhupādasandhiṣu | Sandhiruk | Aniyatavṛddhikṣayaḥ | Vaivarṇyam | Maṇḍalāni ||5-7||
commentary: Excessive or no perspiration, blackish discolouration, loss of sense of touch, severe pain on injury, lack of firmness in the joints, lassitude, depression, appearance of blisters on the skin, pinning sensation, pulsation, breaking sensation, heaviness, numbness and itching sensation in the knees, calf muscle, thighs, pelvis, scapular region, hands, legs and joints. The pain in joints persists and disappears untimely. There will also be discolouration and patches on the body as prodromata of Vatarakta. The commentator explains that excessive or no perspiration results due to the special effect of the disease.

sanskrit_text: वातोल्बणे रुक्स्पन्दनभेदशोफरूक्षश्यावत्वानि । रक्तोल्बणे शोफतोदताम्रता दाहः । पित्तोल्बणे स्वेदमूर्च्छामदतृट्स्पर्शासहत्वानि । कफोल्बणे स्निग्धगुरुसुप्तशीतकण्ड्वः । द्विदोषे द्विलिङ्गम् । त्रिदोषे सर्वम् ॥८-१२॥
transliteration: Vātolbaṇe rukspandanabhedaśopharūkṣaśyāvatvāni | Raktolbaṇe śophatodatāmratā dāhaḥ | Pittolbaṇe svedamūrcchāmadatṛṭsparśāsahatvāni | Kapholbaṇe snigdha gurusuptaśītakaṇḍvaḥ | Dvidoṣe dviliṅgam | Tridoṣe sarvam ||8-12||
commentary: When Vāta is dominant: pain, pulsation, breaking pain, oedema, dryness, blackish discolouration, bluishness, raise and pacification of symptoms, constriction of arteries and fingers, gripping sensation and severe pain in the body, hatred towards cold things, increase on exposure to cold, rigidity, trembling and numbness. When Rakta is dominant: oedema, severe pain, pinning sensation, coppery discolouration, specific burning sensation, increase by oily or dry applications, itching and exudation. When Pitta is dominant: delusion, perspiration, syncope, intoxication, thirst, not being able to withstand touch, pain, reddishness, oedema, ulceration and high temperature. When Kapha is predominant: wetness, heaviness, numbness, oiliness, cold feeling and mild itching. When two Dosas are predominant, respective symptomatology is present. When three Dosas are predominant, all the above signs and symptoms are featured. The commentator explains that when Rakta is dominant, it means the Rakta other than the disease-initiating factor.

sanskrit_text: पादमूले समुत्पन्नम् । कदाचित्करे । शरीरे विसर्पति ॥१३॥
transliteration: Pādamūle samutpannam | Kadācitkare | Śarīre visarpati ||13||
commentary: Taking origination in the roots of legs, sometimes in the hands, Vatarakta spreads to the body on aggravation like the rat poison (poison caused by rat-bite). The commentator explains that Caraka classified this disease into two: Uttāna (rooted in the skin and muscle tissue) and Gambhīra (originated from the deeper strata).

sanskrit_text: त्वक्स्फुटनं जानुपर्यन्तम् । छिन्नत्वक् । स्रावः । मांसबलक्षयोपद्रवैर्युक्तम् । असाध्यम् । संवत्सरोत्थं याप्यम् । अनिद्रारोचकश्वासमांसविदाहशिरोग्रहमूर्च्छामदरुक्पिपासाज्वरमोहकम्पहिक्कापङ्गुत्वविसर्पपाकतोदभ्रमग्लान्यङ्गुल्याकुञ्चनस्फुटनदाहमर्मविद्रधिभिः । युक्तं वर्जयेत् । निरुपद्रवं साध्यम् । एकदोषं साध्यम् । द्विदोषं याप्यम् । त्रिदोषमुपद्रवैर्युक्तमसाध्यम् ॥१४-१८॥
transliteration: Tvak sphuṭanaṃ jānuparyantam | Chinnatvak | Srāvaḥ | Māṃsabalakṣayopadravairyuktam | Asādhyam | Saṃvatsarotthaṃ yāpyam | Anidrārocakaśvāsamāṃsavidāhaśirograhamūrcchāmadarukpipāsājvaramohakampahikkāpaṅgutvavisarpapākatodabhramaglānyaṅgulyākuñcanasphuṭanadāhamarmavidradhibhiḥ | Yuktaṃ varjayet | Nirupadravaṃ sādhyam | Ekadoṣaṃ sādhyam | Dvidoṣaṃ yāpyam | Tridoṣamupadravairyuktamasādhyam ||14-18||
commentary: Vatarakta in which the skin is cracked up to the knee, skin is cut off, exudation and associated with complications like emaciation of energy and muscle tissue, is incurable. That which completed one year of duration is Yāpya (can be prolonged). The complications are: lack of sleep, anorexia, dyspnoea, necrosis of muscle tissue, gripping in the head, syncope, intoxication, pain, thirst, fever, delusion, trembling, hiccup, lameness, erysipalus, ulceration, pricking sensation, giddiness, tiredness, bending of fingers, cracking, burning sensation and abscess in the vital parts. A case with these complications is to be avoided for treatment. The new one and single Dosa dominated is curable. Two Dosa dominated is prolongable. Tridosa associated with complications is incurable. The commentator explains that after one year's duration is prolongable only if skin erosion etc. are not there.

chapter_title: Ūrustambhanidāna (Diagnosis of Rigidity of the Thighs)
sanskrit_text: शीतोष्णद्रवस्थूलगुरुविष्टम्भिभोजनैः । अजीर्णादर्धस्विन्नात् । व्यायामात् । क्रोधात् । दिवास्वप्नात् । रात्रिजागरणात् । वातः कफमेदोभ्यामामेन च । विपरीतदोषं गृहीत्वा । सक्थ्यस्थीनी श्लेष्मणा पूरयति । स्तब्धत्वम् । शीतस्पर्शत्वम् । परसक्थिसंज्ञा । गौरवरुक् । सादः । अङ्गमर्दः । शीतस्पर्शः । तन्द्रा । छर्दिः । अरुचिः । ज्वरः । चेष्टारोधः । उद्धरणासामर्थ्यम् । पादसुप्तता । उरुस्तम्भः । अध्यवातश्च ॥१-५॥
transliteration: Śītoṣṇadravasthūlaguruviṣṭambhibhojanaiḥ | Ajīrṇādardhasvinnāt | Vyāyāmāt | Krodhāt | Divāsvapnāt | Rātrijāgaraṇāt | Vātaḥ kaphamedobhyāmāmena ca | Viparītadoṣaṃ gṛhītvā | Sakthyasthīnī śleṣmaṇā pūrayati | Stabdhatvam | Śītasparśatvam | Parasakthisaṃjñā | Gauravaruk | Sādaḥ | Aṅgamardaḥ | Śītasparśaḥ | Tandrā | Chardiḥ | Aruciḥ | Jvaraḥ | Ceṣṭārodhaḥ | Uddharaṇāsāmarth yam | Pādasuptatā | Urustambhaḥ | Adhyavātaśca ||1-5||
commentary: By consuming cold, warm, liquid, hard, heavy and strong foods, eating on incomplete digestion of previous food or eating half cooked foods, due to strenuous exercise, irritation, day-sleep and waking in the nights, Vāta along with Śleṣma and Medas and Āma which are abundantly increased influences the other Dosa (Pitta), covers it and gets into the bones of Sakthi with the fluidity of Śleṣma and makes both the thighs rigid. By this there arise rigidity, cold touch and immobility in the thighs. The patient feels that his thigh belongs to somebody else and there will also be heaviness and pain. There is depression, myalgia, cold-touch, drowsiness, vomiting, anorexia and fever along with inactivity and difficulty in raising and numbness of the legs. This is called Ūrustambha (rigidity of the thighs) while some call it Adhyavāta. The commentator explains that mentioning of cold and warm things indicates mutually opposite qualities.

chapter_title: Ūrustambhanidāna (Diagnosis of Rigidity of the Thighs)
topic_heading: Purvarupa, Anupasaya and Prognosis of Urustambha
sanskrit_text: अतिनिद्रा । अतिचिन्ता । शीतस्पर्शः । ज्वरः । रोमहर्षः । अरुचिः । छर्दिः । जङ्घोरुसादः । वातशङ्किभिरज्ञानात् स्नेहने । अधिकस्तम्भः । सुप्तता । उद्धरणासामर्थ्यम् । जङ्घोरुग्लानिः । दाहरुक् । पादातिरुक् । स्पर्शाग्रहः । स्थातुं गन्तुं चेष्टितुं न शक्नोति । भिन्नसक्थिसंज्ञः । दाहरुक्तोदकम्पोपद्रवैर्युक्तो हन्ति । निरुपद्रवो नवः साध्यः ॥६-१०॥
transliteration: Atinidrā | Aticintā | Śītasparśaḥ | Jvaraḥ | Romaharṣaḥ | Aruciḥ | Chardiḥ | Jaṅghorusādaḥ | Vātaśaṅkibhirajñānāt snehane | Adhikastambhaḥ | Suptatā | Uddharaṇāsāmarth yam | Jaṅghoruglāniḥ | Dāharuk | Pādātiruk | Sparśāgrahaḥ | Sthātuṃ gantuṃ ceṣṭituṃ na śaknoti | Bhinnasakthisaṃjñaḥ | Dāharuktodakampopadravairyukto hanti | Nirupadravo navaḥ sādhyaḥ ||6-10||
commentary: The premonitory symptoms are: excessive sleep, over thinking, cold touch, fever, horripilation, anorexia, vomiting and lowered activity in the calf muscles and thighs. When unwise people apply oleation therapy thinking that the disease has Vata aggravation alone, there will be increase in immobility of the legs, numbness, difficulty in raising the legs, severe fatigue in the calf muscles and thighs, repeated feeling of burning sensation and pain, the foot pains too much on stepping down, cannot perceive the cold touch, the individual does not have control on standing, walking and moving the legs. There will be feeling as if the thighs are broken and belong to somebody. When there is association of burning sensation, pain, pricking sensation and trembling, this disease kills the individual and without these complications and if it is newly affected, then only one should treat it. The commentator explains that this disease has no classification based on Dosa.

sanskrit_text: विरुद्धाशनाचारात् । मन्दाग्नेः । अव्यायामस्य । स्निग्धभोजनस्य व्यायामात् । आमं कफस्थानेषु गत्वा । दूषितं धमनीः प्रपद्य । दोषैः कुपितम् । नानावर्णम् । पिच्छिलम् । आर्द्रीकरोति । हृद्गौरवम् । आमं तीव्रम् । नानारोगकरम् । वातामौ युगपत्कुपितौ । त्रिकसन्धिं गत्वा । स्तम्भयतः । स आमवातः ॥१-५॥
transliteration: Viruddhāśanācārāt | Mandāgneḥ | Avyāyāmasya | Snigdhabhojanasya vyāyāmāt | Āmaṃ kaphasthāneṣu gatvā | Dūṣitaṃ dhamanīḥ prapadya | Doṣaiḥ kupitam | Nānāvarṇam | Picchilam | Ārdrīkaroti | Hṛdgauravam | Āmaṃ tīvram | Nānārogakaram | Vātāmau yugapatkupitau | Trikasaṃdhiṃ gatvā | Stambhayataḥ | Sa āmavātaḥ ||1-5||
commentary: For those who consume the incompatible combination of food and adopt mutually opposite behavioural aspects, who have lower digestive fire and do not indulge in any physical activity and for those who eat oily foods and immediately indulge in physical exercise, Āma (the indigested food) is motivated and travels towards the places of Śleṣma. On getting spoilt, that reaches the arteries. Again on getting vitiated by three of the Dosas, it becomes multicoloured and sticky and makes the channels wet and immediately causes weakness and heaviness of the heart. Such Āma is very severe and it hosts various diseases. Vāta and Āma get aggravated simultaneously and get seated in the Trika Sandhi (sacrum). Then these two make the body rigid. This disease is called Āmavāta. The commentator explains that Viruddha means foods having mutually opposite qualities, and Āma is the undigested essence of food caused by weak digestive fire.

sanskrit_text: अङ्गमर्दः । अरुचिः । तृष्णा । आलस्यम् । गौरवम् । ज्वरः । अपाकः । अङ्गशून्यता ॥६॥
transliteration: Aṅgamardaḥ | Aruciḥ | Tṛṣṇā | Ālasyam | Gauravam | Jvaraḥ | Apākaḥ | Aṅgaśūnyatā ||6||
commentary: Pain in the body (myalgia), anorexia, thirst, lassitude, heaviness of the body, fever, indigestion and feeling of hollowness of the limbs are the features of Āmavāta. The commentator explains that these are the general symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis.

sanskrit_text: स प्रवृद्धः सन्धिषु शोफम् । वेदनाम् । करोति । अग्निमान्द्यम् । प्रसेकः । अरुचिः । गौरवम् । अनुत्साहः । आध्मानम् । शूलम् । अनिद्रा । तृट् । छर्दिः । भ्रमः । मूर्च्छा । हृद्ग्रहः । विबन्धः । स्तम्भः । कुजनम् । आध्मानम् ॥७-१०॥
