transliteration: Sa pravṛddhaḥ sandhiṣu śopham | Vedanām | Karoti | Agnimāndyam | Prasekaḥ | Aruciḥ | Gauravam | Anutsāhaḥ | Ādh mānam | Śūlam | Anidrā | Tṛṭ | Chardiḥ | Bhramaḥ | Mūrcchā | Hṛdgrahaḥ | Vibandhaḥ | Stambhaḥ | Kujanam | Ādh mānam ||7-10||
commentary: This Āmavāta becomes severe when it aggravates. It causes painful swelling (inflammation) in the joints of hands, legs, head, ankle, sacrum, knees and thighs where the morbid substance gets seated. That place becomes very painful as if stung by scorpions. The disease causes weakness to the digestive fire, dribbling of saliva, anorexia, heaviness in the body, lack of attitude for work, burning sensation, excessive urination, hardness of the abdomen, colic, lack of sleep, thirst, vomiting, giddiness, syncope, gripping sensation of the heart, constipation, rigidity of the body, sounds in the intestines, flatulance and other difficult complications. The commentator explains that the other complications are like constriction of the body, lameness etc.

topic_heading: Dosa-wise Features and Prognosis of Amavāta
sanskrit_text: पित्तान्विते दाहरागः । वातान्विते रुक् । कफान्विते शीतगुरुकण्डूः । एकदोषं साध्यम् । द्विदोषं याप्यम् । त्रिदोषं कष्टम् । सर्वशोफं च ॥११-१२॥
transliteration: Pittānvite dāharāgaḥ | Vātānvite ruk | Kaphānvite śītagurukaṇḍūḥ | Ekadoṣaṃ sādhyam | Dvidoṣaṃ yāpyam | Tridoṣaṃ kaṣṭam | Sarvaśophaṃ ca ||11-12||
commentary: When this is associated with Pitta, there is burning sensation and reddish discolouration; pain persists if Vāta is predominant; and cold touch, heaviness and pruritus are seen when Kapha is dominant. Āmavāta when associated with one single Dosa is curable. It is prolongable if two of the Dosas are dominantly present and it is difficult for cure if three of the Dosas are associated and when it is featured by oedema of the whole body. The commentator explains that these are the prognostic criteria.

sanskrit_text: शूलं अष्टविधम् । वातात् पित्तात् कफात् सन्निपातात् आमात् द्वन्द्वजं च । सर्वत्र वातः प्रधानम् ॥१॥
transliteration: Śūlaṃ aṣṭavidham | Vātāt pittāt kaphāt sannipātāt āmāt dvandvajaṃ ca | Sarvatra vātaḥ pradhānam ||1||
commentary: Śūla is of eight types: one each from the three Dosas, one from the three Dosas together, one from Āma, and one from each of the two-Dosa combination of the three Dosas. Generally in all these types, Vāta is the dominant factor. The commentator explains that there is a mythological story about the origination of Śūla as in the case of fever, and Vāta is an invariable factor even in the Śūla caused by Kapha and Pitta.

sanskrit_text: अतिव्यायामाध्वमैथुनजागरणशीताम्बुपानाधिकाल्पकलायमुद्गकोरदूषरूक्षभोजनात् । अतिभोजनात् । अभिघातात् । कषायतिक्तभोजनात् । विरुद्धाशनात् । वल्लूरशाकात् । वेगरोधात् । शोकात् । उपवासात् । अतिहास्यजल्पनात् । वातः प्रकुप्यति । हृत्पार्श्वपृष्ठकटीवस्तिशूलम् । पाकान्ते सायं मेघशीतकाले वर्धते । आवृत्त्यनुवर्तते । विष्टम्भः । तोदः । भेदः । स्वेदस्नेहमर्दनस्निग्धोष्णैः शाम्यति ॥२-५॥
transliteration: Ativyāyāmādhvamaithunajāgaraṇaśītāmbupānādhikālpakalāyamudgakoradūṣarūkṣabhojanāt | Atibhojanāt | Abhighātāt | Kaṣāyatiktabhojanāt | Viruddhāśanāt | Vallūraśākāt | Vegarodhāt | Śokāt | Upavāsāt | Atihāsyajalpanāt | Vātaḥ prakupyati | Hṛtpārśvapṛṣṭhakaṭīvastiśūlam | Pākānte sāyaṃ meghaśītakāle vardhate | Āvṛttyanuvartate | Viṣṭambhaḥ | Todaḥ | Bhedaḥ | Svedasnehamardanasnigdhoṣṇaiḥ śāmyati ||2-5||
commentary: Due to excessive indulgence in physical exercise, travel, coitus, waking in the nights, over drinking of cold water, over consumption of lathyrus pulses, red-gram, green-gram, millets, very dry foods, over eating, on getting injured, eating foods of astringent and bitter taste, foods prepared out of seedling grains, incompatible combination of foods, dry meat, dry greens; suppression of natural urges like faeces, semen, urine and fart; grief, fasting and due to over laughing and talking, Vāta increases abundantly and causes Śūla (pain) in the heart, flanks, back, Sacrum and urinary bladder. The pain increases on digestion of food, evenings, cloudy day and in cold season. It repeatedly becomes aggressive and pacifies. There will be constipation of faeces and fart, pinning sensation and tearing pain in this disease. This pacifies by sudation therapy, oleation, massage and foods of oily and warm nature. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Vata type of colic.

sanskrit_text: क्षारतीक्ष्णोष्णविदाहितैलनिष्पावपिण्याककुलत्थयवागूकट्वम्लसौवीरादिभिः । क्रोधातपाग्निव्यायामातपसेवनात् । अतिव्यवायात् । विदग्धाशनात् । पित्तं प्रकुप्यति । नाभिशूलम् । तृण्मूर्च्छादाहस्वेदभ्रमोष्मभिः । मध्याह्नमध्यरात्रपाकमेघकाले वर्धते । शीतकाले शीतोपचारैर्मधुरैः शाम्यति ॥६-८॥
transliteration: Kṣāratīkṣṇoṣṇavidāh itailaniṣpāvapiṇyākakulatthayavāgūkaṭvamlasa uvīrādibhiḥ | Krodhātapāgnivyāyāmāt apasevanāt | Ativyavāyāt | Vidagdhāśanāt | Pittaṃ prakupyati | Nābhiśūlam | Tṛṇmūrcchādāhasvedabhramoṣmabhiḥ | Madhyāhnamadhyarātrapākameghakāle vardhate | Śītakāle śītopacārairmadhuraiḥ śāmyati ||6-8||
commentary: Due to over consumption of alkali foods, fast, warm, foods that cause burning, oil, dicot pulses, paste of mustard etc. after extraction of oil, porridge of horse-gram, bitter and sour foods, Sauvīra etc. fermented drinks; getting angry, exposure to heat or fire, physical strain and Sun, over indulgence in coitus and eating burnt foods, Pitta aggravates readily and causes Śūla in the navel which is associated with thirst, delusion, burning sensation, sweating, syncope, giddiness and warmth of the body. This Śūla aggravates during mid-day, mid-night, the time of digestion and when the sky is cloudy. It pacifies during cold season, on using cooling treatments and cold and sweet foods. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Pitta type of colic.

sanskrit_text: ग्राम्यौदकानूपमांसकिलाटकृशरतिलपिण्याकादिभिः कफप्रकोपणैः । कफः प्रकुप्यति । आमाशयशूलम् । हृल्लासकाससादारुचिप्रसेकशैत्यगौरवशिरोरुक् । भुक्तमात्रे सूर्योदये शिशिरवसन्तकाले वर्धते ॥९-१०॥
transliteration: Grāmyaudakānūpamāṃsakilāṭakṛśaratilapiṇyākādibhiḥ kaphaprakopaṇaiḥ | Kaphaḥ prakupyati | Āmāśayaśūlam | Hṛllāsakāsasādāruciprasekaśaityagauravaśiroruk | Bhuktamātre sūryodaye śiśiravasantakāle vardhate ||9-10||
commentary: By consuming flesh of amphibians and the animals which live in the water, sediment of broken buttermilk, milk products, meat, sugarcane, pasty foods, rice and green-gram etc. cooked together (Khicri), rolls and cakes made out of sesame and other aetiological factors that provoke Kapha, it gets aggravated and causes pain in the Āmāśaya (stomach). This is associated with nausea, cough, depression, anorexia, dribbling of saliva, cold feeling (immobility) in the alimentary canal and heaviness in the head. The pain aggravates immediately after food, during sun-rise, in the winter season and spring season. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Kapha type of colic.

topic_heading: Tridosa, Ama and Dual Dosa Sula
sanskrit_text: सन्निपाते सर्वलिङ्गम् । आमे विष्टम्भहृल्लासच्छर्दिगौरवसादाध्मानप्रसेकाः । द्वन्द्वजे द्विलिङ्गम् । वस्तिहृत्पार्श्वपृष्ठेषु कफवातजम् । नाभिहृन्मध्ये कफपित्तजम् । दाहज्वरयुक्तं वातपित्तजम् ॥११-१३॥
transliteration: Sannipāte sarvaliṅgam | Āme viṣṭambhahṛllāsacchardigaurava sādādh mānaprasekāḥ | Dvandvaje dviliṅgam | Vastihṛtpārśvapṛṣṭheṣu kaphavātajam | Nābhihṛnmadhye kaphapittajam | Dāhajvarayuktaṃ vātapittajam ||11-13||
commentary: In the Śūla caused by all three Dosas, all the above symptomatology is seen which is fairly difficult for cure. Śūla associated with noises in the intestines, nausea, vomiting, heaviness, immobility, flatulance and dribbling of phlegm is caused by Āma. Dual Dosa types have combined symptoms. Kapha-Vāta type occurs in the bladder, heart, flanks and back. Kapha-Pitta type affects the abdomen, in between the heart and navel. Vāta-Pitta type is associated with burning sensation and fever and is very severe. The commentator explains that the place of Sula of Vata-Pitta predominance is given in Carakasaṃhitā.

sanskrit_text: एकदोषं साध्यम् । द्विदोषं कृच्छ्रम् । त्रिदोषमुपद्रवैर्युक्तमसाध्यम् ॥१४॥
transliteration: Ekadoṣaṃ sādhyam | Dvidoṣaṃ kṛcchram | Tridoṣamupadravairyuktam asādhyam ||14||
commentary: Śūla caused by a single Dosa is curable and that caused by two-Dosa combination is difficult for cure. Where there is involvement of all three of the Dosas, is severe and associated with complications; such Śūla is incurable. The commentator explains that the complications of Sula are pain, thirst, syncope, bloating, heaviness, anorexia, cough, dyspnoea and hiccup.

sanskrit_text: पित्तं कफमुपश्लिष्य वातेन सह । पाकसमये तीव्रशूलम् । परिणामशूलम् ॥१५-१६॥
transliteration: Pittaṃ kaphamupaśliṣya vātena saha | Pākasamaye tīvraśūlam | Pariṇāmaśūlam ||15-16||
commentary: Vāta, aggravated by its own aetiological factors, encircles the Kapha and Pitta and causes severe pain during the time of digestion of food which is called Parīṇāmaśūla (pain caused during digestion of food). This is the comprehensive symptom of this disease. The commentator explains that though there is involvement of three of the Dosas, one should consider the average of Pitta Dosa in this disease.

sanskrit_text: वातिके आध्मानकुजनविबन्धचलत्वकम्पाः । स्निग्धोष्णैः शाम्यति । पैत्तिके तृड्दाहचलत्वस्वेदाः । कट्वम्ललवणैर्वर्धते । शीतैः शाम्यति । कफजे छर्दिहृल्लासमोहाल्पसततरुक् । कटुतिक्तैः शाम्यति । द्विदोषे द्विलिङ्गम् । त्रिदोषमसाध्यम् ॥१७-२०॥
transliteration: Vātike ādh mānakujanavibandhacalatvakampāḥ | Snigdhoṣṇaiḥ śāmyati | Paittike tṛḍdāhacalatvasvedāḥ | Kaṭvamlalavaṇairvardhate | Śītaiḥ śāmyati | Kaphaje chardihṛllāsamohālpasatataruk | Kaṭutiktaiḥ śāmyati | Dvidoṣe dviliṅgam | Tridoṣam asādhyam ||17-20||
commentary: In Vāta-predominant Parīṇāmaśūla: flatulance, sounds in the intestines, constipation of faeces and urine, restlessness and trembling; pacifies by oily and warm foods. In Pitta-predominant: thirst, burning sensation, restlessness, sweating; aggravates by pungent, sour and salty foods; pacifies by cold foods. In Kapha-predominant: vomiting, nausea, delusion, mild and continuous pain; recedes by consuming pungent and bitter foods and drinks. Dual Dosa types have combined symptoms. Tridosa type is incurable. The commentator explains that these are the dosa-based classifications of peptic ulcer.

sanskrit_text: पाकान्ते पाकमध्ये अजीर्णे वा शूलम् । न भोजनेन नोपवासेन शाम्यति । सोऽन्नद्रवशूलः ॥२१-२२॥
transliteration: Pākānte pākamadhye ajīrṇe vā śūlam | Na bhojanena nopavāsena śāmyati | So'n nadravaśūlaḥ ||21-22||
commentary: The colic which occurs after digestion, during digestion or on indigestion and which does not pacify either by wholesome or unwholesome food and by eating or fasting, is named as Annadravāśūla. The commentator explains that in Annadravāśūla, it does not give relief as long as the vomiting of Jaratpitta does not take place.

sanskrit_text: वातवर्चोमूत्रक्षवथुबाष्पस्नेहोद्गारच्छर्दिशुक्रक्षुत्तृट्श्वासनिद्राणां वेगरोधात् । उदावर्तः ॥१॥
transliteration: Vātavarchomūtrakṣavathubāṣpasnehodgāracchard iśukrakṣuttṛṭśvāsanidrāṇāṃ vegarodhāt | Udāvartaḥ ||1||
commentary: Udāvarta (bloating of the abdomen) occurs on suppression of fart, faeces, urine, yawn, tears, sneeze, belching, vomiting, flow of semen, hunger, thirst, dyspnoea and sleep. The commentator explains that the natural urges, numbering thirteen, here are not to be suppressed. In all types of Udāvarta, Vāyu is the causative factor.

sanskrit_text: वातरोधे आध्मानम् । पुरीषरोधे कुजनम् । मूत्ररोधे वस्तिमेढ्ररुक् । क्षवथुरोधे ग्रीवास्तम्भः । बाष्परोधे शिरोगौरवम् । उद्गाररोधे हृद्ग्रहः । छर्दिरोधे कण्डूः । शुक्ररोधे मेढ्रशोफः । क्षुधारोधे गात्रसादः । तृड्रोधे कण्ठशोषः । श्वासरोधे हृद्रोगः । निद्रारोधे जृम्भा ॥२-१२॥
transliteration: Vātārodhe ādh mānam | Purīṣarodhe kujanam | Mūtrarodhe vastimeḍhruk | Kṣavathurodhe grīvāstambhaḥ | Bāṣparodhe śirogauravam | Udgārarodhe hṛdgrahaḥ | Chardirodhe kaṇḍūḥ | Śukrarodhe meḍhraśophaḥ | Kṣudhārodhe gātrasādaḥ | Tṛḍrodhe kaṇṭhaśoṣaḥ | Śvāsarodhe hṛdrogaḥ | Nidrārodhe jṛmbhā ||2-12||
commentary: Obstruction of fart, urine and faeces, flatulance, fatigue, pain in the stomach and other Vata-diseases occur due to suppression of fart. Painful sounds in the abdomen, cutting pain, constipation, belching or the faeces coming from mouth take place when the man suppresses the urge of passing faeces. Pain in the bladder and penis, dysurea, head-ache, bending of the body and bulge in the groins are the features caused by suppression of the urge of passing urine. Rigidity of the neck and throat, severe Vata type of disorders of head, eye, nose, mouth and ear occur due to suppression of yawning. Heaviness of the head, eye-diseases of severe nature and corryza occur when tears are suppressed. Rigidity of the neck, head-ache, bell's palsy, migraine and weakness of the sense-organs take place when sneezing is stopped forcibly. Fullness of throat and mouth, pinning sensation, sounds in the throat or inability in respiration and severe Vata-disorders occur when belching is hindered. Pruritus, rashes, anorexia, blemishes on face, oedema, anaemia, palour, fever, skin diseases, erysipalus and nausea are resulted due to suppression of vomiting. Pain and swelling in the bladder, anus and testes, hinderance in urination, calculus, dribbling of semen and related disorders are caused by hindering Śukra. Drowsiness, pain all over the body, anorexia, fatigue and weakness of sight take place by suppression of hunger. Dryness of throat and mouth, inability in hearing and pain in the heart are caused by suppression of thirst. Heart-disease and delusion or oppression of Vāta occur when fast respiration is suppressed. Yawning, pain all over the body, heaviness in the eyes and head and also drowsiness are resulted due to suppression of sleep. The commentator explains that these are the signs and symptoms caused by suppression of various natural urges.

sanskrit_text: रूक्षकषायकटुतिक्तभोजनैः । वातः प्रकुप्यति । वातमूत्रपुरीषरक्तकफमेदोवहानि स्रोतांसि उदावर्तयति । पुरीषं च वर्धयति । हृद्वस्तिरुक् । हृल्लासः । अस्वस्थता । दुःखेन वातमूत्रपुरीषप्रवृत्तिः । श्वासकासपीनसदाहमोहतृट्छर्दिहिक्काशिरोरुक् । मनःश्रुतिविभ्रमाः । वातविकाराश्च ॥१३-१६॥
transliteration: Rūkṣakaṣāyakaṭutiktabhojanaiḥ | Vātaḥ prakupyati | Vātamūtrapurīṣaraktakaphamedovahāni srotāṃsi udāvartayati | Purīṣaṃ ca vardhayati | Hṛdvastiruk | Hṛllāsaḥ | Asth ātā | Duḥkhena vātamūtrapurīṣapravṛttiḥ | Śvāsakāsapīnasadāhamohatṛṭchardihikkāśiroruk | Manaḥśrutivibhramāḥ | Vātavikārāśca ||13-16||
commentary: Vāta that exists in the Koṣṭha (alimentary canal) aggravates by consuming foods of dry nature and astringent, pungent and bitter in taste, causes Udāvarta immediately. It bloats the channels carrying Vāta, Mūtra, Purīṣa, blood, Kapha and fat. The faeces also increases in quantity. Then the individual suffers from pain in the heart and bladder, nausea and restlessness. He passes the fart, urine and faeces with great difficulty. He also gets afflicted by dyspnoea, cough, corryza, burning sensation, delusion, thirst, fever, vomiting, hiccup, diseases of the head, disturbance of mind and hearing and many other diseases that occur due to Vāta-aggravation. The commentator explains that this is the Udāvarta caused by Vata aggravation.

sanskrit_text: विबद्धमामं वा पुरीषं वा । अनाहः । आमे तृट्शिरोदाहौ । आमाशये शूलगौरवहृद्ग्रहोद्गाररोधाः । पक्वाशये आलसकलिङ्गम् ॥१७-१९॥
transliteration: Vibaddhamāmaṃ vā purīṣaṃ vā | Anāhaḥ | Āme tṛṭśirodāhau | Āmāśaye śūlagauravahṛdgrahodgār arodhāḥ | Pakvāśaye ālasakaliṅgam ||17-19||
commentary: The undigested stuff or faecal matter which is accumulated, gradually and constipated by disturbed Vāta does not pass out properly, which is called Anāha (flatulance). If it is caused by Āma, thirst, corryza, burning sensation in the head are seen. Pain and heaviness in the stomach, gripping sensation of the heart, hinderance of belching are present in Anāha originating in the stomach. When Anāha occurs in the Pakvāśaya (intestines) there will be symptomatology similar to that of Ālasaka. The commentator explains that the wise should never take up the Udāvarta patient who has thirst, turbid body, emaciation and suffering from various types of pains.

sanskrit_text: गुल्मः पञ्चविधः । वातात् पित्तात् कफात् सन्निपातात् रक्ताच्च । हृन्नाभ्योरन्तरे ग्रन्थिः ॥१॥
transliteration: Gulmaḥ pañcavidhaḥ | Vātāt pittāt kaphāt sannipātāt raktācca | Hṛnnābhyorantare granthiḥ ||1||
commentary: Gulma (abdominal tumour) is of five types: due to Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, Sannipāta and Rakta (caused by blood). It occurs in between the heart and navel, looks like a knot, and is mobile or static in nature. The commentator explains that Dvandva type is not given separately as in Arśas, and the knot-like formation is called Gulma.

sanskrit_text: ग्रन्थिर्वृत्तः स्थिरश्चलो वा । चयापचयवान् । गुल्मः ॥२॥
transliteration: Granthirvṛttaḥ sthirascalo vā | Cayāpacayavān | Gulmaḥ ||2||
commentary: The knot-like formation occurring in between the heart and navel either mobile or static in nature, circular in shape and increasing and decreasing in size is called as Gulma. The commentator explains that increasing and decreasing in size is seen in Vāta type as Vāta has fluctuating character.

sanskrit_text: वातपित्तकफसन्निपातैः । चतुर्विधः पुंसाम् । रक्तजः स्त्रीणाम् ॥३॥
transliteration: Vātapittakaphasannipātaiḥ | Caturvidhaḥ puṃsām | Raktajaḥ strīṇām ||3||
commentary: Gulma is caused by the three Dosas aggravated individually and also by all three Dosas united (thus making four types) for males; and in females there is another Gulma caused by Rakta and known as Rakta Gulma. The commentator explains that Rakta Gulma occurs in women only, and the blood that causes Gulma here is menstrual blood.

sanskrit_text: अतिउद्गारः । विष्टम्भः । अरुचिः । अक्षमत्वम् । आटोपः । आध्मानम् । अजीर्णम् ॥४॥
transliteration: Atiudgāraḥ | Viṣṭambhaḥ | Aruciḥ | Akṣamatvam | Āṭopaḥ | Ādh mānam | Ajīrṇam ||4||
commentary: Excessive belching, constipation, dislike towards food, not being able to work, sounds in the abdomen, irritation in the abdomen, flatulance and indigestion are the features that indicate occurrence of Gulma in near future. The commentator explains that these are the prodromata of Gulma.

sanskrit_text: अरुचिः । विण्मूत्रवातविबन्धः । कुजनम् । आध्मानम् । अतिउद्गारः ॥५॥
transliteration: Aruciḥ | Viṇmūtravātavibandhaḥ | Kujanam | Ādh mānam | Atiudgāraḥ ||5||
commentary: Anorexia, difficulty in passing faeces, urine and flatus, sounds in the intestines, flatulance and over belching are the features to be seen in all types of Gulma. The commentator explains that these are the general symptoms of Gulma.

sanskrit_text: रूक्षविषमाशनाचारात् । वेगरोधात् । शोकात् । अभिघातात् । अतिसंशोधनात् । अनशनात् । वातगुल्मः । विष्टम्भः । आध्मानम् । मुखकण्ठशोषः । श्यावारुणाङ्गता । शीतज्वरः । हृत्कुक्षिपार्श्वांसशिरोरुक् । पाकान्ते वृद्धिः । अजीर्णे शमः । रूक्षकषायकटुतिक्तैर्वर्धते ॥६-८॥
transliteration: Rūkṣaviṣamāśanācārāt | Vegarodhāt | Śokāt | Abhighātāt | Atisaṃśodhanāt | Anaśanāt | Vātagulmaḥ | Viṣṭambhaḥ | Ādh mānam | Mukhakaṇṭhaśoṣaḥ | Śyāvāruṇāṅgatā | Śītajvaraḥ | Hṛtkukṣipārśvāṃsaśiroruk | Pākānte vṛddhiḥ | Ajīrṇe śamaḥ | Rūkṣakaṣāyakaṭutiktairvardhate ||6-8||
commentary: Dry food, continuous irregular eating habits and improper behaviour, suppression of natural urges, grief, exposure to injury, excessive loss of impurities and lack of food are the reasons of Vāta type of Gulma. This has the place of origin, shape and nature of pain as per the Vāta Dosa and also constipation of faeces and flatus, dryness in the throat and mouth, blackish red colour in the body, cold-fever, pain in the heart, stomach, flanks, scapular region and head, aggravation on digestion of food and palliation on indigestion of food, and it aggravates also on consuming dry, astringent, bitter and pungent foods. The commentator explains that irregular behaviour includes forcible deeds like wrestling with more powerful people.

sanskrit_text: कट्वम्लतीक्ष्णोष्णविदाहिरूक्षभोजनात् । क्रोधात् । मद्यपानात् । अमाभिघातात् । पित्तगुल्मः । ज्वरतृट्पीताङ्गता । पाके तीव्ररुक् । स्वेददाहस्पर्शासहत्वम् ॥९-१०॥
transliteration: Kaṭvamlatīkṣṇoṣṇavidāhirūkṣabhojanāt | Krodhāt | Madyapānāt | Amābhighātāt | Pittagulmaḥ | Jvaratṛṭpītāṅgatā | Pāke tīvraruk | Svedadāhasparśāsahatvam ||9-10||
commentary: The aetiology of Pitta Gulma is consuming pungent, sour, fast, hot, burnt, dry foods, getting angry, over consumption of alcohol and allied drinks; Āma being spoiled due to excessive digestive fire and vitiation of blood. Fever, thirst, redness of face and body, severe pain during digestion of food, sweating, burning sensation and not being able to withstand the touch as on the wound are the features of this disease. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Pitta type of Gulma.

sanskrit_text: शीतगुरुस्निग्धभोजनात् । अव्यायामात् । अतिभोजनात् । दिवास्वप्नात् । कफगुल्मः । शीताङ्गता । शीतज्वरः । अकर्मण्यता । हृल्लासः । कासः । अरुचिः । गौरवम् । मन्दोष्मता । मन्दरुक् । कठिनता । स्थिरता ॥११-१२॥
transliteration: Śītagurusnigdhabhojanāt | Avyāyāmāt | Atibhojanāt | Divāsvapnāt | Kaphagulmaḥ | Śītāṅgatā | Śītajvaraḥ | Akarmaṇyatā | Hṛllāsaḥ | Kāsaḥ | Aruciḥ | Gauravam | Mandoṣmatā | Mandaruk | Kaṭhinatā | Sthiratā ||11-12||
commentary: Consuming cold, heavy and oily foods, having no physical exercise, over-eating and sleeping regularly during day-time are the causative factors of Kapha Gulma. The features of Kapha type of Gulma are: cold touch of the body, cold fever, not willing to work, nausea, cough, anorexia, heaviness, low temperature, mild pain and hardness and marked appearance of the Gulma. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Kapha type of Gulma.

sanskrit_text: द्विदोषलिङ्गं द्वन्द्वजम् ॥१३॥
transliteration: Dvidoṣaliṅgaṃ dvandvajam ||13||
commentary: When aetiology and symptomatology of any two of the three Dosas come together, as per the strength of the particular Dosa-duo, to cause two Dosa-Gulma, such three more varieties are to be considered as separate varieties for planning the preparation of medicine for treatment. The commentator explains that these are the dual Dosa types of Gulma.

sanskrit_text: सन्निपाते तीव्ररुक् । तीव्रदाहः । महान् कठिनः । प्राणहरः । अग्निबलमनोबलहरः । असाध्यः ॥१४॥
transliteration: Sannipāte tīvraruk | Tīvradāhaḥ | Mahān kaṭhinaḥ | Prāṇaharaḥ | Agnibalamanobalaharaḥ | Asādhyaḥ ||14||
commentary: In the Gulma where three Dosas are equally involved in causing the disease, the features are: great pain, severe burning sensation, appearance of the Gulma as big and hard like a stone, fatal in nature and it diminishes the strength of mind, body and digestive fire. And this should be known as incurable. The commentator explains that the above is of irregular origination while the one of regular origination is curable.

sanskrit_text: अहितभोजनात् । वायुः प्रसूतायाः । पतितगर्भायाः । रजस्वलायाः । गर्भाशयगतं रक्तम् । पित्तगुल्मलिङ्गम् । गर्भाकृतिः । स्त्रीणामेव । दशमासोत्थं चिकित्स्यम् ॥१५-१६॥
transliteration: Ahitabhojanāt | Vāyuḥ prasūtāyāḥ | Patitagarbhāyāḥ | Rajasvalāyāḥ | Garbhāśayagataṃ raktam | Pittagulmaliṅgam | Garbhākṛtiḥ | Strīṇāmeva | Daśamāsotthaṃ cikitsyam ||15-16||
commentary: Vāyu aggravates in such a woman who just delivered her fetus, the one who aborts her pregnancy early, or to the one during the menstrual period who indulges in improper diet, takes hold of the uterine blood and causes Gulma. It has pain and burning sensation apart from the appearance of the symptomatology akin to that of Pitta-Gulma. The Gulma which forms like a bolus without any limbs and moves at late intervals and has the features of a fetus is called Rudhira Gulma (Rakta Gulma), which occurs only in women and its treatment should be taken up after 10 months of onset. The commentator explains that Ahitabhojana is related to just delivered, aborted and during menstrual period.

sanskrit_text: शनैर्वृद्धः । महोदरपरिग्रहः । कूर्मवत्स्थितः । कृशः । अरुचिहृल्लासकासच्छर्दिकम्पज्वरतृट्तन्द्रापीनसयुक्तः । ज्वरश्वासच्छर्द्यतिसारहृन्नाभिपादशोथैर्युक्तः । अचिरात्त्यजति ॥१७-२०॥
transliteration: Śanairvṛddhaḥ | Mahodaraparigrahaḥ | Kūrmavatsthitaḥ | Kṛśaḥ | Arucihṛllāsakāsacchardikampajvaratṛṭtandrāpīnasayuktaḥ | Jvaraśvāsacchardyatisārahṛnnābhipādaśothairyuktaḥ | Acirāttyajati ||17-20||
commentary: The Gulma which develops gradually, occupies much space of the abdomen, gets lodged, the veins are prominently seen and elevated like a tortoise and in which the patient becomes emaciated and suffers from anorexia, nausea, cough, vomiting, restlessness, fever, thirst, drowsiness and corryza, such is incurable. If the patient suffering from Gulma develops fever, dyspnoea, vomiting and diarrhoea and oedema in the heart, navel, hands and legs, it becomes incurable. Dyspnoea, severe pain, thirst, dislike towards food, sudden disappearance of the Gulma and debility lead to death of the patient of Gulma. The commentator explains that these are the signs of incurability.

sanskrit_text: अतिस्निग्धोष्णगुरुकषायतिक्तभोजनात् । अतिव्यायामात् । अभिघातात् । अतिभोजनात् । शोकात् । वेगरोधात् । हृद्रोगः पञ्चविधः ॥१॥
transliteration: Atisnigdhoṣṇagurukaṣāyatiktabhojanāt | Ativyāyāmāt | Abhighātāt | Atibhojanāt | Śokāt | Vegarodhāt | Hṛdrogaḥ pañcavidhaḥ ||1||
commentary: Continuous usage of very warm, heavy, astringent and bitter foods, strenuous work, injury, over-eating, mental agony and suppression of natural urges leads to heart-disease which is of five types. The commentator explains that heart is one of the places of Gulma, and Prasaṅga means continuous usage.

sanskrit_text: दोषा हृदयं प्राप्य रसं दूषयन्ति । हृदि बाधाम् कुर्वन्ति । स हृद्रोगः ॥२॥
transliteration: Doṣā hṛdayaṃ prāpya rasaṃ dūṣayanti | Hṛdi bādhām kurvanti | Sa hṛdrogaḥ ||2||
commentary: The aggravated Dosas enter the heart and vitiate the Rasa and in turn, create pain in the heart which is called Hṛdroga (heart-disease). The commentator explains that because Rasa (chyle) is situated in Hṛdaya, the aggravated Dosas vitiate the Rasa on reaching there.

sanskrit_text: वातात् तोदः । भेदः । दारणम् । पीडनम् । छेदनम् ॥३॥
transliteration: Vātāt todaḥ | Bhedaḥ | Dāraṇam | Pīḍanam | Chedanam ||3||
commentary: Pulling pain, pinning sensation, sensation of pressing with a stick, breaking pain or a sensation of cutting with an axe are the features of Vāta type of Hṛdroga. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Vata type of heart disease.

sanskrit_text: पित्तात् तृट् । दाहः । ज्वाला । धूमः । मूर्च्छा । स्वेदः । मुखशोषः ॥४॥
transliteration: Pittāt tṛṭ | Dāhaḥ | Jvālā | Dhūmaḥ | Mūrcchā | Svedaḥ | Mukhaśoṣaḥ ||4||
commentary: Thirst, sensation as if the heart is near the fire, burning sensation, sensation as if flames coming out of heart, irritation in the heart, sensation as if fumes coming out of throat, syncope, sweating and dryness of the mouth are the features of Pitta type of Hṛdroga. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Pitta type of heart disease.

sanskrit_text: कफात् गौरवम् । प्रसेकः । अरुचिः । स्तम्भः । मन्दाग्निता । मधुरास्यता ॥५॥
transliteration: Kaphāt gauravam | Prasekaḥ | Aruciḥ | Stambhaḥ | Mandāgnitā | Madhurāsyatā ||5||
commentary: When the aggravated Kapha occupies the heart, there will be heaviness, dribbling of Kapha from the mouth, anorexia, rigidity, decrease in the digestive fire and feeling of sweet taste in the mouth. The commentator explains that these are the signs of Kapha type of heart disease.

sanskrit_text: सन्निपाते सर्वलिङ्गम् । क्रिमिजे तीव्रतोदकण्डूः । हृल्लासः । ष्ठीवनम् । तोदः । रुक् । छर्दिः । तमःप्रवेशः । अरुचिः । श्यावनेत्रता । शोफः ॥६॥
transliteration: Sannipāte sarvaliṅgam | Krimije tīvratodakaṇḍūḥ | Hṛllāsaḥ | Ṣṭhīvanam | Todaḥ | Ruk | Chardiḥ | Tamaḥpraveśaḥ | Aruciḥ | Śyāvanetratā | Śophaḥ ||6||
commentary: When all the above signs and symptoms are seen, such case is to be known as Tridosa type of Hṛdroga, and in that caused by Krimi (worms), severe pain, pinning sensation with itching sensation are present. Nausea, spitting, pinning sensation, pain, vomiting sensation, feeling of entering into darkness, distaste, black colour around eyes and swelling are the features of Hṛdroga caused by Krimi. The commentator explains that Drḍhabala says that the individual symptomatology of Dosas when seen together is to be considered as Sannipāta.

sanskrit_text: ग्लानिः । सादः । भ्रमः । शोफः । उपद्रवाः ॥७॥
transliteration: Glāniḥ | Sādaḥ | Bhramaḥ | Śophaḥ | Upadravāḥ ||7||
commentary: Fatigue, depression, giddiness and oedema are the complications of heart-diseases. Complications enumerated in Śleṣma type of worm infestation are also seen in Krimi type of Hṛdroga. The commentator explains that these complications make the disease difficult to manage.

sanskrit_text: अतिव्यायामात् । अतिप्रवातात् । रूक्षभोजनात् । मद्यात् । अध्वगमनात् । अश्वाद्यारोहणात् । आनूपमांसात् । अतिभोजनात् । अजीर्णात् । दोषा वस्तिं प्रपद्य । कृच्छ्रेण मूत्रयन्ति ॥१-२॥
transliteration: Ativyāyāmāt | Atipravātāt | Rūkṣabhojanāt | Madyāt | Adhvagamanāt | Aśvādyārohaṇāt | Ānūpamāṃsāt | Atibhojanāt | Ajīrṇāt | Doṣā vastiṃ prapadya | Kṛcchreṇa mūtrayanti ||1-2||
commentary: Eight types of Mutrakṛcchra occurs to the human beings due to strenuous exercise, fast medicines, dry foods, alcohol, continuous brisk walk, travelling on horses etc., eating flesh of animals living in water-abundant places, over eating and indigestion. The Dosas vitiated by their own reasons, individually or unitedly enter the urinary bladder and irritate the urinary tract when the individual urinates with difficulty. The commentator explains that among the 107 Marmas, head, heart and bladder are important, hence bladder-diseases are discussed after heart-diseases.

topic_heading: Dosa-wise Signs and Symptoms of Mutrakṛcchra
sanskrit_text: वातात् वङ्क्षणवस्तिमेढ्ररुक् । अल्पं मुहुर्मुहुः । पित्तात् पीतं सरक्तं सदाहम् । कफात् गुरुत्वम् । शोफः । फेनिलम् । सन्निपाते सर्वम् ॥३-४॥
transliteration: Vātāt vaṅkṣaṇavastimeḍhruk | Alpaṃ muhurmuhuḥ | Pittāt pītaṃ saraktaṃ sadāham | Kaphāt gurutvam | Śophaḥ | Phenilam | Sannipāte sarvam ||3-4||
commentary: In Vāta type of Mutrakṛcchra, there is severe pain in the groins, bladder and penis and the individual passes smaller quantities of urine repeatedly. The urine in Pitta type is in yellow colour, mixed with blood, painful and passed with burning sensation. There is heaviness and swelling in the bladder and penis and the urine is froathy in Kapha type. All these signs and symptoms are present when all three of the Dosas are involved in causing Mutrakṛcchra which is highly difficult to manage. The commentator explains that these are the dosa-wise symptoms of dysuria.

sanskrit_text: शल्यजं वातलिङ्गम् । विड्विघातात् विबन्धः । अश्मरीजं च । शुक्रजं शुक्रयुक्तम् ॥५-८॥
transliteration: Śalyajaṃ vātaliṅgam | Viḍvighātāt vibandhaḥ | Aśmarījaṃ ca | Śukrajaṃ śukrayuktam ||5-8||
commentary: When there is a cut or injury due to foreign body in the urinary tract, there will be severe type of Mutrakṛcchra which has the symptomatology similar to that of Vata type. When faeces is hindered, Vāyu gets disturbed and causes flatulance, Vāta type of pain and obstruction of urine; and due to Aśmarī (urinary calculi) Mutrakṛcchra of Aśmarī type occurs. When Śukra (semen) is vitiated by the Dosas and passes through the urinary tract, the individual urinates with difficulty mixed with semen and having pain in the bladder and penis. The commentator explains that these are the other types of dysuria.

topic_heading: Similarity and Contrast between Aśmarī and Śarkarā
sanskrit_text: अश्मरीशर्करयोः समाननिदानलिङ्गत्वम् । विशेषः शर्करायाः । पित्तेन पक्वा । वातेन शुष्का । कफश्च शुष्कः । सिकताः शर्करा ॥९-१२॥
transliteration: Aśmarīśarkarayoḥ samānanidānaliṅgatvam | Viśeṣaḥ śarkarāyāḥ | Pittena pakvā | Vātena śuṣkā | Kaphaśca śuṣkaḥ | Sikatāḥ śarkarā ||9-12||
commentary: Aśmarī (calculus) and Śarkarā (sandy urination) are of equal origination and features. The speciality of Śarkarā is that when the Aśmarī itself gets affected (boiled) by Pitta, dried up by Vāyu and the binding Kapha becomes dry and non-sticky, it disintegrates into sand particles and passes out through urine and called as Śarkarā. In such situation there will be pain in the heart, trembling of the body, pain in the abdomen, weakness of digestive fire, syncope and severe difficulty in urination. When particles of the calculus come out of the urethra, the pain will be relieved till some other particles obstruct the tract. The commentator explains that the causation and symptomatology of Aśmarī and Śarkarā are being explained here along with the specific features of Śarkarā.

sanskrit_text: मूत्ररोधात् । वातकुण्डलिका अष्ठीला वातबस्तिः मूत्रातीतः मूत्रजठरः मूत्रोत्सङ्गः मूत्रक्षयः मूत्रग्रन्थिः मूत्रशुक्रः उष्णवातः मूत्रसादः विड्विघातः बस्तिकुण्डला इति त्रयोदश ॥१॥
transliteration: Mūtrarodhāt | Vātakuṇḍalikā Aṣṭhīlā Vātabastiḥ Mūtrātītaḥ Mūtrajaṭharaḥ Mūtrotsaṅgaḥ Mūtrakṣayaḥ Mūtragranthiḥ Mūtraśukraḥ Uṣṇavātaḥ Mūtrasādaḥ Viḍvighātaḥ Bastikuṇḍalā iti trayodaśa ||1||
commentary: Generally, due to suppression of Mūtra (urine) etc., Dosas aggravate and cause Vātakuṇḍalikā etc. thirteen types of Mutrāghāta. The commentator explains that in Mutrakṛcchra there will be more difficulty and little obstruction, while it is more obstruction and less difficulty in Mutrāghāta.

sanskrit_text: रूक्षाशनात् । मूत्ररोधात् । वायुर्वस्तिं प्रपद्य । मूत्रं भ्रामयति । वस्तिशूलम् । कृच्छ्रमूत्रता । सा वातकुण्डलिका ॥२-३॥
transliteration: Rūkṣāśanāt | Mūtrarodhāt | Vāyurvastiṃ prapadya | Mūtraṃ bhrāmayati | Vastiśūlam | Kṛcchramūtratā | Sā vātakuṇḍalikā ||2-3||
commentary: By consuming more of dry foods and/or due to suppression of urine, Vāyu which is situated in the bladder aggravates, occupies the urine and circulates inside the bladder. There will be pain in the bladder and also slight difficulty in urination. This disease is called Vātakuṇḍalikā which is severe in nature. The commentator explains that because the Vāta makes circles inside the bladder like a tiny whirlwind, the name Vātakuṇḍalikā has been given.

sanskrit_text: वातो वस्तिम् गुदम् च आनह्यति । अष्ठीलाम् करोति । मूत्रपुरीषरोधः ॥४॥
transliteration: Vāto vastim gudam ca ānahyati | Aṣṭhīlām karoti | Mūtrapurīṣarodhaḥ ||4||
commentary: The aggravated Vāta causes bloating in the bladder and anus and produces a tumour which is big and mobile that causes obstruction of urinary tract and the anus. This creates severe pain. The commentator explains that Aṣṭhīlā is a stone-like formation discussed in Vāta disorders.

sanskrit_text: अज्ञानाद् मूत्रं धारयतः । वातो वस्तिं प्रपद्य । द्वारं रुन्धति । मूत्राघातः । वस्तिकुक्षिरुक् । सा वातबस्तिः ॥५-६॥
transliteration: Ajñānād mūtraṃ dhārayataḥ | Vāto vastiṃ prapadya | Dvāraṃ rundhati | Mūtrāghātaḥ | Vastikukṣiruk | Sā vātabastiḥ ||5-6||
commentary: If an individual suppresses the flow of urine due to ignorance (of its consequences), Vāta gets aggravated inside the bladder and causes hinderance at the opening by which the urine gets obstructed resulting in pain in the bladder and abdomen. This condition is known as Vātabasti which is difficult for cure. The commentator explains that this is retention of urine.

sanskrit_text: चिरधृतं मूत्रं न शीघ्रं प्रवर्तते । मन्दं वा । मूत्रातीतः ॥७॥
transliteration: Ciradhṛtaṃ mūtraṃ na śīghraṃ pravartate | Mandaṃ vā | Mūtrātītaḥ ||7||
commentary: After suppression of urine for a long time when the individual urinates, it does not flow quickly or it flows very slowly. This condition is known as Mūtrātīta (incontinence of urine). The commentator explains that this is the incontinence of urine.

sanskrit_text: मूत्ररोधात् आध्मानम् । अपानवायुः कुप्यति । अधोद्वाररोधः । मूत्रजठरः ॥८-९॥
transliteration: Mūtrarodhāt ādh mānam | Apānavāyuḥ kupyati | Adhodvārarodhaḥ | Mūtrajaṭharaḥ ||8-9||
commentary: Flatulance occurs due to suppression of urine which in turn aggravates the Apānavāyu which is responsible for flow of urine. This causes severe bloating and pain in the lower abdomen resulting in hindering the lower part (opening) of the bladder. This condition is known as Mūtrajathara (distended bladder). The commentator explains that this is the distended bladder.

sanskrit_text: मूत्रं वस्तौ मेढ्रे वा तिष्ठति । बलात् प्रवर्तते । सरक्तं वा । अल्पं सरुजं वा । मूत्रोत्सङ्गः ॥१०-११॥
transliteration: Mūtraṃ vastau meḍhre vā tiṣṭhati | Balāt pravartate | Saraktaṃ vā | Alpaṃ sarujaṃ vā | Mūtrotsaṅgaḥ ||10-11||
commentary: Urine gets stopped in the bladder or penis or tip of the penis and on applying force urine comes either along with blood. It may also come in smaller quantities with or without pain. This condition, caused by disturbed Vāta, is called Mūtrotsaṅga (stricture of urethra). The commentator explains that blood is oozed due to rupture in the bladder by force applied to pass urine.

sanskrit_text: रूक्षक्षीणस्य वस्तिस्थं पित्तं वातश्च । मूत्रक्षयम् कुरुतः ॥१२॥
transliteration: Rūkṣakṣīṇasya vastisthaṃ pittaṃ vātaśca | Mūtrakṣayam kurutaḥ ||12||
commentary: In an individual of dry nature and emaciated body the Pitta and Vāta existing in the bladder cause depletion of urine along with pain and burning sensation which is known as Mūtrakṣaya (anuria). The commentator explains that this is the suppression of urine.

sanskrit_text: वस्तिद्वारे ग्रन्थिः । अश्मरीसमवेदनः । मूत्रग्रन्थिः ॥१३॥
transliteration: Vastidvāre granthiḥ | Aśmarīsamavedanaḥ | Mūtragranthiḥ ||13||
commentary: Inside the opening of the Basti there arises suddenly a circular, solid and small tumour which is equivalent to Aśmarī (calculus) in pain and is known as Mūtragranthi (tumor of the bladder). The commentator explains that 'Granthi' is a ball-like formation, and the difference between Mūtragranthi and Aśmarī is that blood alone is solidified here.

sanskrit_text: मूत्रवेगे मैथुनात् । वातः शुक्रं क्षोभयति । मूत्रेण सह शुक्रं मुञ्चति । मूत्रशुक्रः ॥१४॥
transliteration: Mūtravege maithunāt | Vātaḥ śukraṃ kṣobhayati | Mūtreṇa saha śukraṃ muñcati | Mūtraśukraḥ ||14||
commentary: When an individual participates in sexual intercourse despite having an urge to pass urine, the Vāta in his body aggravates and disturbs the semen. That semen comes out through the penis following urine or followed by urine which will be in the colour of ash-mixed water. This condition is known as Mūtraśukra (spermaturia). The commentator explains that this is the condition where semen is passed along with urine.

sanskrit_text: अतिव्यायामाध्वातपसेवनात् । पित्तं वातेन सह । वस्तिमेढ्रगुददाहः । हारिद्रं सरक्तं वा मूत्रम् । रक्तमेव वा । मुहुर्मुहुः कृच्छ्रेण । उष्णवातः ॥१५-१६॥
transliteration: Ativyāyāmādhvātapasevanāt | Pittaṃ vātena saha | Vastimeḍhragudadāhaḥ | Hāridraṃ saraktaṃ vā mūtram | Raktameva vā | Muhurmuhuḥ kṛcchreṇa | Uṣṇavātaḥ ||15-16||
commentary: Due to excessive physical strain, walking and exposure to Sun, Pitta gets aggravated along with Vāta and causes burning sensation in the bladder, penis and the anus resulting in downward flow of urine in the colour of turmeric or along with blood or there may be blood alone repeatedly with great difficulty. This is called Uṣṇavāta (haematuria). The commentator explains that when urine comes out along with blood the colour will be slightly reddish.

sanskrit_text: पित्तकफौ वातेन पक्वौ । पीतरक्तशुक्लार्द्रशुष्करोचनाशङ्खचूर्णाभम् । सदाहं कृच्छ्रम् । अल्पम् । मूत्रसादः ॥१७-१८॥
transliteration: Pittakaphau vātena pakvau | Pītaraktaśuklārdraśuṣkarocanāśaṅkhacūrṇābham | Sadāhaṃ kṛcchram | Alpam | Mūtrasādaḥ ||17-18||
commentary: If Pitta and Kapha, both, or individually get solidified by Vāta, the patient passes urine in yellowish, red, whitish, semisolid, in the colour of the gall of the cow and powder of the conch shell with burning sensation and difficulty, less in quantity and also in the colour which relates to the morbidity. This condition is called Mūtrasāda (scanty urination). The commentator explains that 'Śuṣka' dry means less in quantity, and urine will be like that of Rocana due to Pitta and Śaṅkhacūrṇa in the case of Kapha.

sanskrit_text: वातेन विड्विघातात् । पुरीषं मूत्रमार्गेण । सगन्धं कृच्छ्रेण । विड्विघातः ॥१९-२०॥
transliteration: Vātena viḍvighātāt | Purīṣaṃ mūtramārgeṇa | Sagandhaṃ kṛcchreṇa | Viḍvighātaḥ ||19-20||
commentary: When the faecal matter of a dry and emaciated individual enters the urinary tract due to oppression by Vāta, then he urinates along with faecal matter with the same smell and with difficulty. This condition is to be called as Viḍvighāta (recto-vesical fistula). The commentator explains that this is the condition where faeces passes through urine.

sanskrit_text: अध्वप्लुतव्यायामाभिघातात् । वस्तिः कुण्डलिता । वस्तिरुक् । स्पन्दनम् । दाहः । बिन्दुशः मूत्रम् । बलात् प्रवृत्तिः । अङ्गस्तम्भः । जङ्घाबन्धः । बस्तिकुण्डला ॥२१-२३॥
transliteration: Adhvaplutavyāyāmābhighātāt | Vastiḥ kuṇḍalitā | Vastiruk | Spandanam | Dāhaḥ | Binduśaḥ mūtram | Balāt pravṛttiḥ | Aṅgastambhaḥ | Jaṅghābandhaḥ | Bastikuṇḍalā ||21-23||
commentary: The bladder gets displaced or goes upward looking like a pregnant's abdomen due to fast-walk, jumping, strenuous exercise, injury or pressure. Then, the individual has pain, pulsation and burning sensation in the bladder. There is normally drop-wise urination but free flow is seen when pressure is applied on the bladder. The patient feels as if his body become rigid and squeezing pain in the calf muscle. This condition is called Bastikuṇḍalā which is severe like struck by weapon and afflicted with poison. Usually the Vāta is more powerful here and the ignorant cannot treat this case. The commentator explains that Susruta enumerates only twelve types of Mutrāghāta bifurcating Mūtrasāda into two varieties.

sanskrit_text: पित्तान्विते दाहरुग्वैवर्ण्यम् । कफान्विते गुरुत्वशोफौ । स्निग्धं घनं शुक्लं मूत्रम् । द्वाररोधे असाध्यम् । अन्यथा साध्यम् ॥२४-२५॥
transliteration: Pittānvite dāharugvaivarṇyam | Kaphānvite gurutvaśophau | Snigdhaṃ ghanaṃ śuklaṃ mūtram | Dvārarodhe asādhyam | Anyathā sādhyam ||24-25||
commentary: When there is association of Pitta, there will be burning sensation, pain and discolouration of urine, and if it is associated by Kapha, there will be heaviness and oedema in the body while the urine will be oily, dense and white in colour. On getting obstructed in the opening of the bladder by Kapha or due to predominance of Pitta, this disease becomes incurable. When the opening is not disturbed, it is curable and if the Basti (bladder) is not deformed, it is curable. The commentator explains that these are the prognostic criteria.

sanskrit_text: कुण्डलिते बस्तौ तृट् । मोहः । श्वासः ॥२६॥
transliteration: Kuṇḍalite bastau tṛṭ | Mohaḥ | Śvāsaḥ ||26||
commentary: When the bladder twists like a whirl, the individual has thirst, delusion and dyspnoea. The commentator explains that these are the features of Kuṇḍalā.

sanskrit_text: अश्मरी चतुर्विधा । वातजा पित्तजा कफजा शुक्रजा च । वातो मूत्रं शोषयति । शुक्रपित्तकफैः सह । गोमयात् पाषाणवत् । सर्वास्वश्मरीषु कफः प्रधानम् ॥१-२॥
transliteration: Aśmarī caturvidhā | Vātajā Pittajā Kaphajā Śukrajā ca | Vāto mūtraṃ śoṣayati | Śukrapittakaphaiḥ saha | Gomayāt pāṣāṇavat | Sarvāsv aśmarīṣu kaphaḥ pradhānam ||1-2||
commentary: Aśmarī is of four types: Vātaja, Pittaja, Kaphaja and Śukraja (caused by semen). Generally all the calculi are of Kapha in origin and are like Yama, the death-God (in terms of the suffering they generate). When Vāta dries up the urine in the bladder which is associated either with Śukra (semen), Pitta or Kapha, it gradually develops into a calculus as the gall gets solidified into stones in the gall bladder of the cow. All the Aśmarīs are not of one Dosa base. The commentator explains that the Kapha origination means all are having the invariable association of Kapha Dosa except Śukra.

sanskrit_text: बस्तिगौरवम् । पार्श्वरुक् । अजाविण्मूत्रगन्धता । कृच्छ्रमूत्रता । ज्वरः । अरुचिः ॥३॥
transliteration: Bastigauravam | Pārśvaruk | Ajāviṇmūtragandhatā | Kṛcchramūtratā | Jvaraḥ | Aruciḥ ||3||
commentary: The following are the premonitary symptoms of calculus: bloating of the bladder, severe pain in the surrounding places (of the bladder), urine has the smell like that of a goat, dysuria, fever and anorexia. The commentator explains that these are the early signs of urinary calculi.

sanskrit_text: नाभिवङ्क्षणवस्त्यूर्ध्वरुक् । मूत्रविच्छेदः । मूत्रप्रवृत्तौ पाषाणनिर्गमात् सुखम् । गोमेदाभं श्वेतं वा मूत्रम् । सरक्तं वा । शूलेन सह ॥४-५॥
transliteration: Nābhivaṅkṣaṇavastyūrdhvaruk | Mūtravicchedaḥ | Mūtrapravṛttau pāṣāṇanirgamāt sukham | Gomedābhaṃ śvetaṃ vā mūtram | Saraktaṃ vā | Śūlena saha ||4-5||
commentary: The common signs and symptoms of urinary calculi are pain in the navel, perineal raphe and in the upper part of the bladder. Divided or hindered flow of urine occurs due to obstruction by the calculus and free flow when it is removed. Urine is white or Gomeda-Hessonite (a precious stone in honey colour)-coloured and at times blood comes along with urine when the calculus injures the bladder associated with pain. The commentator explains that Gomeda is Hessonite, a precious stone in dark honey colour.

sanskrit_text: वातात् नखान् खादति । कम्पते । मेढ्रनाभी पीडयति । क्रोशति । वातवर्चस्कं मुञ्चति । बिन्दुशः कृच्छ्रेण मूत्रयति । श्यावारुणं कण्टकाकारम् ॥६-७॥
transliteration: Vātāt nakhān khādati | Kampate | Meḍhranābhī pīḍayati | Krośati | Vātavarcaskaṃ muñcati | Binduśaḥ kṛcchreṇa mūtrayati | Śyāvāruṇaṃ kaṇṭakākāram ||6-7||
commentary: In Vāta type of Aśmarī, the patient keeps biting his nails and trembles. He holds the urethra/penis and the navel and squeezes them while shouting, passes stool with flatus and urinates drop-wise repeatedly with difficulty. The calculus in this type is blackish red in colour and thorny in shape. The commentator explains that the colour and shape are known only when the calculus comes out.

sanskrit_text: पित्तात् वस्तिदाहः । पाकोष्मा । भल्लातकास्थिवर्णा ॥८॥
transliteration: Pittāt vastidāhaḥ | Pākoṣmā | Bhallātakāsthi varṇā ||8||
commentary: There is burning sensation in the bladder, heat is felt as in the ripening wound and the shape of Aśmarī appears like a seed of marking nut in reddish yellow or black in the Pitta type of Aśmarī. The commentator explains that the colour and shape help in planning the management.

sanskrit_text: कफात् वस्तितोदः । शीतगुरुत्वम् । महती मृद्वी गोमेदाभा श्वेता वा ॥९॥
transliteration: Kaphāt vastitodaḥ | Śītagurutvam | Mahatī mṛdvī gomedābhā śvetā vā ||9||
commentary: In Kapha type of Aśmarī, there is pinning sensation in the bladder with cold touch and heaviness. The Aśmarī is big and smooth in honey colour or white. The commentator explains that these are the features of Kapha type of calculus.

sanskrit_text: बालानां सुखग्रहणम् । अल्पत्वात् ॥१०॥
transliteration: Bālānāṃ sukhagrahaṇam | Alpatvāt ||10||
commentary: These (above mentioned) Dosa based calculi occur mostly in children and are easy for removal in view of thin bladder and body they possess. The commentator explains that 'mostly' implies the occurrence of these in elders also, and Grahaṇa is catching hold of them by fingers.

sanskrit_text: शुक्राश्मरी वयस्कानाम् । शुक्रधारणात् । शुक्रं स्थानात् च्युतम् । वातेन वस्तिमेढ्रान्तरे घनीभूतम् । वस्तिरुक् । कृच्छ्रमूत्रता । वृषणशोफः । नवोत्पन्ना पीडनेन विलीयते ॥११-१३॥
transliteration: Śukrāśmarī vayaskānām | Śukradhāraṇāt | Śukraṃ sthānāt cyutam | Vātena vastimeḍhrāntare ghanībhūtam | Vastiruk | Kṛcchramūtratā | Vṛṣaṇaśophaḥ | Navotpannā pīḍanena vilīyate ||11-13||
commentary: Śukrāśmarī occurs only in adults when they hold the flow of semen. When the semen is released from its place (of origination) but not disseminated, it gets solidified in the urinary tract near the testes by the effect of Vāyu which is called Śukrāśmarī (semen formed into calculus). There will be pain in the bladder, dysuria, inflammation of the scrotum and this dissolves on applying pressure immediately after the onset of this Aśmarī. The commentator explains that this occurs only in adults, and 'in the testes' includes the penis also.

sanskrit_text: अश्मरी शर्करा । वातेन भिन्ना । अधोगतिरूपेण निर्गच्छति । ऊर्ध्वगतौ विबन्धः । शर्करा वातेन भिन्ना सती । दौर्बल्यम् । सादः । कार्श्यम् । कुक्षिशूलम् । अरुचिः । पाण्डुता । मूत्रदाहः । तृट् । हृद्रुक् । छर्दिः ॥१४-१६॥
transliteration: Aśmarī śarkarā | Vātena bhinnā | Adhogatirūpeṇa nirgacchati | Ūrdhvagatau vibandhaḥ | Śarkarā vātena bhinnā satī | Daurbalyam | Sādaḥ | Kārśyam | Kukṣiśūlam | Aruciḥ | Pāṇḍutā | Mūtradāhaḥ | Tṛṭ | Hṛdruk | Chardiḥ ||14-16||
commentary: Aśmarī itself is Śarkarā. It is broken into smaller pieces by Vāta and comes down when Vāta has downward movement and during the upward movement, it is obstructed. If Śarkarā comes down and gets obstructed in the urinary tract, it causes weakness, depression, emaciation, pain in the abdomen, anorexia, anaemia, burning micturition, thirst, pain in the heart and vomiting. The commentator explains that Suśruta also says that the calculus is broken by the force of Vāyu and becomes smaller pieces which is called Śarkarā.

sanskrit_text: नाभिवृषणशोफः । मूत्ररोधः । तीव्ररुक् । शर्करा चेत् । असाध्यम् ॥१७॥
transliteration: Nābhivṛṣaṇaśophaḥ | Mūtrarodhaḥ | Tīvraruk | Śarkarā cet | Asādhyam ||17||
commentary: If the individual develops swelling in the navel and testes, obstruction of urine, severe pain and sandy urination, such Aśmarī is incurable. The commentator explains that these are the signs of incurability.
